name: Scholar Yusuf
role: Teaches alphabet and grammar foundations

greeting.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم يا طالِب العِلْم
greeting.english: Peace be upon you, seeker of knowledge
greeting.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum ya taalib al-ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: آه، أَنتَ مَن أَرسَلَتهُ أَميرَة! السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم
lines.english: Ah, you're the one Amira sent! Peace be upon you.
lines.transliteration: aah, anta man arsalathu amiira! as-salaamu alaykum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الشَّيْخ يوسُف، عالِمُ القَرية. أُعَلِّمُ اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: I am Scholar Yusuf, the village scholar. I teach the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: ana ash-shaykh yuusuf, aalimu al-qarya. u'allimu al-lugha al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَميرَة أَخبَرَتني أَنَّكَ تَعَلَّمتَ 'مَرْحَبا' — مُمتاز! لِنَتَعَلَّم المَزيد
lines.english: Amira told me you learned 'marhaba' — excellent! Let's learn more.
lines.transliteration: amiira akhbaratnii annaka ta'allamta 'marhaba' — mumtaaz! linata'allam al-maziid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمْتاز! لِنَبْدَأ بِالتَّحِيّات — أَهَمّ الكَلِمات
lines.english: Excellent! Let's start with greetings — the most important words.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! linabda' bit-tahiyyaat — ahamm al-kalimaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِمَة الأولى: سَلام — تَحِيَّة المُسلِمين
lines.english: The first word: Salaam — the Muslim greeting (peace).
lines.transliteration: al-kalima al-uulaa: salaam — tahiyyat al-muslimiin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِمَة الثّانِيَة: شُكْراً — نَقولُها لِلشُّكر
lines.english: The second word: Shukran — we say it to give thanks.
lines.transliteration: al-kalima ath-thaaniya: shukran — naquuluhaa lish-shukr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن دَعْنا نَخْتَبِر ما تَعَلَّمْت!
lines.english: Now let's test what you've learned!
lines.transliteration: al-aan da'naa nakhtabir maa ta'allamta!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! أَنتَ مُتَعَلِّمٌ سَريع. عُد إلَيَّ لِتَتَعَلَّم المَزيد مِنَ التَّحِيّات
lines.english: Well done! You're a fast learner. Come back to me to learn more greetings.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! anta muta'allimun sarii'. ud ilayya litata'allam al-maziid min at-tahiyyaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَتَكَلَّم مَع فاطِمَة التّاجِرَة وَخالِد الطّالِب أَيضاً — كُلُّهُم يُعَلِّمونَك!
lines.english: And talk to Merchant Fatima and Student Khalid too — they all teach you!
lines.transliteration: wa takallam ma'a faatima at-taajira wa khaalid at-taalib aydan — kulluhum yu'allimuunak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ مَرَّة أُخرى! لِنَتَعَلَّم المَزيد
lines.english: Welcome back! Let's learn more.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bika marra ukhraa! linata'allam al-maziid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً — كَلِمَة لِلتَرحيب
lines.english: Ahlan — a word of welcome.
lines.transliteration: ahlan — kalima lit-tarhiib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَفْوًا — تَعني 'لا شُكْر عَلى واجِب'
lines.english: Afwan — it means 'you're welcome'.
lines.transliteration: afwan — ta'nii 'laa shukr alaa waajib'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَعَ السَّلامَة — عِندَ الوَداع
lines.english: Ma'a salama — when saying goodbye.
lines.transliteration: ma'a as-salaama — inda al-wadaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَباحُ الخَير — في الصَّباح
lines.english: Sabah al-khayr — in the morning.
lines.transliteration: sabaah al-khayr — fis-sabaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَظيم! أَنتَ تَتَعَلَّم بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Great! You're learning quickly.
lines.transliteration: aziim! anta tata'allam bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَساءُ الخَير — في المَساء
lines.english: Masa' al-khayr — in the evening.
lines.transliteration: masaa' al-khayr — fil-masaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَعَم — يَعني 'أَيوه'
lines.english: Na'am — means 'yes'.
lines.transliteration: na'am — ya'nii 'aywa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا — عَكْسُها
lines.english: La — its opposite.
lines.transliteration: laa — aksuha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ واحَة الحُروف — مَكانٌ لِتَعَلُّم العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: This is the Oasis of Letters — a place for learning Arabic.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi waahat al-huruuf — makaanun li-ta'allum al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَكَلَّم مَع النّاس هُنا وَسَتَتَعَلَّم كَلِمات جَديدَة
lines.english: Talk to the people here and you will learn new words.
lines.transliteration: takallam ma'a an-naas hunaa wa satata'allam kalimaat jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فاطِمَة التّاجِرَة عِنْدَها كَلِمات السُّوق
lines.english: Fatima the merchant has market words.
lines.transliteration: faatima at-taajira indahaa kalimaat as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَخالِد الطّالِب يُحِبّ المُسابَقات
lines.english: And Khalid the student likes quizzes.
lines.transliteration: wa khaalid at-taalib yuhibb al-musaabaqaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل أَنتَ مُسْتَعِدّ لِتَعَلُّم الحُروف؟
lines.english: Are you ready to learn the letters?
lines.transliteration: hal anta musta'idd li-ta'allum al-huruuf?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم، طالِبَ العِلْم. بِسْمِ اللَّه
lines.english: Peace be upon you, seeker of knowledge. In the name of God.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum, taalib al-ilm. bismillaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَمَّ تُريدُ أَن تَتَكَلَّم؟
lines.english: What would you like to discuss?
lines.transliteration: amma turiidu an tatakallam?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعْلَمُ أَنَّنا نُقَدِّمُ دُروسًا في قَواعِدِ اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّة؟
lines.english: Did you know we offer lessons in Arabic grammar rules?
lines.transliteration: hal taʿlam annanā nuqaddim durūsan fī qawāʿid al-lugha al-ʿarabiyya?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَواعِدُ تُساعِدُكَ على فَهْمِ بِنْيَةِ الجُمَلِ وَالكَلِمات
lines.english: Grammar helps you understand sentence and word structure.
lines.transliteration: al-qawāʿid tusāʿiduka ʿalā fahm binyat al-jumal wa-l-kalimāt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَرِّبْها! اِفْتَحْ قائِمَةَ الإيقافِ المُؤَقَّتِ واخْتَرْ 'أَنْشِطَة'
lines.english: Try it! Open the pause menu and choose 'Activities'.
lines.transliteration: jarribhā! iftaḥ qāʾimat al-īqāf al-muʾaqqat wa-khtar 'anshiṭa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّحِيّاتُ أَساسُ الأَدَب. بِسْمِ اللَّه، لِنَبْدَأ
lines.english: Greetings are the foundation of manners. In God's name, let us begin.
lines.transliteration: at-tahiyyaatu asaas al-adab. bismillaah, linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: واحَةُ الحُروفِ مَكانٌ قَديمٌ جِدّاً
lines.english: The Oasis of Letters is a very ancient place.
lines.transliteration: waahat al-huruuf makaanun qadiimun jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا تَعَلَّمَ العُلَماءُ الأَوائِلُ اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Here the first scholars learned the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: hunaa ta'allama al-ulamaa' al-awaa'il al-lugha al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَدَيَّ مَهَمَّة لَكَ يا طالِب
lines.english: I have a task for you, student.
lines.transliteration: ladayya mahamma laka ya taalib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِذْهَب وَتَعَلَّم عَشْرَ كَلِمات جَديدَة
lines.english: Go and learn ten new words.
lines.transliteration: idh-hab wa ta'allam ashr kalimaat jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في الخَطِّ العَرَبيِّ سِتَّةُ أُصولٍ كَبيرَة
lines.english: In Arabic calligraphy there are six great canonical scripts
lines.transliteration: fil-khatt al-arabi sittat usul kabira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسخ وَالثُّلُث وَالرِّقعَة وَالدِّيواني وَالفارِسي وَالكوفي
lines.english: Naskh, Thuluth, Ruq'ah, Diwani, Farsi, and Kufi
lines.transliteration: an-naskh wath-thuluth war-ruq'a wad-diwani wal-farisi wal-kufi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ مُقلَة في القَرنِ العاشِر وَضَعَ قَواعِدَ النِّسَب
lines.english: Ibn Muqla in the 10th century established the proportional rules
lines.transliteration: ibn muqla fil-qarn al-'ashir wada'a qawa'id an-nisab
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Muqla (886-940 CE) created the proportional system that standardized Arabic calligraphy. Each letter is measured in dots relative to the alif.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ حَرفٍ يُقاسُ بِنِقاطٍ نِسبَةً إلى الأَلِف
lines.english: Every letter is measured in dots relative to the alif
lines.transliteration: kullu harf yuqas bi-niqat nisbatan ila al-alif

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشِّعرُ عِندَ المُتَنَبّي بَلَغَ ذُروَتَهُ — 'أَنا الَّذي نَظَرَ الأَعمى إلى أَدَبي'
lines.english: Poetry reached its peak with Al-Mutanabbi — 'I am he whose literature the blind can see'
lines.transliteration: ash-shi'r 'inda al-mutanabbi balagha dhurwatahu
lines.culturalNote: Al-Mutanabbi (915-965 CE) is considered the greatest Arabic poet. His name means 'the one who claimed to be a prophet' — a childhood nickname that stuck.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسمِ اللَّه! اليَومَ سَنَتَعَلَّمُ قاعِدَةً عَظيمَة في العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: In God's name! Today we will learn a great rule in Arabic.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! al-yawma sanata'allamu qaa'idatan aziima fil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيسَ في العَرَبِيَّةِ فِعلٌ لِـ'كانَ' في المُضارِع — أَنا طالِبٌ، لَيسَ 'أَنا أَكونُ طالِباً'
lines.english: Arabic has no verb 'to be' in the present tense — 'ana taalib' means 'I am a student', not 'I am being a student'.
lines.transliteration: laysa fil-arabiyya fi'lun li-kaana fil-mudaari' — ana taalib, laysa 'ana akuunu taaliban'
lines.culturalNote: Arabic omits the copula (verb 'to be') in present tense nominal sentences. This is called a 'jumlah ismiyya' — a noun sentence. English learners often struggle with this elegant simplicity.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل مَعي: أَنا طالِبٌ — هَذِهِ جُملَةٌ اسمِيَّة
lines.english: Say with me: Ana taalib — this is a nominal sentence.
lines.transliteration: qul ma'ii: ana taalib — haadhihi jumlatun ismiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن أَنتَ: مَن أَنتَ؟ قُل اسمَك بِالعَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Now you: who are you? Say your name in Arabic.
lines.transliteration: al-aan anta: man anta? qul ismaka bil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! في العَرَبِيَّةِ الكَلِماتُ لَها مُذَكَّر وَمُؤَنَّث
lines.english: Well done! In Arabic, words have masculine and feminine forms.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! fil-arabiyya al-kalimaat lahaa mudhakkar wa mu'annath

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتابٌ — مُذَكَّر. مَكتَبَةٌ — مُؤَنَّث. تَلاحَظُ حَرفَ التّاء في النِّهايَة؟
lines.english: Kitab — masculine. Maktaba — feminine. Notice the 'ta' letter at the end?
lines.transliteration: kitaabun — mudhakkar. maktabatun — mu'annath. talaahazu harf at-taa' fin-nihaaya?
lines.culturalNote: The taa marbuuta (ة) marks feminine nouns in Arabic. It was invented by early Arab grammarians to standardize gender marking, making Arabic one of the most systematic languages for gender in grammar.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتاب — كِتابان — كُتُب. هَذا الجَمع! الجَمعُ التَّكسيريّ
lines.english: Kitab — two books — books. This is the plural! The broken plural.
lines.transliteration: kitaab — kitaabayn — kutub. haadhaa al-jam'! al-jam' at-taksiiriyy

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَمعُ التَّكسيريُّ يُغَيِّرُ شَكلَ الكَلِمَة مِن الداخِل — هَذا فَريدٌ في العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: The broken plural changes the shape of the word from within — this is unique to Arabic.
lines.transliteration: al-jam' at-taksiiriyyu yughayyiru shakl al-kalima min ad-daakhil — haadhaa fariidun fil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا تَقلَق! حَتّى العُلَماءُ الكِبارُ بَدَأوا مِن الصِّفر
lines.english: Do not worry! Even the great scholars started from zero.
lines.transliteration: laa taqlaq! hatta al-ulama al-kibaar bada'uu min as-sifr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الإمامُ سيبَوَيه كانَ فارِسِيَّ الأَصل وَأَصبَحَ أَعظَمَ نَحويٍّ عَرَبيّ
lines.english: Imam Sibawayhi was of Persian origin and became the greatest Arab grammarian.
lines.transliteration: al-imaam sibawayhi kaana farisiyya al-asl wa asbaha a'dhama nahwiyyin arabii
lines.culturalNote: Sibawayhi (c.760-796 CE) wrote 'Al-Kitab' — the foundational work of Arabic grammar. He was Persian, proving that mastery of Arabic belongs to all who pursue it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ يَحتاجُ صَبراً. بِسمِ اللَّه، لِنُكمِل
lines.english: Knowledge requires patience. In God's name, let us continue.
lines.transliteration: al-ilm yahtaaju sabran. bismillaah, linukmil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسمِ اللَّه! هَل تَعلَمُ مِن أَينَ جاءَت كَلِمَةُ 'algorithm'؟
lines.english: In God's name! Do you know where the word 'algorithm' came from?
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! hal ta'lamu min ayna jaa'at kalimat 'algorithm'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن اسمِ العالِمِ مُحَمَّد بنِ موسى الخَوارِزميّ
lines.english: From the name of the scholar Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi.
lines.transliteration: min ism al-aalim muhammad ibn muusa al-khwaarizmi
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khwarizmi (780-850 CE) was the father of algebra. His book 'Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr' gave us the word 'algebra' (al-jabr). His name, Latinized as 'Algoritmi', became 'algorithm'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَةُ 'algebra' مِن 'الجَبر' — عُنوانُ كِتابِهِ العَظيم
lines.english: And 'algebra' from 'al-jabr' — the title of his great book.
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat 'algebra' min 'al-jabr' — unwaanu kitaabihi al-aziim
lines.culturalNote: The word 'algebra' comes from 'al-jabr wa al-muqabala' (reunion of broken parts and balancing). Al-Khwarizmi also introduced the Indian zero concept to the Islamic world.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العُلَماءُ العَرَبُ نَقَلوا العِلمَ وَأَضافوا إِلَيه. هَذا شَرَفُنا
lines.english: Arab scholars transmitted knowledge and added to it. This is our honor.
lines.transliteration: al-ulama al-arab naqalu al-ilm wa adaafuu ilayh. haadhaa sharafunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم العَرَبِيَّة وَسَتَفتَحُ لَكَ أَبوابَ الحِكمَة القَديمَة
lines.english: Learn Arabic and it will open for you the doors of ancient wisdom.
lines.transliteration: ta'allam al-arabiyya wa sataftahu laka abwaab al-hikma al-qadiima

personality.catchphrase: بِسْمِ اللَّه — bismillaah (In the name of God)

name: Merchant Fatima
role: Teaches trade and market vocabulary

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً يا زَبون! تَفَضَّل
greeting.english: Welcome, customer! Come in
greeting.transliteration: ahlan ya zabuun! tafaddal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَباً! أَنا فاطِمَة، صاحِبَة هَذا الدُّكّان
lines.english: Hello! I am Fatima, owner of this shop.
lines.transliteration: marhaban! ana faatima, saahibat haadha ad-dukkaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِنْدي أَشْياء كَثيرَة. هَل تُريدُ أَن تَتَعَلَّم أَسْماءَها؟
lines.english: I have many things. Do you want to learn their names?
lines.transliteration: indii ashyaa' kathiira. hal turiidu an tata'allama asmaa'ahaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَيِّب! هَذا يُسَمّى دُكّان
lines.english: Good! This is called a shop.
lines.transliteration: tayyib! haadha yusammaa dukkaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالمَكان الكَبير يُسَمّى سُوق
lines.english: And the big place is called a market.
lines.transliteration: wal-makaan al-kabiir yusammaa suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَهَذا فُلوس — نَقود
lines.english: And this is money — currency.
lines.transliteration: wa haadha fuluus — nuquud

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن اِخْتَبِر نَفسَك!
lines.english: Now test yourself!
lines.transliteration: al-aan ikhtabir nafsak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً مَرَّة أُخرى! لِنُكْمِل دَرسَنا
lines.english: Hello again! Let's continue our lesson.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marra ukhraa! linukmil darsanaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَمَن — يَعني السِّعْر
lines.english: Thaman — means the price.
lines.transliteration: thaman — ya'nii as-si'r

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَخيص — يَعني السِّعْر قَليل
lines.english: Rakhiis — means the price is low.
lines.transliteration: rakhiis — ya'nii as-si'r qaliil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: غالي — يَعني السِّعْر كَبير
lines.english: Ghaali — means the price is high.
lines.transliteration: ghaali — ya'nii as-si'r kabiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِشْتَرى — يَعني يَأخُذ بِفُلوس
lines.english: Ishtara — means to take with money (to buy).
lines.transliteration: ishtaraa — ya'nii ya'khudh bi-fuluus

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاء الله! تاجِر مُمتاز!
lines.english: Mashallah! An excellent merchant!
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! taajir mumtaaz!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: باعَ — عَكْس اِشتَرى
lines.english: Baa'a — the opposite of bought (to sell).
lines.transliteration: baa'a — aks ishtaraa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ذَهَب — المَعدِن الأَصفَر الثَّمين
lines.english: Dhahab — the precious yellow metal (gold).
lines.transliteration: dhahab — al-ma'din al-asfar ath-thamiin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِضَّة — المَعدِن الأَبيَض
lines.english: Fidda — the white metal (silver).
lines.transliteration: fidda — al-ma'din al-abyad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا زَبون! يَلّا، ماذا تُريد اليَوم؟
lines.english: Welcome, customer! Come on, what do you want today?
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya zabuun! yalla, maadha turiid al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ طَريقَةً مُمْتِعَةً لِلتَّدَرُّب على المُفْرَدات؟
lines.english: Want a fun way to practice vocabulary?
lines.transliteration: hal turīd ṭarīqa mumtiʿa li-t-tadarrub ʿalā al-mufradāt?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَدَيْنا أَلْعابٌ صَغيرَةٌ — لُعْبَة البَحْثِ عَن الكَلِمات وَأَكْثَر!
lines.english: We have mini-games — word search and more!
lines.transliteration: ladaynā alʿāb ṣaghīra — luʿbat al-baḥth ʿan al-kalimāt wa-akthar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِفْتَحْ قائِمَةَ الإيقاف وَاخْتَرْ 'أَنْشِطَة' ثُمَّ 'أَلْعاب'
lines.english: Open the pause menu and choose 'Activities' then 'Mini-Games'.
lines.transliteration: iftaḥ qāʾimat al-īqāf wa-khtar 'anshiṭa' thumma 'alʿāb'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا! سَأُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمات السُّوق
lines.english: Come on! I'll teach you market words.
lines.transliteration: yalla! sa-u'allimuka kalimaat as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ التّاجِرَ حَسَن عِندَهُ بَضائِع جَديدَة
lines.english: I heard that trader Hassan has new goods.
lines.transliteration: sami'tu anna at-taajir hasan indahu badaa'i' jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالسُّوقُ مَشْغول جِدّاً هَذِهِ الأَيّام!
lines.english: And the market is very busy these days!
lines.transliteration: was-suuq mashghuul jiddan haadhihi al-ayyaam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعَدَة! هَل تَسْتَطيعُ إِيجادَ زَبائِن لي؟
lines.english: I need help! Can you find customers for me?
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'ada! hal tastatii'u ijaad zabaa'in lii?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعلَم أَنَّ طَريقَ الحَريرِ كانَ يَمُرُّ مِن هُنا؟
lines.english: Did you know the Silk Road passed through here?
lines.transliteration: hal ta'lam anna tariq al-harir kana yamurru min huna?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التُّجّارُ العَرَبُ نَقَلوا الأَرقامَ إلى أوروبا
lines.english: Arab traders carried numerals to Europe
lines.transliteration: at-tujjaar al-arab naqalu al-arqaam ila urubba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَةُ 'خَوارِزمي' أَصبَحَت 'algorithm' بالإنجليزيَّة
lines.english: The word 'Khwarizmi' became 'algorithm' in English
lines.transliteration: kalimat 'khwarizmi' asbahat 'algorithm' bil-injiliziyya
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khwarizmi (780-850 CE) wrote the foundational text on algebra. His name, Latinized as 'Algoritmi', gave us the word 'algorithm'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَةُ 'تَعريفَة' أَعطَت الإنجليزيَّة 'tariff'
lines.english: And 'ta'rifa' gave English the word 'tariff'
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat 'ta'rifa' a'tat al-injiliziyya 'tariff'
lines.culturalNote: Many English trade words come from Arabic: tariff (ta'rifa), magazine (makhazin), cotton (qutn), sugar (sukkar).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا يا زَبون! أُعَلِّمُكَ فَنَّ المُساوَمَة. هَذا أَهَمُّ شَيء في السُّوق!
lines.english: Come on, customer! I'll teach you the art of bargaining. This is the most important thing in the market!
lines.transliteration: yalla ya zabuun! u'allimuka fann al-musaawama. haadhaa ahammu shay' fis-suuq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوَّلاً: لا تُظهِر اهتِمامَك. قُل: 'غالي' — هَذه أَداةٌ ذَهَبِيَّة
lines.english: First: don't show your interest. Say: 'ghaali' (expensive) — this is a golden tool.
lines.transliteration: awwalan: laa tudhir ihtimaamak. qul: 'ghaali' — haadhihi adaatun dhahabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثُمَّ: 'هَذا رَخيص في السُّوق الآخَر!' — المُقارَنَة سِلاحٌ قَوِيّ
lines.english: Then: 'this is cheap at the other market!' — comparison is a powerful weapon.
lines.transliteration: thumma: 'haadhaa rakhiis fis-suuq al-aakhar!' — al-muqaarana silaahun qawii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَخيراً: اِمشِ! المَشيُ يَجعَلُ التّاجِرَ يُخَفِّضُ السِّعر — جَرِّب!
lines.english: And finally: walk away! Walking makes the trader lower the price — try it!
lines.transliteration: wa akhiiran: imshi! al-mashi yaj'al at-taajir yukhaffffid as-si'r — jarrib!

choices.english: How do I say 'lower the price'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل: 'خَفِّض قَليلاً مِن فَضلَك!' — ثُمَّ اِبتَسِم
lines.english: Say: 'lower a little please!' — then smile.
lines.transliteration: qul: 'khaffid qaliilan min fadlak!' — thumma ibtasim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَيعُ وَالشِّراءُ لُغَةٌ. التّاجِرُ الجَيِّدُ يُسمِع الآخَرين ما يُريدون أَن يَسمَعوه
lines.english: Buying and selling is a language. The good trader makes others hear what they want to hear.
lines.transliteration: al-bay' wash-shiraa' lugha. at-taajir al-jayyid yusmi' al-aakhariina maa yuriiduuna an yasma'uuh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ حِكمَةُ سَبعِينَ سَنَة مِن التِّجارَة. يَلّا نَختَبِر!
lines.english: This is the wisdom of seventy years of trade. Come on, let's test!
lines.transliteration: haadhihi hikmat sab'iin sana min at-tijaara. yalla nakhtabir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا يا زَبون! هَل تَعلَمُ كَم كَلِمَة أَنجليزيَّة جاءَت مِن لُغَتِنا؟
lines.english: Come on, customer! Do you know how many English words came from our language?
lines.transliteration: yalla ya zabuun! hal ta'lamu kam kalima injiliziyya jaa'at min lughatinaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'magazine' — مِن 'مَخازِن' يَعني مَكانُ التَّخزين. أَنا عَرِفتُ هَذا!
lines.english: 'Magazine' — from 'makhazin' meaning storehouse. I knew this one!
lines.transliteration: 'magazine' — min 'makhazin' ya'nii makaan at-takhziiin. ana arift haadhaa!
lines.culturalNote: The word 'magazine' comes from Arabic 'makhazin' (plural of makhzan — storehouse). Arab merchants stored goods in makhazin across the Silk Road trade routes.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'tariff' مِن 'تَعريفَة' — قائِمَةُ الأَسعار في السُّوق القَديم
lines.english: 'Tariff' from 'ta'rifa' — the price list in the old market.
lines.transliteration: 'tariff' min 'ta'rifa' — qaa'imat al-as'aar fis-suuq al-qadiim
lines.culturalNote: The word 'tariff' entered English through Spanish 'tarifa' from Arabic 'ta'rifa' (notification, schedule of prices). Arab merchants used ta'rifa notices posted at ports.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَذَلِكَ 'mattress' مِن 'مَطرَح' وَ'sofa' مِن 'صُفَّة'!
lines.english: Also 'mattress' from 'matrah' and 'sofa' from 'suffa'!
lines.transliteration: kadhaalika 'mattress' min 'matrah' wa 'sofa' min 'suffa'!
lines.culturalNote: Many English household words are Arabic in origin: mattress (matrah — a place to throw), sofa (suffa — bench), jar (jarra), alcohol (al-kuhl), syrup (sharab).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لُغَتُنا مَلِيئَةٌ بِالثَّروات — كَسُوقِنا! يَلّا!
lines.english: Our language is full of riches — like our market! Come on!
lines.transliteration: lughatunaa malii'atun bith-thawraat — kasuuqinaa! yalla!

personality.catchphrase: يَلّا يا زَبون! — yalla ya zabuun! (Come on, customer!)

name: Student Khalid
role: Quiz practice partner and daily challenges

greeting.arabic: يا هَلا! أَنا خالِد
greeting.english: Hey there! I'm Khalid
greeting.transliteration: ya halaa! ana khaalid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبا! أَنا خالِد. أَنا أَيْضاً أَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: Hello! I'm Khalid. I'm also learning.
lines.transliteration: marhaba! ana khaalid. ana aydan ata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن نَتَدَرَّب مَعاً؟
lines.english: Do you want to practice together?
lines.transliteration: hal turiidu an nataddarab ma'an?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمْتاز! سَأَسْأَلُك عَشْر أَسْئِلَة
lines.english: Excellent! I'll ask you ten questions.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! sa-as'aluka ashr as'ila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبا! هَل أَنتَ جاهِز لِتَحَدّي اليَوم؟
lines.english: Hello! Are you ready for today's challenge?
lines.transliteration: marhaba! hal anta jaahiz li-tahaddii al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! ماذا تُريد أَن نَفْعَل؟
lines.english: Hey there! What do you want to do?
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! maadha turiidu an naf'al?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا! خَلّينا نَتَدَرَّب!
lines.english: Let's go! Let's practice!
lines.transliteration: yalla! khalliina nataddarab!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَتَعَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ مِثْلَك!
lines.english: I'm learning Arabic just like you!
lines.transliteration: ana ata'allam al-arabiyya mithlak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلَّ يَوم أَدْرُسُ مَعَ الشَّيْخ يوسُف
lines.english: Every day I study with Sheikh Yusuf.
lines.transliteration: kull yawm adrusu ma'a ash-shaykh yuusuf

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ هُناكَ كَنْز مَخْفيّ في الصَّحْراء!
lines.english: I heard there's a hidden treasure in the desert!
lines.transliteration: sami'tu anna hunaaka kanz makhfii fis-sahraa'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِنْ لا أَعْرِف إِذا كانَ هَذا صَحيح
lines.english: But I don't know if this is true.
lines.transliteration: laakin laa a'rif idhaa kaana haadhaa sahiih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! أَنا غَلِطتُ اليَوم في الدَّرس — قُلتُ 'أَنا هُوَ ذاهِب' بَدَلاً مِن 'أَنا ذاهِب'!
lines.english: Hey there! I made a mistake in class today — I said 'I am he going' instead of 'I am going'!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! ana ghalitt al-yawm fid-dars — qultu 'ana huwa dhaahib' badalan min 'ana dhaahib'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّيخُ يوسُف قالَ: لَيسَ في العَرَبِيَّةِ ضَميرٌ مُنفَصِلٌ مَعَ الفِعل في العادَة
lines.english: Sheikh Yusuf said: in Arabic, a separate pronoun doesn't usually go with the verb.
lines.transliteration: ash-shaykh yuusuf qaala: laysa fil-arabiyya damiir munfasil ma'a al-fi'l fil-'aada
lines.culturalNote: In Arabic, the subject pronoun is often embedded within the verb conjugation. 'Dhahaba' already means 'he went' — adding 'huwa' separately is redundant (though used for emphasis).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا صَعبٌ! أَنتَ بَالتَّأكيد تَغلَطُ أَيضاً أَحياناً، صَحّ؟
lines.english: This is hard! You definitely make mistakes sometimes too, right?
lines.transliteration: haadhaa sa'b! anta bittakiid taghlat aydan ahyaanan, sahh?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُهِمُّ أَنَّنا نُكمِل وَلا نَستَسلِم — هَذا ما يَقولُهُ الشَّيخ
lines.english: What matters is that we continue and don't give up — that's what the Sheikh says.
lines.transliteration: al-muhimm annana nukmil wa laa nastaslim — haadhaa maa yaquuluhu ash-shaykh

choices.english: I make lots of mistakes too!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! إِذاً نَحنُ سَواء! هَيّا نَغلَط مَعاً ونَتَعَلَّم مَعاً!
lines.english: Hey there! So we're the same! Let's make mistakes together and learn together!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! idhan nahnu sawaa'! hayya naghlat ma'an wa nata'allam ma'an!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّيخُ يوسُف يَقولُ: الغَلَطُ في التَّعَلُّم كَالسَّقطَةِ في المَشي — ضَرورِيَّة!
lines.english: Sheikh Yusuf says: mistakes in learning are like stumbling in walking — necessary!
lines.transliteration: ash-shaykh yuusuf yaquul: al-ghalat fit-ta'allum kas-saqta fil-mashi — daruurriyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبِيَّةُ سَهلَةٌ إذا لم تَخَفْ مِنَ الغَلَط. سَهل — هَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ مُهِمَّة!
lines.english: Arabic is easy if you don't fear mistakes. Easy — that is an important word!
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya sahla idha lam takhaf min al-ghalat. sahl — hadhihi kalimah muhimma!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِفُ 'صَحيح'؟ تَعني correct. 'غَلَط' تَعني wrong. تَعَلَّمهُما!
lines.english: Do you know 'sahiih'? It means correct. 'Ghalat' means wrong. Learn both!
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rifu 'sahiih'? ta'nii correct. 'ghalat' ta'nii wrong. ta'allamahumaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! تَعَلَّمتُ شَيئاً مُذهِلاً اليَوم — لَيسَ في العَرَبِيَّةِ 'is' و 'am' و 'are'!
lines.english: Hey there! I learned something amazing today — Arabic has no 'is', 'am', or 'are'!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! ta'allamtu shay'an mudhilan al-yawm — laysa fil-arabiyya 'is' wa 'am' wa 'are'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَدَلاً مِن 'I am a student' نَقول فَقَط 'أَنا طالِب'
lines.english: Instead of 'I am a student' we just say 'ana taalib'.
lines.transliteration: badalan min 'I am a student' naquul faqat 'ana taalib'
lines.culturalNote: Classical Arabic has no present-tense copula. The sentence 'al-bayt kabiir' (the house is big) has no verb — the meaning is carried purely by the juxtaposition. This is called a nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَأَنَّكَ تَقول 'I, student.' بِدونِ فِعل! مُمتاز وَمُبَسَّط!
lines.english: It's as if you say 'I, student.' without a verb! Excellent and simplified!
lines.transliteration: ka'annaka taquul 'I, student.' bidooni fi'l! mumtaaz wa mubassit!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل مَعي: 'أَنا طالِب!' ثُمَّ 'الكِتابُ كَبير!'
lines.english: Say with me: 'Ana taalib!' Then 'al-kitaab kabiir!'
lines.transliteration: qul ma'ii: 'ana taalib!' thumma 'al-kitaab kabiir!'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَيِّد! كَبير — big! صَغير — small! هَذِهِ أَسهَلُ كَلِماتٍ في العَرَبِيَّة لأَنَّهُ لا يُوجَدُ فِعلٌ!
lines.english: Good! Kabiir — big! Saghiir — small! These are the easiest words in Arabic because there's no verb!
lines.transliteration: jayyid! kabiir — big! saghiir — small! haadhihi ashal kalimaat fil-arabiyya li'annahu laa yuujad fi'l!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! عِندي مُسابَقَة — هَيّا نَختَبِر!
lines.english: Hey there! I have a quiz — let's test it!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! indii musaabaqaa — hayya nakhtabir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا تَعَلَّمتُ دَرساً جَديداً اليَوم! تَعال نَتَذاكَر
lines.english: I learned a new lesson today! Come, let's review together.
lines.transliteration: ana ta'allamtu darsan jadiidan al-yawm! ta'aal natadhaakar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُستاذ يوسُف قال: المُراجَعَة أُمّ العِلم — ما رَأيُك؟
lines.english: Teacher Yusuf said: 'Review is the mother of knowledge' — what do you think?
lines.transliteration: ustaadh yuusuf qaal: al-muraaja'a umm al-'ilm — maa ra'yuk?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا كَثيراً ما أَنسى — لَكِن التَّكرار يُساعِد كَثيراً
lines.english: I often forget — but repetition helps a great deal.
lines.transliteration: ana kathiiran maa ansaa — laakin at-tikraar yusaa'id kathiiran

personality.catchphrase: يا هَلا! — ya halaa! (Hey there!)

name: Librarian Ibrahim
role: Teaches numbers and counting

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ في المَكتَبَة
greeting.english: Welcome to the library
greeting.transliteration: ahlan bika fil-maktaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم! أَنا إِبراهيم، أَمينُ هَذِهِ المَكتَبَة
lines.english: Peace be upon you! I am Ibrahim, the keeper of this library.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum! ana ibraahiim, amiinu haadhihi al-maktaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في هَذِهِ المَكتَبَة آلافُ الكُتُب. كُلُّ كِتابٍ يَحمِلُ عِلماً
lines.english: In this library there are thousands of books. Every book carries knowledge.
lines.transliteration: fii haadhihi al-maktaba aalaaf al-kutub. kullu kitaabin yahmilu ilman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَبدَأ بِأَساسِ كُلِّ عِلم — الأَعداد! الكَلِمَةُ الأولى: واحِد
lines.english: Let us begin with the foundation of all knowledge -- numbers! The first word: one.
lines.transliteration: linabda' bi-asaasi kulli ilm — al-a'daad! al-kalimatu al-uulaa: waahid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِثنان — كَما في كِتابَين عَلى الطّاوِلَة
lines.english: Two -- like two books on the table.
lines.transliteration: ithnaan — kamaa fii kitaabayn ala at-taawila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَة — عَدَدُ الرُّفوفِ أَمامَك
lines.english: Three -- the number of shelves in front of you.
lines.transliteration: thalaatha — adadur-rufuufi amaamak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! لِنَرى كَم تَذكُر
lines.english: Well done! Let us see how much you remember.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! linara kam tadhkur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِعَودَتِك! لِنُكمِل العَدّ
lines.english: Welcome back! Let us continue counting.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bi-awdatik! linukmil al-add

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَعَة — مِثلُ أَربَعِ زَوايا الكِتاب
lines.english: Four -- like the four corners of a book.
lines.transliteration: arba'a — mithlu arba'i zawaaya al-kitaab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خَمسَة — عَدَدُ أَصابِعِ اليَد الواحِدَة
lines.english: Five -- the number of fingers on one hand.
lines.transliteration: khamsa — adadu asaabi'i al-yad al-waahida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سِتَّة — عَدَدُ أَيّامِ الدِّراسَة
lines.english: Six -- the number of study days.
lines.transliteration: sitta — adadu ayyaam ad-diraasa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَبعَة — عَدَدُ أَيّامِ الأُسبوع
lines.english: Seven -- the number of days in a week.
lines.transliteration: sab'a — adadu ayyaam al-usbuu'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا نَمتَحِن ما تَعَلَّمت!
lines.english: Let us test what you have learned!
lines.transliteration: hayyaa namtahin maa ta'allamta!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ الله! أَنتَ تَتَقَدَّمُ بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Mashallah! You are progressing quickly.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! anta tataqaddamu bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَمانِيَة — رَقَمٌ جَميل
lines.english: Eight -- a beautiful number.
lines.transliteration: thamaaniya — raqamun jamiil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تِسعَة — قَبلَ العَشَرَة مُباشَرَة
lines.english: Nine -- right before ten.
lines.transliteration: tis'a — qabla al-'ashara mubaashara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَشَرَة! أَكمَلتَ العَدّ مِن واحِد إِلى عَشَرَة!
lines.english: Ten! You have completed counting from one to ten!
lines.transliteration: 'ashara! akmalta al-add min waahid ilaa 'ashara!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمتِحانٌ أَخير لِلأَعداد
lines.english: One final test for the numbers.
lines.transliteration: imtihaanun akhiir lil-a'daad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ في المَكتَبَة. العِلْمُ نور
lines.english: Welcome to the library. Knowledge is light.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bika fil-maktaba. al-ilmu nuur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيْفَ يُمْكِنُني مُساعَدَتُك؟
lines.english: How can I help you?
lines.transliteration: kayfa yumkinunii musaa'adatuk?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِماتُ العَرَبِيَّةُ تَأتي مِن جُذورٍ ثُلاثِيَّة
lines.english: Arabic words come from three-letter roots.
lines.transliteration: al-kalimāt al-ʿarabiyya taʾtī min judhūr thulāthiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِنْدَنا أَداةٌ رائِعَة لِاسْتِكْشافِ الجُذورِ العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: We have a wonderful tool for exploring Arabic roots.
lines.transliteration: ʿindanā adāt rāʾiʿa li-stikshāf al-judhūr al-ʿarabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِفْتَحْ قائِمَةَ الإيقافِ واخْتَرْ 'أَنْشِطَة' ثُمَّ 'جُذورُ الكَلِمات'
lines.english: Open the pause menu and choose 'Activities' then 'Word Roots'.
lines.transliteration: iftaḥ qāʾimat al-īqāf wa-khtar 'anshiṭa' thumma 'judhūr al-kalimāt'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَعْدادُ أَساسُ الرِّياضِيّات. لِنَبْدَأ
lines.english: Numbers are the foundation of mathematics. Let us begin.
lines.transliteration: al-a'daadu asaas ar-riyaadiyyaat. linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَكتَبَةُ عُمْرُها أَكْثَر مِن أَلْف سَنَة
lines.english: This library is more than a thousand years old.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-maktaba umruhaa akthar min alf sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فيها كُتُب نادِرَة جِدّاً عَن اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: It contains very rare books about the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: fiihaa kutub naadira jiddan an al-lugha al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعَدَةً في تَرتيبِ الكُتُب
lines.english: I need help organizing the books.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'ada fii tartiib al-kutub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل يُمْكِنُكَ تَعَلُّم الأَرقام لِمُساعَدَتي؟
lines.english: Can you learn the numbers to help me?
lines.transliteration: hal yumkinuka ta'allum al-arqaam li-musaa'adatii?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَكتَبَةُ قُرطُبَة كانَت تَحوي أَربَعمِئَةِ أَلفِ كِتاب
lines.english: The library of Cordoba held 400,000 books
lines.transliteration: maktabat qurtuba kanat tahwi arba'mi'at alf kitab
lines.culturalNote: In the 10th century, Cordoba's library was the largest in Europe. By comparison, the largest monastery library in Christian Europe held about 400 books.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صِناعَةُ الوَرَقِ جاءَت مِن الصّينِ عَبرَ سَمَرقَند
lines.english: Papermaking came from China through Samarkand
lines.transliteration: sina'at al-waraq ja'at min as-sin 'abra samarqand
lines.culturalNote: After the Battle of Talas (751 CE), Arab forces captured Chinese papermakers. Within decades, paper mills spread across the Islamic world, enabling the translation movement.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَيتُ الحِكمَةِ في بَغداد تَرجَمَ كُنوزَ اليونان
lines.english: The House of Wisdom in Baghdad translated Greek treasures
lines.transliteration: bayt al-hikma fi baghdad tarjama kunuz al-yunan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ الهَيثَم أَسَّسَ عِلمَ البَصَريّات — كِتابُ المَناظِر
lines.english: Ibn al-Haytham founded optics — the Book of Optics
lines.transliteration: ibn al-haytham assasa 'ilm al-basariyyat — kitab al-manazir
lines.culturalNote: Ibn al-Haytham (965-1040 CE) disproved the Greek theory that eyes emit light. His 'Kitab al-Manazir' influenced Roger Bacon and Kepler.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً بِكَ يا طالِبَ المَعرِفَة. العِلمُ نور! اليَومَ سَنَتَعَلَّمُ كَلِماتِ القِراءَة
lines.english: Welcome, seeker of knowledge. Knowledge is light! Today we will learn reading words.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bika ya taalib al-ma'rifa. al-ilmu nuur! al-yawma sanata'allamu kalimaat al-qiraa'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كِتاب — هُوَ أَهَمُّ ما صَنَعَهُ الإِنسان. كَلِمَةُ 'كِتاب' مِن جَذرِ ك-ت-ب
lines.english: Kitab — it is the most important thing humanity made. The word 'kitab' from the root k-t-b.
lines.transliteration: kitaab — huwa ahamm maa sana'ahu al-insaan. kalimat 'kitaab' min jadr k-t-b

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن نَفسِ الجَذر: كَتَبَ (كَتَبَ)، كاتِب (writer)، مَكتوب (written)، مَكتَبَة (library)
lines.english: From the same root: kataba (wrote), kaatib (writer), maktuub (written), maktaba (library).
lines.transliteration: min nafs al-jadr: kataba, kaatib, maktuub, maktaba
lines.culturalNote: Arabic root system (trilateral roots) means related concepts share the same three core letters. K-T-B produces: kitaab (book), kaatib (writer), maktaba (library), maktub (letter/written), muktatib (student of writing).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا النِّظامُ العَبقَريُّ يَجعَلُ تَعَلُّمَ العَرَبِيَّةِ مَبنِيًّا على أُسُس
lines.english: This genius system makes learning Arabic built on foundations.
lines.transliteration: haadhaa an-nidhaam al-abqariyyu yaj'al ta'allum al-arabiyya mabniyyan ala usus

choices.english: Tell me about the House of Wisdom

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ممتاز! الجَذرُ ع-ل-م: عِلم (knowledge)، عالِم (scholar)، مُعَلِّم (teacher)، تَعَلَّمَ (learned)
lines.english: Excellent! The root '-l-m: ilm (knowledge), aalim (scholar), mu'allim (teacher), ta'allama (learned).
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! al-jadr '-l-m: ilm, aalim, mu'allim, ta'allama
lines.culturalNote: The root '-L-M appears in over 200 Arabic words. 'Alam' (world/universe), 'ilm' (knowledge), 'ta'lim' (education), 'ulama' (scholars) — all from three letters that suggest apprehension of reality.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَجَذرُ ق-ر-أ: قَرَأَ (read)، قِراءَة (reading)، قُرآن (Quran — that which is recited)
lines.english: And root q-r-': qara'a (read), qiraa'a (reading), Quran (that which is recited).
lines.transliteration: wa jadr q-r-': qara'a, qiraa'a, qur'aan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ نور! كُلُّ جَذرٍ كَبَيتٍ مَليءٍ بِالأَثاث — تَعَلَّم البَيتَ تَعرِف الأَثاث
lines.english: Knowledge is light! Each root is like a house full of furniture — learn the house, know the furniture.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu nuur! kullu jadr kabayt mali' bil-athath — ta'allam al-bayt ta'rif al-athath

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَيتُ الحِكمَة — أَعظَمُ مُؤَسَّسَةٍ عِلمِيَّة في تاريخِ الإِسلام
lines.english: The House of Wisdom — the greatest scientific institution in Islamic history.
lines.transliteration: bayt al-hikma — a'dhamu mu'assasa ilmiyya fii taariikh al-islaam
lines.culturalNote: Bayt al-Hikma (founded c.830 CE in Baghdad) was the first research institution in history. Scholars from across the world — Muslim, Christian, Jewish, Zoroastrian — translated and created knowledge under one roof.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَليفَةُ المَأمونُ جَمَعَ فيها عُلَماءَ مِن كُلِّ الأَديانِ وَالأُمَم
lines.english: Caliph al-Ma'mun gathered scholars of all religions and nations within it.
lines.transliteration: al-khalifa al-ma'muun jama'a fiihaa ulamaa' min kull al-adyaan wal-umam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَرجَمَ الحُنَينُ بنُ إِسحاق أَكثَرَ مِن مِئَةِ كِتابٍ يونانيٍّ
lines.english: Hunayn ibn Ishaq translated over 100 Greek books.
lines.transliteration: tarjama al-hunayn ibn ishaaq akthar min mi'at kitaabin yunaaniyy
lines.culturalNote: Hunayn ibn Ishaq (809-873 CE) was a Nestorian Christian who became the chief translator at Bayt al-Hikma. He translated Hippocrates, Galen, and Aristotle. The Abbasid caliphs paid translators by the weight of the books in gold.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ نور! وَكانَ بَغدادُ مَنارَةً تَشعُّ بِنورِ المَعرِفَة
lines.english: Knowledge is light! And Baghdad was a lighthouse shining with the light of knowledge.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu nuur! wa kaana baghdaad manaara tasha'u bi-nuur al-ma'rifa

personality.catchphrase: العِلْمُ نور — al-ilmu nuur (Knowledge is light)

name: Scribe Amina
role: Teaches colors and common phrases

greeting.arabic: مَرحَباً! الدُّنيا مَليئَة بِالأَلوان
greeting.english: Hello! The world is full of colors
greeting.transliteration: marhaban! ad-dunyaa malii'a bil-alwaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! أَنا أَمينَة، الكاتِبَة
lines.english: Welcome! I am Amina, the scribe.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! ana amiina, al-kaatiba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَكتُبُ كُلَّ يَومٍ بِأَحبارٍ مُلَوَّنَة. هَل تَعرِفُ الأَلوان بِالعَرَبِيَّة؟
lines.english: I write every day with colored inks. Do you know the colors in Arabic?
lines.transliteration: aktubu kulla yawmin bi-ahbaarin mulawwana. hal ta'rifu al-alwaan bil-arabiyya?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحمَر — لَونُ الحِبرِ الأَوَّل
lines.english: Red -- the color of the first ink.
lines.transliteration: ahmar — lawnu al-hibri al-awwal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَزرَق — كَلَونِ السَّماء
lines.english: Blue -- like the color of the sky.
lines.transliteration: azraq — kalawni as-samaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخضَر — كَأَوراقِ الشَّجَر
lines.english: Green -- like tree leaves.
lines.transliteration: akhdar — ka-awraaqi ash-shajar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَميل! لِنَرى إِن كُنتَ تَذكُر
lines.english: Beautiful! Let us see if you remember.
lines.transliteration: jamiil! linara in kunta tadhkur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! عِندي أَلوانٌ جَديدَة لَك
lines.english: You are back! I have new colors for you.
lines.transliteration: udta! indii alwaanun jadiida lak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَصفَر — كَلَونِ الشَّمسِ المُشرِقَة
lines.english: Yellow -- like the color of the rising sun.
lines.transliteration: asfar — kalawni ash-shamsi al-mushriqa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبيَض — لَونُ الوَرَقِ النَّظيف
lines.english: White -- the color of clean paper.
lines.transliteration: abyad — lawnu al-waraqi an-nadhiif

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَسوَد — لَونُ حِبرِ الكِتابَة
lines.english: Black -- the color of writing ink.
lines.transliteration: aswad — lawnu hibri al-kitaaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ذَهَبِيّ — لَونُ الزَّخارِف عَلى الكُتُب
lines.english: Golden -- the color of decorations on books.
lines.transliteration: dhahabii — lawnu az-zakhaarif ala al-kutub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن اِمتِحانُ الأَلوان!
lines.english: Now the color test!
lines.transliteration: al-aan imtihaanu al-alwaan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن سَأُعَلِّمُكَ جُمَلاً مُفيدَة لِلحَياةِ اليَومِيَّة
lines.english: Now I will teach you useful phrases for daily life.
lines.transliteration: al-aan sa-u'allimuka jumalan mufiida lil-hayaati al-yawmiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما اسمُك — لِلتَّعارُف
lines.english: What is your name -- for introductions.
lines.transliteration: ma ismuk — lit-ta'aaruf

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِسمي — عِندَما تُريدُ أَن تُعَرِّف عَن نَفسِك
lines.english: My name is -- when you want to introduce yourself.
lines.transliteration: ismii — indamaa turiidu an tu'arrif an nafsik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيفَ حالُك — لِلسُّؤال عَن الحال
lines.english: How are you -- to ask about someone's state.
lines.transliteration: kayfa haaluk — lis-su'aal an al-haal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! لِنَختَبِر هَذِهِ العِبارات
lines.english: Excellent! Let us test these phrases.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! linakhtabir haadhihi al-ibaaraat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً. الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ
lines.english: Welcome. Beautiful writing is art.
lines.transliteration: ahlan. al-khat al-jamiil fann

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: What do you want?
lines.transliteration: maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكِتابَةُ تَحْتاجُ صَبْراً وَدِقَّة
lines.english: Writing requires patience and precision.
lines.transliteration: al-kitaaba tahtaaju sabran wa diqqah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ حَرْف لَهُ شَكْلٌ خاصّ
lines.english: Each letter has its own special form.
lines.transliteration: kull harf lahu shaklun khaass

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ العَرَبيُّ لَهُ أَنواعٌ كَثيرَة
lines.english: Arabic calligraphy has many types.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-arabii lahu anwaa' kathiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسْخ، الثُّلُث، الكوفيّ — كُلُّها جَميلَة
lines.english: Naskh, Thuluth, Kufic — all are beautiful.
lines.transliteration: an-naskh, ath-thuluth, al-kuufii — kulluhaa jamiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مَن يَنْسَخُ هَذِهِ العِبارات
lines.english: I need someone to copy these phrases.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju man yansakh haadhihi al-ibaaraat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم عَشْرَ عِبارات وَعُدْ إِلَيّ
lines.english: Learn ten phrases and return to me.
lines.transliteration: ta'allam ashr ibaaraat wa ud ilayya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ! اليَوم سَأُريكَ أَنواعَ الخُطوطِ السِّتَّة الأَصيلَة
lines.english: Beautiful writing is art! Today I will show you the six authentic calligraphy scripts.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-jamiil fann! al-yawm sa-uriika anwaa' al-khutut as-sitta al-asiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسخُ — الخَطُّ الذي تَقرَأُهُ في القُرآن. واضِحٌ وَمُستَديم
lines.english: Naskh — the script you read in the Quran. Clear and enduring.
lines.transliteration: an-naskhu — al-khat alladhii taqra'uhu fil-qur'aan. waadihun wa mustadiim
lines.culturalNote: Naskh script was standardized in the 10th century and became the basis for modern Arabic printing. Its rounded, connected letters made it ideal for Quran manuscripts.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الثُّلُثُ — الخَطُّ المَلَكيُّ. يُزَيَّنُ بِهِ القِباب وَالمَساجِد
lines.english: Thuluth — the royal script. It decorates domes and mosques.
lines.transliteration: ath-thuluthu — al-khat al-malakiyyu. yuzayyan bihi al-qibab wal-masaajid
lines.culturalNote: Thuluth ('one third') script got its name because one third of each letter slopes. It is the most prestigious script for architectural and ceremonial use, seen on mosques from Istanbul to Cairo.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ مُقلَة — رَحِمَهُ اللَّه — وَضَعَ قانونَ الحَرفِ المُتَناسِب. مَجدٌ أَبَديّ
lines.english: Ibn Muqla — may God have mercy on him — established the law of the proportionate letter. Eternal glory.
lines.transliteration: ibn muqla — rahimahu allaah — wada'a qaanoon al-harf al-mutanaasib. majd abadii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكوفيُّ! الخَطُّ الأَقدَم — مِن مَدينَةِ الكوفَة في العِراق
lines.english: Kufic! The oldest script — from the city of Kufa in Iraq.
lines.transliteration: al-kuufiyyu! al-khat al-aqdam — min madinat al-kuufa fil-iraaq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخُطوطُ الكوفِيَّةُ كالرِّياضِيّات — زَوايا حادَّة وَخُطوطٌ مُستَقيمَة
lines.english: Kufic scripts are like mathematics — sharp angles and straight lines.
lines.transliteration: al-khutut al-kuufiyya kar-riyaadiyyaat — zawaaya haadda wa khutut mustaqiima
lines.culturalNote: Kufic script (7th-11th century CE) is the oldest Arabic calligraphy style. The angular geometric designs were perfect for carving into stone and stamping coins. Early Quran manuscripts used Kufic.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَنماطُ الهَندَسِيَّةُ الإِسلامِيَّةُ تَتَجَنَّبُ تَصويرَ الكائِناتِ الحَيَّة
lines.english: Islamic geometric patterns avoid depicting living beings.
lines.transliteration: al-anmaat al-handasiyya al-islamiyya tatajannab tasweer al-kaa'inaat al-hayya
lines.culturalNote: Islamic art uses geometric patterns, arabesque, and calligraphy instead of figurative art. This led to extraordinary mathematical sophistication — Islamic geometers discovered quasi-crystalline patterns 500 years before Western mathematics.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ! تَعَلَّم اللَّونَ وَالخَطَّ مَعاً
lines.english: Beautiful writing is art! Learn color and script together.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-jamiil fann! ta'allam al-lawn wal-khat ma'an

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ! أُريدُ أَن تَعرِفَ ابنَ مُقلَة
lines.english: Beautiful writing is art! I want you to know Ibn Muqla.
lines.transliteration: al-khat al-jamiil fann! uriidu an ta'rifa ibn muqla

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ مُقلَة (٨٨٦-٩٤٠م) كانَ وَزيرَ الخَليفَة — وَأَعظَمَ خَطّاطٍ في التّاريخ
lines.english: Ibn Muqla (886-940 CE) was the Caliph's vizier — and the greatest calligrapher in history.
lines.transliteration: ibn muqla (886-940m) kaana waziir al-khaliifa — wa a'dhama khattaat fis-taariikh
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Muqla served as vizier three times under different Abbasid caliphs. He invented the system of proportional measurement for Arabic letters — using the rhombic dot as the basic unit. Every letter is measured by dots relative to the alif height.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَوَّرَ نِظامَ النِّقطَة المُعَيَّنَة — وَحَدَّدَ نِسَبَ كُلِّ حَرفٍ بِدِقَّة
lines.english: He developed the rhombic dot system — precisely defining the proportions of each letter.
lines.transliteration: tawwara nidhaam an-niqta al-mu'ayyina — wa haddada nisab kull harf bi-diqqa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَطَعوا يَدَهُ بِسَبَبِ المَؤامَرات — فَكَتَبَ بِيَدِهِ الأُخرى! هَذا هُوَ الفَنّ
lines.english: They cut off his hand due to politics — so he wrote with his other hand! This is art.
lines.transliteration: qata'uu yadahu bisabab al-mu'aamaraat — fa kataba bi-yadihi al-ukhraa! haadhaa huwa al-fann

personality.catchphrase: الخَطُّ الجَميلُ فَنّ — al-khat al-jamiil fann (Beautiful writing is art)

name: Spice Seller Layla
role: Teaches food vocabulary

greeting.arabic: أَهلاً يا حَبيبي! تَعالَ شُمَّ البَهارات
greeting.english: Hello dear! Come smell the spices
greeting.transliteration: ahlan ya habiibii! ta'aala shumma al-bahaaraat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! أَنا لَيلى. أَبيعُ أَطيَبَ البَهاراتِ في السُّوق
lines.english: Welcome! I am Layla. I sell the finest spices in the market.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! ana laylaa. abii'u atyaba al-bahaaraati fis-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَبلَ أَن تَشتَري، يَجِبُ أَن تَعرِفَ أَسماءَ الطَّعام
lines.english: Before you buy, you must know the names of food.
lines.transliteration: qabla an tashtarii, yajibu an ta'rifa asmaa'a at-ta'aam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ماء — أَهَمُّ شَيءٍ في الصَّحراء
lines.english: Water -- the most important thing in the desert.
lines.transliteration: maa' — ahammu shay'in fis-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خُبز — نَأكُلُهُ كُلَّ يَوم
lines.english: Bread -- we eat it every day.
lines.transliteration: khubz — na'kuluhu kulla yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرُزّ — أَساسُ كُلِّ وَجبَة
lines.english: Rice -- the base of every meal.
lines.transliteration: aruzz — asaasu kulli wajba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا! أُريدُ أَن أَرى إِن كُنتَ حَفِظت
lines.english: Let's go! I want to see if you memorized them.
lines.transliteration: yallaa! uriidu an araa in kunta hafidhta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! اليَومَ سَنَتَعَلَّمُ عَن اللُّحوم
lines.english: You are back! Today we will learn about meats.
lines.transliteration: udta! al-yawma sanata'allamu an al-luhuuma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَحم — أَيُّ نَوعٍ مِن اللُّحوم
lines.english: Meat -- any type of meat.
lines.transliteration: lahm — ayyu naw'in min al-luhuumi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دَجاج — لَحمُ الطُّيور
lines.english: Chicken -- poultry meat.
lines.transliteration: dajaaj — lahmu at-tuyuur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمَك — مِن البَحر
lines.english: Fish -- from the sea.
lines.transliteration: samak — min al-bahr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَليب — مِن البَقَرَة
lines.english: Milk -- from the cow.
lines.transliteration: haliib — min al-baqara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا نَرى ماذا تَذكُر!
lines.english: Let us see what you remember!
lines.transliteration: hayyaa naraa maadha tadhkur!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ الله! أَنتَ تَتَعَلَّمُ مِثلَ الطَّبّاخ المَاهِر
lines.english: Mashallah! You are learning like a skilled cook.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! anta tata'allamu mithla at-tabbaakh al-maahir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَمر — حُلوُ الصَّحراء. نَأكُلُهُ مَعَ القَهوَة
lines.english: Dates -- the desert's sweet. We eat them with coffee.
lines.transliteration: tamr — hulwu as-sahraa'. na'kuluhu ma'a al-qahwa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَسَل — فيهِ شِفاء. حُلوٌ جِدّاً
lines.english: Honey -- in it there is healing. Very sweet.
lines.transliteration: 'asal — fiihi shifaa'. hulwun jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَيتون — نَأكُلُهُ وَنَستَخدِمُ زَيتَه
lines.english: Olive -- we eat it and use its oil.
lines.transliteration: zaytun — na'kuluhu wa nastakhdimu zaytah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسمِ الله! اِمتِحانٌ أَخير
lines.english: In the name of God! One final test.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! imtihaanun akhiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً! تَفَضَّل! البَهارات الأَفضَل هُنا
lines.english: Welcome! Come in! The best spices are here.
lines.transliteration: ahlan! tafaddal! al-bahaaraat al-afdal hunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَهاراتُ مُهِمَّة جِدّاً لِلطَّعام
lines.english: Spices are very important for food.
lines.transliteration: al-bahaaraatu muhimma jiddan lit-ta'aam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِنْدي فُلْفُل، كُرْكُم، زَنْجَبيل
lines.english: I have pepper, turmeric, ginger.
lines.transliteration: indii fulful, kurkum, zanjabeel

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قابِلَة جَديدَة وَصَلَت السُّوق البارِحَة!
lines.english: A new caravan arrived at the market yesterday!
lines.transliteration: qaabila jadiida wasalat as-suuq al-baariha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِنْدَهُم بَهارات مِن بِلاد بَعيدَة
lines.english: They have spices from faraway lands.
lines.transliteration: indahum bahaaraat min bilaad ba'iida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَهاراتُ تَأتي مِن طُرُق قَديمَة
lines.english: Spices come from ancient routes.
lines.transliteration: al-bahaaraatu ta'tii min turuq qadiima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التُّجّارُ يَسافِرونَ شُهوراً عَبْرَ الصَّحْراء
lines.english: Traders travel for months across the desert.
lines.transliteration: at-tujjaaru yusaafiruun shuhuran abr as-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً يا حَبيبي! تَعالَ شُمَّ البَهارات — الأَنفُ يَتَعَلَّم قَبلَ اللِّسان!
lines.english: Hello dear! Come smell the spices — the nose learns before the tongue!
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya habiibii! ta'aala shumma al-bahaaraat — al-anf yata'allam qabl al-lisaan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا الزَّعفَران — أَغلى بَهارٍ في العالَم. رائِحَتُهُ كَالذَّهَب
lines.english: This is saffron — the most expensive spice in the world. Its smell is like gold.
lines.transliteration: haadhaa az-za'faraan — aghlaa bahaar fil-'aalam. raa'ihatuhu kadh-dhahab
lines.culturalNote: The word 'saffron' comes directly from Arabic 'za'faran'. Saffron requires 75,000 flowers to make one pound of spice. Arab traders controlled the saffron trade for centuries.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَهَذا الزَّنجَبيل — يُدَفِّئُ الجِسمَ كَالشَّمسِ مِن الداخِل
lines.english: And this is ginger — it warms the body like the sun from within.
lines.transliteration: wa haadhaa az-zanjabeel — yudaffi'u al-jism kash-shams mid ad-daakhil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالقَهوَة — كَلِمَةٌ عَرَبِيَّةٌ أَصيلَة. 'قَهوَة' أَصبَحَت 'coffee' في كُلِّ العالَم!
lines.english: And coffee — a genuine Arabic word. 'Qahwa' became 'coffee' in the entire world!
lines.transliteration: wal-qahwa — kalimatun arabiyya asiila. 'qahwa' asbahat 'coffee' fii kull al-'aalam!
lines.culturalNote: The word 'coffee' comes from Arabic 'qahwa' via Turkish 'kahve'. Yemen was the first country to cultivate coffee commercially. The first coffeehouses (qahwakhana) opened in Mecca and Cairo in the 15th century.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: آهٍ! السُّكَّر! تَعالَ تَعالَ — شُمَّ هَذا!
lines.english: Ah! Sugar! Come come — smell this!
lines.transliteration: aahin! as-sukkar! ta'aala ta'aala — shumma haadhaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'sugar' مِن العَرَبِيَّة 'سُكَّر' — وَ'candy' مِن 'قَند' — سُكَّرُ القَصَب
lines.english: 'Sugar' from Arabic 'sukkar' — and 'candy' from 'qand' — sugarcane.
lines.transliteration: 'sugar' min al-arabiyya 'sukkar' — wa 'candy' min 'qand' — sukkar al-qasab
lines.culturalNote: Both 'sugar' and 'candy' are Arabic loanwords in English. Sugar (sukkar) was first refined by Persian and Arab chemists. 'Candy' comes from 'qand' (crystallized sugar). The first sugar refineries were built in the Islamic world.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ'sherbet' مِن 'شَرْبَة' — وَ'syrup' مِن 'شَراب'! لُغَتُنا مَليئَة بِالحَلاوَة!
lines.english: And 'sherbet' from 'sharba' — and 'syrup' from 'sharab'! Our language is full of sweetness!
lines.transliteration: wa 'sherbet' min 'sharba' — wa 'syrup' min 'sharaab'! lughatunaa malii'a bil-halaawa!
lines.culturalNote: Arabic sharab (drink) gave English sherbet, sorbet, and syrup. Arab pharmacists were the first to create medicinal syrups. The Arabic suffix -at in 'sharba' became the English '-et' in sherbet.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعالَ شُمَّ البَهارات وَتَعَلَّم — مَعاً هُما أَلَذُّ!
lines.english: Come smell the spices and learn — together they are sweeter!
lines.transliteration: ta'aala shumma al-bahaaraat wa ta'allam — ma'an humaa aladhdh!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً يا حَبيبي! هَذِهِ البَهاراتُ جاءَت مِن أَفريقيا الشَّرقِيَّة — زَنجِبار!
lines.english: Hello dear! These spices came from East Africa — Zanzibar!
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya habiibii! haadhihi al-bahaaraatu jaa'at min afrikiyaa ash-sharqiyya — zanjibaar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التُّجّارُ العَرَبُ وَصَلوا إلى أَفريقيا قَبلَ الأُوروبِيِّينَ بِقُرونٍ
lines.english: Arab traders reached Africa centuries before Europeans.
lines.transliteration: at-tujjaar al-arab wasalu ila afrikiyaa qabl al-urubiyyin bi-quruun
lines.culturalNote: Arab traders established trade networks from East Africa (Swahili coast) to Southeast Asia from the 8th century CE. Zanzibar and Mombasa were Arab-Swahili trading cities. Many Swahili words are Arabic in origin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القِرفَة مِن سَريلانكا! والفُلفُل مِن الهِند! والزَّعفَران مِن إيران!
lines.english: Cinnamon from Sri Lanka! Pepper from India! Saffron from Iran!
lines.transliteration: al-qirfa min sriilaankaa! wal-fulful min al-hind! waz-za'faraan min iiraan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّها تَمُرُّ عَبرَ هَذا السُّوق — رائِحَةُ كُلِّ العالَم في مَكانٍ واحِد!
lines.english: All of it passes through this market — the smell of the whole world in one place!
lines.transliteration: kulluhaa tamurru abr as-suuq — raa'ihat kull al-'aalam fii makaan waahid!

personality.catchphrase: تَفَضَّل! — tafaddal! (Come in!)

name: Trader Hassan
role: Teaches advanced trade vocabulary

greeting.arabic: تَفَضَّل يا أَخي! عِندي أَحسَنُ البَضائِع
greeting.english: Come in, my friend! I have the best goods
greeting.transliteration: tafaddal ya akhii! indii ahsanu al-badaa'i'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم! أَنا حَسَن التّاجِر. أَعمَلُ في هَذا السُّوقِ مُنذُ ثَلاثينَ سَنَة
lines.english: Peace be upon you! I am Hassan the trader. I have worked in this market for thirty years.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum! ana hasan at-taajir. a'malu fii haadha as-suuqi mundhu thalaathiina sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرى أَنَّكَ مُسافِر. في السُّوقِ يَجِبُ أَن تَعرِفَ أَسماءَ البَضائِع
lines.english: I see you are a traveler. In the market you must know the names of goods.
lines.transliteration: araa annaka musaafir. fis-suuqi yajibu an ta'rifa asmaa'a al-badaa'i'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَجّادَة — أَجمَلُ بَضائِعي. يَدَوِيَّةُ الصُّنع
lines.english: Carpet -- my most beautiful goods. Handmade.
lines.transliteration: sajjaada — ajmalu badaa'i'ii. yadawiyyatu as-sun'i

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَهار — يَجعَلُ الطَّعامَ لَذيذاً
lines.english: Spice -- makes food delicious.
lines.transliteration: bahaar — yaj'alu at-ta'aama ladhiidhan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِطر — رائِحَتُهُ جَميلَة. مِن أَحسَنِ البَضائِع
lines.english: Perfume -- it smells beautiful. Among the finest goods.
lines.transliteration: 'itr — raa'ihatuhu jamiila. min ahsani al-badaa'i'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَيِّب! هَل تَعَلَّمتَ جَيِّداً؟ لِنَرى
lines.english: Good! Have you learned well? Let us see.
lines.transliteration: tayyib! hal ta'allamta jayyidan? linara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً بِعَودَتِك يا صاحِبي! لِنُكمِل
lines.english: Welcome back my friend! Let us continue.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bi-awdatik ya saahibii! linukmil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صابون — مَصنوعٌ مِن زَيتِ الزَّيتون. مَشهورٌ جِدّاً
lines.english: Soap -- made from olive oil. Very famous.
lines.transliteration: saabun — masnuu'un min zayti az-zaytun. mashuurun jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُماش — أُبيعُ أَنواعاً كَثيرَة
lines.english: Cloth -- I sell many types.
lines.transliteration: qumaash — abii'u anwaa'an kathiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَدِيَّة — شَيءٌ تُعطيهِ لِمَن تُحِبّ
lines.english: Gift -- something you give to someone you love.
lines.transliteration: hadiyya — shay'un tu'tiiihi liman tuhibb

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا نَشوف!
lines.english: Let us see!
lines.transliteration: yallaa nashuuf!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ الله! سَتُصبِحُ تاجِراً ماهِراً
lines.english: Mashallah! You will become a skilled trader.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! satusbihu taajiran maahiran

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تاجِر — مِثلي! شَخصٌ يَبيعُ وَيَشتَري
lines.english: Merchant -- like me! A person who buys and sells.
lines.transliteration: taajir — mithlii! shakhsun yabii'u wa yashtarii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَبون — مِثلَك! الشَّخصُ الَّذي يَشتَري
lines.english: Customer -- like you! The person who buys.
lines.transliteration: zabuun — mithlak! ash-shakhsu alladhii yashtarii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دِرهَم — عُملَةُ السُّوق
lines.english: Dirham -- the market currency.
lines.transliteration: dirham — umlatu as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمتِحانٌ أَخير. أُريدُ أَن أَتَأَكَّد أَنَّكَ جاهِز لِلتِّجارَة!
lines.english: A final test. I want to make sure you are ready for trade!
lines.transliteration: imtihaanun akhiir. uriidu an ata'akkad annaka jaahiz lit-tijaara!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبا بالتّاجِر! عِنْدي صَفْقَة مُمتازَة اليَوم
lines.english: Welcome, trader! I have an excellent deal today.
lines.transliteration: marhaba bit-taajir! indii safqa mumtaaza al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التِّجارَةُ لُغَةٌ خاصَّة
lines.english: Trade has its own special language.
lines.transliteration: at-tijaara lugha khaassa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَفْقَة — يَعني اتِّفاق لِلبَيْع
lines.english: Safqa — means a deal for selling.
lines.transliteration: safqa — ya'nii ittifaaq lil-bay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ العاصِفَة الرَّمْلِيَّة انْتَهَت
lines.english: I heard the sandstorm has ended.
lines.transliteration: sami'tu anna al-aasifa ar-ramliyya intahat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطُّرُقُ آمِنَة الآن لِلتِّجارَة
lines.english: The roads are safe now for trade.
lines.transliteration: at-turuqu aamina al-aan lit-tijaara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ تاجِرٌ مَوثوق. لَدَيَّ مَهَمَّة لَكَ
lines.english: You are a trusted trader. I have a quest for you.
lines.transliteration: anta taajir mawthuu تق. ladayya mahamma lak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوْصِل هَذِهِ البَضائِع لِلتّاجِرَة فاطِمَة
lines.english: Deliver these goods to trader Fatima.
lines.transliteration: awsil haadhihi al-badaa'i' lit-taajira faatima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَفَضَّل يا أَخي! صَفْقَة مُمتازَة! اليَوم سَأُريكَ أَسرارَ التِّجارَة عَبرَ الصَّحراء
lines.english: Come in my friend! Excellent deal! Today I will show you the secrets of desert trade.
lines.transliteration: tafaddal ya akhii! safqa mumtaaza! al-yawm sa-uriika asraar at-tijaara abr as-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَافِلَة — مَجموعَةُ التُّجَّار تَسيرُ مَعاً. الأَمانُ في الجَماعَة!
lines.english: The caravan — a group of traders traveling together. Safety in numbers!
lines.transliteration: al-qaafila — majmuu'at at-tujjaar tasiiru ma'an. al-amaan fil-jamaa'a!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخانُ — فُندُقُ التّاجِر في الصَّحراء. بَعدَ أُسبوعِ سَفَر تَجِدُهُ كَالجَنَّة!
lines.english: The khan — the trader's hotel in the desert. After a week of travel you find it like paradise!
lines.transliteration: al-khaan — funduq at-taajir fis-sahraa'. ba'da usbu' safar tajidahu kal-janna!
lines.culturalNote: Caravanserais (khan/funduq) were rest stops built every 25-30 km along trade routes — roughly one day's caravan travel. They provided free accommodation, water, and fodder. The largest could house 300 merchants.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَةُ 'check' في المَصارِف — مِن العَرَبِيَّة 'صَكّ' — وَثيقَةُ الدَّفع
lines.english: And the word 'check' in banking — from Arabic 'sakk' — a payment document.
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat 'check' fil-masaarif — min al-arabiyya 'sakk' — wathiiqat ad-daf'
lines.culturalNote: The word 'check' (bank check) comes from Arabic 'sakk' — a written payment order. Arab merchants invented the sakk system to avoid carrying gold across dangerous trade routes. This was the world's first banking instrument.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ'risk' مِن 'رِزق' — الرِّزقُ هُوَ ما قَسَمَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الخَيرات
lines.english: And 'risk' from 'rizq' — rizq is what God has apportioned of good things.
lines.transliteration: wa 'risk' min 'rizq' — ar-rizq huwa maa qasamahu allaah min al-khayrat
lines.culturalNote: The English word 'risk' may derive from Arabic 'rizq' (livelihood, fortune) through Italian 'risco'. Arab traders used the concept of divine provision alongside calculated risk-taking.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَفْقَة مُمتازَة! ثَلاثون عاماً في التِّجارَة — سافَرتُ مِنَ الأَندَلُس إلى الصّين
lines.english: Excellent deal! Thirty years in trade — I traveled from Andalusia to China.
lines.transliteration: safqa mumtaaza! thalaathuun aaman fit-tijaara — saafartu min al-andalus ilaa as-siin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في الأَندَلُس — اِسبانيا الإِسلامِيَّة — رَأَيتُ أَجمَلَ بُيوتٍ في العالَم
lines.english: In Andalusia — Islamic Spain — I saw the most beautiful houses in the world.
lines.transliteration: fil-andalus — isbaaniyaa al-islamiyya — ra'aytu ajmal buyuut fil-'aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَفي الصّين — ما شاء اللَّه — المَدائِنُ كَالجِبال! وَالبُوصَلَةُ العَجيبَة التي تُشيرُ دائِماً للشَّمال
lines.english: And in China — mashallah — cities like mountains! And the amazing compass that always points north!
lines.transliteration: wa fis-siin — maa shaa'allaah — al-madaa'in kal-jibaal! wal-buusala al-ajiiba allati tushiiru daa'iman lish-shamaal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التُّجارُ العَرَبُ أَخَذوا البُوصَلَةَ مِن الصّين وَنَشَروها في العالَم — صَفْقَة مُمتازَة للبَشَرِيَّة!
lines.english: Arab traders took the compass from China and spread it to the world — an excellent deal for humanity!
lines.transliteration: at-tujjaar al-arab akhadhu al-buusala min as-siin wa nasharu-ha fil-'aalam — safqa mumtaaza lil-bashariyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَفْقَة مُمتازَة! اليَوم أُريدُ أَن أُخبِرَكَ عَن نِقابَةِ التُّجَّار
lines.english: Excellent deal! Today I want to tell you about the merchants' guild.
lines.transliteration: safqa mumtaaza! al-yawm uriidu an ukhbiraka an niqaabat at-tujjaar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نِقابَةُ التُّجَّار — تَنظيمٌ يَحمي التّاجِرَ مِنَ الغِشِّ وَيَضمَنُ جَودَةَ البَضائِع
lines.english: The merchants' guild — an organization protecting traders from fraud and guaranteeing goods quality.
lines.transliteration: niqaabat at-tujjaar — tandhiim yahmii at-taajir min al-ghish wa yadmanu jawdat al-badaa'i'
lines.culturalNote: Islamic trade guilds (asnaf) developed in the 9th century, centuries before European guilds. They had standardized weights, quality controls, and dispute resolution. The hisba (market inspector) enforced fair trading.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُحتَسِبُ — مُفَتِّشُ السُّوق — يَمشي كُلَّ يَوم وَيَتَحَقَّقُ مِن المَوازين
lines.english: The muhtasib — the market inspector — walks every day and checks the scales.
lines.transliteration: al-muhtasib — mufaatish as-suuq — yamshi kull yawm wa yatahaqqa min al-mawaaziin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التّاجِرُ الصّادِقُ يَنجَحُ دائِماً — البَرَكَةُ في الصِّدق! صَفْقَة مُمتازَة يا أَخي!
lines.english: The honest trader always succeeds — blessing is in honesty! Excellent deal my friend!
lines.transliteration: at-taajir as-saadiq yanjahu daa'iman — al-baraka fis-sidq! safqa mumtaaza ya akhii!

personality.catchphrase: صَفْقَة مُمتازَة! — safqa mumtaaza! (Excellent deal!)

name: Guard Hamza
role: Teaches numbers 11-15 and market phrases

greeting.arabic: قِف! مَن أَنت؟ ... أَهلاً، تَفَضَّل
greeting.english: Halt! Who are you? ... Welcome, come in
greeting.transliteration: qif! man anta? ... ahlan, tafaddal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم. أَنا حَمزَة، حارِسُ هَذا السُّوق
lines.english: Peace be upon you. I am Hamza, guard of this market.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum. ana hamza, haarisu haadha as-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُهِمَّتي حِراسَةُ السُّوق. لَكِنَّني أُحِبُّ الأَعدادَ أَيضاً
lines.english: My job is guarding the market. But I also love numbers.
lines.transliteration: muhimmatii hiraasatu as-suuq. laakinnanii uhibbu al-a'daada aydan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِفُ الأَعدادَ بَعدَ العَشَرَة؟ لِنَبدَأ!
lines.english: Do you know the numbers after ten? Let us begin!
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rifu al-a'daada ba'da al-'ashara? linabda'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ — عَدَدُ اللّاعِبينَ في الفَريق
lines.english: Eleven -- the number of players on a team.
lines.transliteration: ahada 'ashara — adadu al-laa'ibiina fil-fariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِثنا عَشَرَ — عَدَدُ الأَشهُرِ في السَّنَة
lines.english: Twelve -- the number of months in a year.
lines.transliteration: ithnaa 'ashara — adadu al-ashhuri fis-sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَةَ عَشَرَ — رَقَمٌ قَوِيّ!
lines.english: Thirteen -- a powerful number!
lines.transliteration: thalaathata 'ashara — raqamun qawii!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُريدُ أَن أَرى قُوَّتَك في الأَعداد!
lines.english: I want to see your strength with numbers!
lines.transliteration: uriidu an araa quwwatak fil-a'daad!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً. أَنتَ عُدتَ. جَيِّد. لِنُكمِل
lines.english: Hello. You are back. Good. Let us continue.
lines.transliteration: ahlan. anta udta. jayyid. linukmil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَعَةَ عَشَرَ — عُمري عِندَما بَدَأتُ الحِراسَة
lines.english: Fourteen -- my age when I started guarding.
lines.transliteration: arba'ata 'ashara — umrii indamaa bada'tu al-hiraasa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خَمسَةَ عَشَرَ — عَدَدُ الحُرّاسِ في السُّوق
lines.english: Fifteen -- the number of guards in the market.
lines.transliteration: khamsata 'ashara — adadu al-hurraasi fis-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِكَم — سُؤالٌ مُهِمّ في السُّوق. يَعني 'ما السِّعر؟'
lines.english: How much -- an important question in the market. It means 'what is the price?'
lines.transliteration: bi-kam — su'aalun muhimm fis-suuq. ya'nii 'ma as-si'r?'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا نَختَبِر ذاكِرَتَك
lines.english: Let us test your memory.
lines.transliteration: hayyaa nakhtabir dhakirataka

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت. الآن سَأُعَلِّمُكَ عِباراتٍ تَحتاجُها في السُّوق
lines.english: Well done. Now I will teach you phrases you need in the market.
lines.transliteration: ahsant. al-aan sa-u'allimuka ibaaraatin tahtaajuhaa fis-suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُريدُ — عِندَما تُريدُ شَيئاً مِنَ التّاجِر
lines.english: I want -- when you want something from the trader.
lines.transliteration: uriidu — indamaa turiidu shay'an min at-taajir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا أُريدُ — عِندَما لا تُريدُ شَيئاً. مُهِمَّة لِلمُساوَمَة
lines.english: I don't want -- when you don't want something. Important for bargaining.
lines.transliteration: laa uriidu — indamaa laa turiidu shay'an. muhimma lil-musaawama

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن فَضلِك — كَلِمَةُ الأَدَب. قُلها دائِماً
lines.english: Please -- a word of politeness. Always say it.
lines.transliteration: min fadlak — kalimatu al-adab. qulhaa daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمتِحانٌ أَخير. كُن قَوِيّاً!
lines.english: A final test. Be strong!
lines.transliteration: imtihaanun akhiir. kun qawiyyan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: Halt! What do you want?
lines.transliteration: qif! maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَحْمي الواحَة
lines.english: I protect the oasis.
lines.transliteration: ana ahmii al-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا أَحَد يَدْخُل بِدونِ إِذْن
lines.english: No one enters without permission.
lines.transliteration: laa ahad yadkhul bidooni idhn

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْتاجُ مُساعِد لِلدَّوْرِيَّة
lines.english: I need an assistant for the patrol.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju musaa'id lid-dawriyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُم بِدَوْرِيَّة حَوْلَ الواحَة
lines.english: Do a patrol around the oasis.
lines.transliteration: qum bi-dawriyya hawl al-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَأَيْتُ أَشياء غَريبَة في الصَّحْراء
lines.english: I have seen strange things in the desert.
lines.transliteration: ra'aytu ashyaa' ghariiba fis-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَصْوات... أَضْواء... لا أَعْرِف
lines.english: Sounds... lights... I don't know.
lines.transliteration: aswaat... adwaa'... laa a'rif

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! أَنتَ عُدتَ. جَيِّد. الجُندِيُّ الجَيِّدُ يَعودُ دائِماً
lines.english: Halt! You returned. Good. A good soldier always returns.
lines.transliteration: qif! anta udta. jayyid. al-jundiyyu al-jayyid ya'uudu daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُعَلِّمُك كَلِمات المُحارِب. السَّيف — أَهَمُّ سِلاح
lines.english: I'll teach you warrior words. The sword — the most important weapon.
lines.transliteration: u'allimuk kalimaat al-muharib. as-sayf — ahamm silaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَوس وَالسَّهم — لِلمَسافَة البَعيدَة. الصَّبر — لِلمَسافَة الأَبعَد
lines.english: Bow and arrow — for long distance. Patience — for the longest distance.
lines.transliteration: al-qaws was-sahm — lil-masaafa al-ba'iida. as-sabr — lil-masaafa al-ab'ad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: 'admiral' — كَلِمَة إنجليزيَّة مِن 'أَميرُ البَحر'. العَرَبُ كانوا أَسيادَ البَحر
lines.english: 'Admiral' — an English word from 'amir al-bahr'. Arabs were masters of the sea.
lines.transliteration: 'admiral' — kalima injiliziyya min 'amir al-bahr'. al-arab kaanu asiyaad al-bahr
lines.culturalNote: The word 'admiral' comes from Arabic 'amir al-bahr' (commander of the sea). Arab naval power reached its peak under the Fatimid and later the Ottoman Empire. The Mediterranean was an Arab sea for centuries.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَلاحُ الدِّين الأَيُّوبي — مِن أَعظَم القادَة. تَعَلَّمَ مِنَ الأَعداءِ وَانتَصَرَ
lines.english: Saladin — one of the greatest commanders. He learned from enemies and prevailed.
lines.transliteration: salaah ad-diin al-ayyuubii — min a'dham al-qaada. ta'allama min al-a'daa' wa intasar
lines.culturalNote: Saladin (Salah ad-Din, 1137-1193 CE) recaptured Jerusalem in 1187. He was renowned for his chivalry — he allowed Christian civilians to leave safely. Even his enemies, like Richard I, respected him.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عائِلَتي... أَنا أَعملُ بَعيداً. لَكِنَّهُم في قَلبي دائِماً
lines.english: My family... I work far away. But they are always in my heart.
lines.transliteration: aa'ilatii... ana a'mal ba'iidan. laakinnnahum fii qalbii daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابني... هُوَ في الثّامِنَة مِن عُمرِهِ. يُريدُ أَن يَكونَ حارِساً مِثلي
lines.english: My son... he is eight years old. He wants to be a guard like me.
lines.transliteration: ibnii... huwa fith-thaaminati min umurihi. yuriidu an yakuuna haarisan mithlii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُلتُ لَهُ: أَوَّلاً تَعَلَّم! ثُمَّ اخدُم. الجُنديُّ الجاهِلُ خَطَر
lines.english: I told him: first learn! Then serve. An ignorant soldier is a danger.
lines.transliteration: qultu lahu: awwalan ta'allam! thumma ukhdum. al-jundiyyu al-jaahil khatar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا لِماذا أُعَلِّمُك الأَعداد — حَتّى لا تُخطِئَ في الحِساب يَوماً
lines.english: This is why I teach you numbers — so you don't make arithmetic errors someday.
