lines.english: Come! Let me show you something beautiful. This fabric carries the secret of Islamic civilization.
lines.transliteration: Ta'aal! Uriika shay'an jamiilan. Haadhihi al-qumaasha jaa'at min sirr al-hadaara al-islaamiyya.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "muslin" الإِنجليزِيَّة؟ مِن مَوصِل بِالعِراق! وَ"damask"؟ مِن دِمَشق!
lines.english: The English word "muslin"? From Mosul, Iraq! And "damask"? From Damascus!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'muslin' al-injliiziyya? Min Mawsil bil-'Iraq! Wa 'damask'? Min Dimashq!
lines.culturalNote: "Muslin" comes from Mosul, Iraq, where this fine cotton fabric was perfected. "Damask" comes from Damascus, Syria. "Gauze" comes from Gaza, Palestine. Three English fabric words, three Arab cities.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"gauze"؟ مِن غَزَّة! ثَلاثُ مُدُن عَرَبِيَّة في ثَلاثِ كَلِمَات إِنجليزِيَّة!
lines.english: And "gauze"? From Gaza! Three Arab cities in three English words!
lines.transliteration: Wa 'gauze'? Min Ghazza! Thalaathu mudun 'arabiyya fii thalaathi kalimaat injliiziyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الثَّوب — لِأَنَّ كُلَّ ثَوب يَحكِي قِصَّة حَضَارَة!
lines.english: Learn: the thobe — because every garment tells the story of a civilization!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: ath-thawb — li-anna kull thawb yahkii qissat hadaara!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِكُلِّ سُرور! الحِجَاب — يَحمِي مِن الشَّمس والرِّيح ويُزَيِّن في آنٍ وَاحِد.
lines.english: With pleasure! The hijab — it protects from sun and wind while also adorning.
lines.transliteration: Bi-kulli suruur! Al-hijaab — yahmii min ash-shams war-riyaah wa yuzayyin fii aanin waahid.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالقَميص — أَبسَطُ قِطعَة في المَلبَس وَأَكثَرُها فَائِدَة!
lines.english: And the shirt — the simplest garment and the most useful!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-qamiis — absatu qit'a fil-malbas wa aktharuhaa faa'ida!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالحِذَاء! بِدُون حِذَاء لا تَستَطيع السَّفَر. الحِذَاء أَوَّل وَرِيث الإِنسَان!
lines.english: And shoes! Without shoes you cannot travel. Shoes are humanity's first inheritance!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-hidhaa'! Bi-duun hidhaa' laa tastatiiu as-safar. Al-hidhaa' awwal warith al-insaan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَختَبِر ما تَعَلَّمتَ! المَلابِس كَالكَلِمَات — لازِمَة كُلَّ يَوم.
lines.english: Let's test what you learned! Clothing is like words — needed every day.
lines.transliteration: Li-nakhtabir maa ta'allamta! Al-malaabis kal-kalimaat — laazima kull yawm.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! تَعلَّمتَ مَلابِسَ خَمسَة. عُد إِليَّ وَسَأُعَلِّمُكَ المَزيد!
lines.english: Excellent! You learned five clothing items. Come back and I will teach you more!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Ta'allamta malaabisa khamsa. 'Ud ilayya wa sa-u'allimuka al-maziid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنسُج سِجَّادَة لِبَيتِ تَاجِر ثَرِيٍّ. انظُر — كُلُّ خَيطٍ في مَكانِه الصَّحيح.
lines.english: I am weaving a carpet for a wealthy merchant's home. See — every thread in its right place.
lines.transliteration: Ansuj sijjaada li-bayt taajir thariyy. Unzur — kullu khaytin fii makaanhi as-sahiih.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النَّسيج مِثلُ اللُّغَة — كُلُّ كَلِمَة خَيطٌ، وَالجُملَة سِجَّادَة!
lines.english: Weaving is like language — every word is a thread, and the sentence is a carpet!
lines.transliteration: An-nasiij mithlu al-lugha — kullu kalima khaytin, wa al-jumla sijjaada!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذَا اللَّون الأَحمَر؟ مِن الزَّعفَران. تَعَلَّم: الأَحمَر!
lines.english: This red color? From saffron. Learn: red!
lines.transliteration: Haadha al-lawn al-ahmar? Min az-za'faraan. Ta'allam: al-ahmar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالأَزرَق مِن النِّيلَة. وَالأَخضَر مِن أَعشَاب الجَبَل. الطَّبيعَة لَوحَتُنا!
lines.english: And blue from indigo. And green from mountain herbs. Nature is our palette!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-azraq min an-niila. Wa al-akhdar min a'shaab al-jabal. At-tabii'a lawhatunaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَتَعرِف أَنَّ النَّسيجَ يُعَلِّمُنَا عَن الحَيَاة؟ كُلُّ خَيطٍ يَمُرُّ فَوق وَتَحت.
lines.english: Do you know that weaving teaches us about life? Every thread goes over and under.
lines.transliteration: Ata'rif anna an-nasiij yu'allimunaa 'an al-hayaah? Kullu khaytin yamurr fawqa wa tahta.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصَّبر — هَذَا سِرُّ النَّسَّاج الجَيِّد. أَلفُ خَيطٍ في يَومٍ وَاحِد!
lines.english: Patience — that is the good weaver's secret. A thousand threads in one day!
lines.transliteration: As-sabr — haadha sirr an-nassaaj al-jayyid. Alfu khaytin fii yawmin waahid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: القُماش — لِأَنَّ الحَضَارَة الإِسلَامِيَّة بَنَت طُرُق التِّجَارَة على القُماش!
lines.english: Learn: cloth — because Islamic civilization built trade routes on cloth!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-qumaash — li-anna al-hadaara al-islaamiyya banat turuq at-tijaara 'alaa al-qumaash!
lines.culturalNote: The Islamic world dominated textile production and trade from 700-1400 CE. Words like "cotton" (from Arabic "qutn" قُطن), "satin" (from Zaytun/Quanzhou, China), and "taffeta" (from Persian) entered European languages through Arab trade.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالحِزام — يَربِط كُلَّ شَيء مَعاً. مِثلَ الصَّداقَة تَماماً!
lines.english: And the belt — it holds everything together. Exactly like friendship!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-hizaam — yarbut kull shay' ma'an. Mithla as-sadaaqa tamaaман!

personality.catchphrase: الجَمالُ في التَّفاصيل — al-jamaal fit-tafaasiil (Beauty is in the details)

name: Healer Khadija
role: Teaches adjectives for describing conditions

greeting.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم يا بُنَيّ. كَيفَ حالُك؟
greeting.english: Peace be upon you, dear child. How are you?
greeting.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum ya bunayy. kayfa haaluk?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا خَديجَة. أُعالِجُ النّاس بِالأَعشاب مُنذُ سَنَوات طَويلَة
lines.english: I am Khadija. I have been treating people with herbs for many long years.
lines.transliteration: ana khadiija. u'aaliju an-naas bil-a'shaab mundhu sanawaat tawiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِكَي تَفهَم الطِّبّ، يَجِب أَن تَعرِف الصِّفات
lines.english: To understand medicine, you must know adjectives.
lines.transliteration: likay tafham at-tibb, yajib an ta'rif as-sifaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِندَما يَأتي مَريض، أَسأَلُهُ عَن حالِه. لِنَبدَأ
lines.english: When a patient comes, I ask about their condition. Let's begin.
lines.transliteration: indamaa ya'tii mariid, as'aluhu an haalihi. linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَظِيفٌ — الجُرح يَجِب أَن يَكون نَظيفاً
lines.english: Clean — the wound must be clean.
lines.transliteration: naziifun — al-jurh yajib an yakuuna naziifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَسِخٌ — إِذا كانَ وَسِخاً، يُصبِح أَسوَأ
lines.english: Dirty — if it is dirty, it gets worse.
lines.transliteration: wasikhun — idhaa kaana wasikhan, yusbihu aswa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَوِيٌّ — الجِسم القَوِيّ يُشفى بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Strong — a strong body heals quickly.
lines.transliteration: qawiyyun — al-jism al-qawiyy yushfaa bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَيِّد. هَل فَهِمتَ هَذِهِ الصِّفات؟
lines.english: Good. Did you understand these adjectives?
lines.transliteration: jayyid. hal fahimta haadhihi as-sifaat?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا بُنَيّ. لِنُكمِل دَرسَنا في الصِّفات
lines.english: Welcome, dear child. Let's continue our lesson in adjectives.
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya bunayy. linukmil darsanaa fis-sifaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ضَعِيفٌ — عَكس قَوِيّ. المَريض يَكون ضَعيفاً
lines.english: Weak — the opposite of strong. The sick person is weak.
lines.transliteration: da'iifun — aks qawiyy. al-mariid yakuun da'iifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَوِيلٌ — الشَّجَرَة طَويلَة فيها أَعشاب مُفيدَة
lines.english: Tall/Long — the tall tree has useful herbs.
lines.transliteration: tawiilun — ash-shajara tawiila fiihaa a'shaab mufiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَصِيرٌ — الأَعشاب القَصيرَة قَريبَة مِن الأَرض
lines.english: Short — the short herbs are close to the ground.
lines.transliteration: qasiirun — al-a'shaab al-qasiira qariiba min al-ard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَبِيحٌ — بَعض الأَدوِيَة طَعمُها قَبيح لَكِنَّها مُفيدَة
lines.english: Ugly/Unpleasant — some medicines taste bad but they are useful.
lines.transliteration: qabiihun — ba'd al-adwiya ta'muhaa qabiih laakinnaha mufiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَع صِفات جَديدَة. لِنَرى ماذا تَذكُر
lines.english: Four new adjectives. Let's see what you remember.
lines.transliteration: arba' sifaat jadiida. linaraa maadha tadhkur

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ تَتَقَدَّم. اليَوم نَتَعَلَّم شَيئاً مُختَلِفاً
lines.english: You are progressing. Today we learn something different.
lines.transliteration: anta tataqaddam. al-yawm nata'allam shay'an mukhtalifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَوَارِب — تَحمي القَدَمَين مِن البَرد
lines.english: Socks — protect the feet from the cold.
lines.transliteration: jawaarib — tahmii al-qadamayn min al-bard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَظَّارَات — تُساعِد العُيون الضَّعيفَة
lines.english: Glasses — help weak eyes.
lines.transliteration: nazzaaraat — tusaa'id al-uyuun ad-da'iifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَعِيدٌ — الإِنسان السَّعيد يَشفى أَسرَع
lines.english: Happy — a happy person heals faster.
lines.transliteration: sa'iidun — al-insaan as-sa'iid yashfaa asra'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! هَيّا نَختَبِر كُلّ ما تَعَلَّمتَ
lines.english: Excellent! Let's test everything you learned.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! hayyaa nakhtabir kulla maa ta'allamta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَعشاب هِيَ دَواء الطَّبيعَة. كُلّ عُشبَة لَها فائِدَة
lines.english: Herbs are nature's medicine. Every herb has a benefit.
lines.transliteration: al-a'shaab hiya dawaa' at-tabii'a. kullu ushba lahaa faa'ida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِن أَوَّلاً يَجِب أَن تَعرِف الصِّفات لِتَصِف الأَعراض
lines.english: But first you must know adjectives to describe symptoms.
lines.transliteration: laakin awwalan yajib an ta'rif as-sifaat litasif al-a'raad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً يا بُنَيّ. بِالشِّفاء إِن شاء الله
lines.english: Hello, dear child. May healing come, God willing.
lines.transliteration: ahlan ya bunayy. bish-shifaa' in shaa' allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيفَ أُساعِدُك اليَوم؟
lines.english: How can I help you today?
lines.transliteration: kayfa usaa'iduk al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجِسمُ أَمانَة. لِنَتَعَلَّم أَجزاءَهُ
lines.english: The body is a trust. Let us learn its parts.
lines.transliteration: al-jismu amaana. linata'allam ajzaa'ahu

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَأْسٌ — يَحمِلُ العَقل
lines.english: Head — it carries the mind.
lines.transliteration: ra'sun — yahmilu al-'aql

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَدٌ — بِها نَلمِسُ وَنُشفي
lines.english: Hand — with it we touch and heal.
lines.transliteration: yadun — bihaa nalmisu wa nushfii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَيْنٌ — تَرى الدَّواء وَالمَرَض
lines.english: Eye — it sees medicine and illness.
lines.transliteration: 'aynun — taraa ad-dawaa' wal-marad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنت! تَعَلَّمتَ ثَلاثَ كَلِمات
lines.english: Well done! You learned three words.
lines.transliteration: ahsant! ta'allamta thalaath kalimaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطِّبُّ العَرَبِيّ قَديم جِدّاً
lines.english: Arab medicine is very ancient.
lines.transliteration: at-tibbu al-'arabiyy qadiim jiddan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَجدادُنا اِستَخدَموا النَّعناع لِلمَعِدَة وَالبابونَج لِلنَّوم
lines.english: Our ancestors used mint for the stomach and chamomile for sleep.
lines.transliteration: ajdaadunaa istakhdamuu an-na'naa' lil-ma'ida wal-baabunaj lin-nawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ عُشبَة فيها حِكمَة مِن الله
lines.english: Every herb contains wisdom from God.
lines.transliteration: kullu 'ushba fiihaa hikma min allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَنا أُحاوِل أَن أُعَلِّم هَذِهِ الحِكمَة لِلجيل الجَديد
lines.english: And I try to teach this wisdom to the new generation.
lines.transliteration: wa ana uhaawilu an u'allima haadhihi al-hikma lil-jiil al-jadiid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل سَمِعت؟ الحَدّاد داوود يَشكو مِن ظَهرِه
lines.english: Have you heard? Blacksmith Daud complains about his back.
lines.transliteration: hal sami't? al-haddaad daawuud yashkuu min zahrihi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُلتُ لَهُ: اِشرَب شاي الزَّنجَبيل كُلّ صَباح
lines.english: I told him: drink ginger tea every morning.
lines.transliteration: qultu lahu: ishrab shaay az-zanjabiil kulla sabaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالأَميرَة عائِشَة طَلَبَت مِنّي أَعشاباً لِلنَّوم
lines.english: And Princess Aisha asked me for herbs for sleep.
lines.transliteration: wal-amiira 'aa'isha talabat minnii a'shaaban lin-nawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ سينا كَتَبَ القانونَ في الطِّبّ — أَعظَمُ كِتابٍ طِبّي
lines.english: Ibn Sina wrote the Canon of Medicine — the greatest medical text
lines.transliteration: ibn sina kataba al-qanun fit-tibb — a'zam kitab tibbi
lines.culturalNote: Ibn Sina's (Avicenna, 980-1037 CE) Canon of Medicine was used as a textbook in European universities until the 17th century — over 600 years.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البيمارِستان — المُستَشفى — اختِراعٌ عَرَبي
lines.english: The bimaristan — the hospital — is an Arab invention
lines.transliteration: al-bimaristan — al-mustashfa — ikhtira' arabi
lines.culturalNote: The first hospitals (bimaristans) were established in Baghdad in the 9th century. They were free, treated all patients regardless of religion, and had separate wards for different conditions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرّازي فَرَّقَ بَينَ الحَصبَة وَالجُدَري أَوَّلَ مَرَّة
lines.english: Al-Razi distinguished between measles and smallpox for the first time
lines.transliteration: ar-razi farraqa bayna al-hasba wal-judari awwal marra

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَلَس، أُرِيدُ أَن أُحَدِّثَكَ عَن عَظِيم مِن أَطِبَّاء الإِسلَام: ابن النَّفيس.
lines.english: Sit, I want to tell you about a great Muslim physician: Ibn al-Nafis.
lines.transliteration: Jalis, uriiду an uhaddithak 'an 'aziim min atibba' al-islaam: Ibn an-Nafis.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في القَرنِ الثَّالِثَ عَشَر، اِكتَشَفَ ابن النَّفيس الدَّورَة الرِّئَوِيَّة — قَبلَ هَارفَي بِثَلاثِمِائَة سَنَة!
lines.english: In the 13th century, Ibn al-Nafis discovered pulmonary circulation — 300 years before Harvey!
lines.transliteration: Fil-qarn ath-thaalith 'ashar, iktashafa Ibn an-Nafis ad-dawra ar-ri'awiyya — qabla Harvey bi-thalathimi'at sana!
lines.culturalNote: Ibn al-Nafis (1213-1288 CE) discovered that blood flows through the lungs (pulmonary circulation), not through the heart septum as Galen claimed. This was rediscovered in Europe by William Harvey in 1628 — 300 years later.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَال: الدَّم يَمُرُّ عَبرَ الرِّئَة لا عَبرَ القَلب مُبَاشَرَةً. كَانَ مُحِقاً تَماماً!
lines.english: He said: blood passes through the lungs, not directly through the heart. He was completely right!
lines.transliteration: Qaala: ad-dam yamurr 'abra ar-ri'a laa 'abra al-qalb mubaasharatan. Kaana muhiqqqan tamааman!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: القَلب — هُوَ مَركَز الحَيَاة. اِعتَنِ بِقَلبِك دَائِماً!
lines.english: Learn: the heart — it is the center of life. Always take care of your heart!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-qalb — huwa markaz al-hayaah. I'tani bi-qalbik daa'iman!

choices.english: What do you know about Arabic medicine?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِكُلِّ سُرور! الجِسم هُوَ أَعظَم كِتَاب. لِنَبدَأ مِن الرَّأس.
lines.english: With pleasure! The body is the greatest book. Let us begin from the head.
lines.transliteration: Bi-kulli suruur! Al-jism huwa a'zam kitaab. Li-nabda' min ar-ra's.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرَّأس — مَقَرُّ العَقل. العَقل هُوَ أَغلى ما تَملِك!
lines.english: The head — dwelling of the mind. The mind is the most precious thing you own!
lines.transliteration: Ar-ra's — maqarr al-'aql. Al-'aql huwa aghlaa maa tamlik!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَين — بِها تَرى جَمَال العَالَم. اِحفَظها بِالنَّوم الكَافي!
lines.english: The eye — with it you see the beauty of the world. Guard it with sufficient sleep!
lines.transliteration: Al-'ayn — bihaa taraa jamaal al-'aalam. Ihfazhaa bin-nawm al-kaafi!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأُذُن — بِها تَسمَع. وَالطَّبيب يَسمَع دَائِماً قَبلَ أَن يَتَكَلَّم!
lines.english: The ear — with it you hear. And a physician always listens before speaking!
lines.transliteration: Al-udhun — bihaa tasma'. Wa at-tabiib yasma' daa'iman qabla an yatakallam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! الجِسم هُوَ أَمَانَة الله عِندَكَ — اِعتَنِ بِه كَمَا تَعتَني بِحَديقَتِك.
lines.english: Well done! The body is God's trust with you — tend to it as you tend your garden.
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Al-jism huwa amaana Allaah 'indak — i'tani bihi kamaa ta'tani bi-hadiigatik.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطِّبُّ العَرَبي! ابن سِينا كَتَبَ "القَانون في الطِّبّ" — المَرجِع الطِّبِّيّ في أُوروبَّا لِسِتِّمِائَة سَنَة!
lines.english: Arabic medicine! Ibn Sina wrote "The Canon of Medicine" — the medical reference in Europe for 600 years!
lines.transliteration: At-tibb al-'arabi! Ibn Sina kataba 'Al-Qaanuun fit-Tibb' — al-marja' at-tibbiyy fii Uurubba li-sittimi'at sana!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "syrup" الإِنجليزِيَّة مِن العَرَبِيَّة "شَرَاب" — الدَّواء الحُلو!
lines.english: The English word "syrup" comes from Arabic "sharaab" — the sweet medicine!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'syrup' al-injliiziyya min al-'arabiyya 'sharaab' — ad-dawaa' al-hulw!
lines.culturalNote: "Syrup" comes from Arabic "sharaab" (شَرَاب, drink/potion). "Camphor" comes from Arabic "kafuur" (كَافور). "Alcohol" comes from Arabic "al-kuhl" (الكُحل, the kohl/essence). Arab pharmacists invented distillation and modern drug preparation.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "camphor" مِن "كَافور". الأَطِبَّاء العَرَب أَعطَوا العَالَم ثَمَانِيَة أَعشَار عِلم الصَّيدَلَة!
lines.english: And "camphor" from "kafuur." Arab physicians gave the world eight-tenths of pharmacy!
lines.transliteration: Wa kalima 'camphor' min 'kaafuur'. Al-atibba' al-'Arab a'taw al-'aalam thamaaniyat a'shaarin 'ilm as-saydala!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الفَم — بِه تَأكُل وَتَتَكَلَّم. اِحفَظه بِالسِّواك!
lines.english: Learn: the mouth — with it you eat and speak. Guard it with siwak!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-fam — bihi ta'kul wa tatakallam. Ihfazh bis-siwaak!

personality.catchphrase: بِالشِّفاء إِن شاء الله — bish-shifaa' in shaa' allaah (May you be healed, God willing)

name: Captain Rashid
role: Teaches directions and navigation

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً يا بَحّار! هَل أَنتَ مُستَعِدّ لِلبَحر؟
greeting.english: Welcome, sailor! Are you ready for the sea?
greeting.transliteration: ahlan ya bahhaar! hal anta musta'idd lil-bahr?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا القُبطان رَشيد! أُبحِرُ في هَذا البَحر مُنذُ عِشرين سَنَة
lines.english: I am Captain Rashid! I've sailed this sea for twenty years.
lines.transliteration: ana al-qubtaan rashiid! ubhiru fii haadha al-bahr mundhu ishriina sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَحّار الحَقيقِيّ يَعرِف الاِتِّجاهات. بِدون ذَلِك تَضيع
lines.english: A true sailor knows directions. Without that, you get lost.
lines.transliteration: al-bahhaar al-haqiiqiyy ya'rif al-ittijaahaat. biduun dhaalik tadii'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِسمَع جَيِّداً! هَذِهِ أَهَمّ الاِتِّجاهات
lines.english: Listen well! These are the most important directions.
lines.transliteration: isma' jayyidan! haadhihi ahamm al-ittijaahaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَمَال — حَيثُ يُشيرُ نَجم القُطب
lines.english: North — where the North Star points.
lines.transliteration: shamaal — haythu yushiiru najm al-qutb

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَنُوب — عَكس الشَّمال، حَيثُ المِياه الدّافِئَة
lines.english: South — opposite of north, where the warm waters are.
lines.transliteration: januub — aks ash-shamaal, haythu al-miyaah ad-daafi'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَرْق — حَيثُ تَطلُع الشَّمس
lines.english: East — where the sun rises.
lines.transliteration: sharq — haythu tatlu' ash-shams

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاث اِتِّجاهات. هَل تَستَطيع أَن تَتَذَكَّرها؟
lines.english: Three directions. Can you remember them?
lines.transliteration: thalaath ittijaahaat. hal tastatii' an tatadhaakkarahaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ يا بَحّار! لِنُكمِل خَريطَتَنا
lines.english: You're back, sailor! Let's complete our map.
lines.transliteration: udta ya bahhaar! linukmil khariitanaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: غَرْب — حَيثُ تَغرُب الشَّمس
lines.english: West — where the sun sets.
lines.transliteration: gharb — haythu taghrubu ash-shams

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَمِين — أَدِر الدَّفَّة يَمين!
lines.english: Right — turn the rudder right!
lines.transliteration: yamiin — adir ad-daffa yamiin!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَسَار — أَدِر الدَّفَّة يَسار!
lines.english: Left — turn the rudder left!
lines.transliteration: yasaar — adir ad-daffa yasaar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فَوْق — اُنظُر فَوق إِلى الشِّراع
lines.english: Up/Above — look up at the sail.
lines.transliteration: fawq — unzur fawq ila ash-shiraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَعَة كَلِمات! اِختَبِر نَفسَك
lines.english: Four words! Test yourself.
lines.transliteration: arba'at kalimaat! ikhtabir nafsak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ الله! أَنتَ مَلّاح مُمتاز
lines.english: Mashallah! You are an excellent navigator.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! anta mallaah mumtaaz

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَحْت — الكَنز تَحت الماء
lines.english: Below/Under — the treasure is under the water.
lines.transliteration: taht — al-kanz taht al-maa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَرِيب — الميناء قَريب! أَستَطيع أَن أَراه
lines.english: Near — the port is near! I can see it.
lines.transliteration: qariib — al-miinaa' qariib! astatii' an araahu

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَعِيد — الجَزيرَة بَعيدَة، نَحتاج يَومَين
lines.english: Far — the island is far, we need two days.
lines.transliteration: ba'iid — al-jaziira ba'iida, nahtaaj yawmayn

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآن تَعرِف كُلّ الاِتِّجاهات! اِختِبار أَخير
lines.english: Now you know all the directions! One final test.
lines.transliteration: al-aan ta'rif kull al-ittijaahaat! ikhtibaar akhiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَحر مِثل الحَياة — أَحياناً هادِئ وَأَحياناً عاصِف
lines.english: The sea is like life — sometimes calm and sometimes stormy.
lines.transliteration: al-bahr mithl al-hayaah — ahyaanan haadi' wa ahyaanan aasif

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَنا في الميناء تَجِد سَمَكاً طازَجاً عِند هَنا
lines.english: Here at the port you'll find fresh fish at Hana's stall.
lines.transliteration: hunaa fil-miinaa' tajid samakan taazajan inda hanaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَداوُد الحَدّاد يَصنَع أَفضَل المَراسي
lines.english: And Daud the blacksmith makes the best anchors.
lines.transliteration: wa daawuud al-haddaad yasna' afdal al-maraasii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ماذا تُريد؟ يا لَلبَحر، الوَقتُ ضَيِّق
lines.english: What do you want? By the sea, time is short.
lines.transliteration: maadha turiid? ya lal-bahr, al-waqtu dayyiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَحّار يَحتاج يَعرِف الاتِّجاهات
lines.english: A sailor needs to know directions.
lines.transliteration: al-bahhaar yahtaaj ya'rif al-ittijaahaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَمال — نَحوَ النَّجم القُطبي
lines.english: North — toward the pole star.
lines.transliteration: shamaal — nahwa an-najm al-qutbii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَمين — الجانِب الأَيمَن مِن السَّفينَة
lines.english: Right — the starboard side of the ship.
lines.transliteration: yamiin — al-jaanib al-ayman min as-safiina

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَسار — الجانِب الأَيسَر
lines.english: Left — the port side.
lines.transliteration: yasaar — al-jaanib al-aysar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ كانوا سادَة البِحار
lines.english: The Arabs were masters of the seas.
lines.transliteration: al-'arabu kaanuu saadat al-bihaar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِبنُ ماجِد كانَ أَعظَم مَلّاح عَرَبي
lines.english: Ibn Majid was the greatest Arab navigator.
lines.transliteration: ibnu maajid kaana a'zam mallaah 'arabii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُوَ الَّذي أَرشَدَ فاسكو دي غاما إِلى الهِند
lines.english: He is the one who guided Vasco da Gama to India.
lines.transliteration: huwa alladhii arshada faaskuu dii ghaamaa ilaa al-hind

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُناكَ شُحنَة فُقِدَت قُربَ المَرفَأ
lines.english: There is a shipment lost near the harbor.
lines.transliteration: hunaaka shuhna fuqidat qurba al-marfa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحتاجُ شَخصاً يَعرِف الاتِّجاهات لِيَجِدَها
lines.english: I need someone who knows directions to find it.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju shakhsan ya'rif al-ittijaahaat liyajidahaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل أَنتَ مُستَعِدّ؟
lines.english: Are you ready?
lines.transliteration: hal anta musta'idd?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَفينَة جَديدَة وَصَلَت مِن المَغرِب
lines.english: A new ship arrived from Morocco.
lines.transliteration: safiina jadiida wasalat min al-maghrib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَنادِيَة رَئيسَة المِيناء تَشكو مِن التُّجّار
lines.english: And Nadia the dockmaster complains about the merchants.
lines.transliteration: wa naadiya ra'iisat al-miinaa' tashkuu min at-tujjaar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَةُ 'أَميرال' جاءَت مِن 'أَمير البَحر'
lines.english: The word 'admiral' came from 'amir al-bahr'
lines.transliteration: kalimat 'admiral' ja'at min 'amir al-bahr'
lines.culturalNote: Admiral comes from Arabic 'amir al-bahr' (أمير البحر), meaning 'commander of the sea'. Other nautical terms from Arabic include monsoon (mawsim) and cable (habl).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَلّاحونَ العَرَبُ اختَرَعوا الإسطُرلاب البَحري
lines.english: Arab sailors invented the maritime astrolabe
lines.transliteration: al-mallahun al-arab ikhtara'u al-isturlab al-bahri

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابنُ ماجِد — أُسطورَةُ المُحيطِ الهِندي
lines.english: Ibn Majid — legend of the Indian Ocean
lines.transliteration: ibn majid — usturat al-muhit al-hindi
lines.culturalNote: Ahmad ibn Majid (1421-1500 CE) wrote over 40 works on navigation. He is said to have guided Vasco da Gama's fleet from East Africa to India in 1498.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَا رَفِيقي! هَل تَعرِف سِرَّ البَحَّارَة العَرَب؟ الرِّيح! المَوسِم!
lines.english: My companion! Do you know the secret of Arab sailors? The wind! The monsoon!
lines.transliteration: Yaa rafiiq! Hal ta'rif sirr al-bahhaara al-'Arab? Ar-riyaah! Al-mawsim!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "monsoon" الإِنجليزِيَّة مِن العَرَبِيَّة "مَوسِم" — أَي الوَقت المُحَدَّد لِلرِّيح!
lines.english: The English word "monsoon" comes from Arabic "mawsim" — the fixed season of the wind!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'monsoon' al-injliiziyya min al-'arabiyya 'mawsim' — ay al-waqt al-muhaddad lir-riyaah!
lines.culturalNote: "Monsoon" comes from Arabic "mawsim" (مَوسِم, season/time). Arab sailors were the first to systematically chart monsoon winds, enabling reliable trade routes across the Indian Ocean from East Africa to India and China from the 8th century CE.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَحنُ العَرَب عَرَفنَا المَوسِم قَبلَ كُلِّ أُمَّة — لِذَلِكَ أَبحَرنَا مِن أَفريقيا إِلى الصِّين!
lines.english: We Arabs knew the monsoon before every nation — that is why we sailed from Africa to China!
lines.transliteration: Nahnu al-'Arab 'arafnaa al-mawsim qabla kulli umma — li-dhaalik abharnaaa min Afriqiyaa ilaa as-Siin!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: البَحر! لِأَنَّ البَحر هُوَ طَريق التِّجَارَة والمَعرِفَة!
lines.english: Learn: the sea! Because the sea is the road of trade and knowledge!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-bahr! Li-anna al-bahr huwa tariiq at-tijaara wal-ma'rifa!

choices.english: Tell me about your most dangerous journey

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيَّا! كَلِمَات البَحر! أَولاً: الرِّيح — صَدِيقُ البَحَّار أَو عَدُوُّه!
lines.english: Let us go! Sea words! First: wind — the sailor's friend or enemy!
lines.transliteration: Hayya! Kalimaat al-bahr! Awwalan: ar-riyaah — sadiiq al-bahhaar aw 'aduwwuh!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَانِياً: المَطَر — نِعمَة في الصَّحرَاء، لَكِن في البَحر؟ يَجلِب العَواصِف!
lines.english: Second: rain — a blessing in the desert, but at sea? It brings storms!
lines.transliteration: Thaaniyan: al-matar — ni'ma fis-sahraa', laakin fil-bahr? Yajilib al-'awaasif!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَالِثاً: النَّجم — البَحَّار يَسير بِالنُّجوم! بِدُون نُجوم، ضَاع البَحَّار!
lines.english: Third: star — the sailor navigates by stars! Without stars, the sailor is lost!
lines.transliteration: Thaalithan: an-najm — al-bahhaar yasiir bin-nujuum! Bi-duun nujuum, daa' al-bahhaar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَختَبِر! مَن يَعرِف هَذِهِ الكَلِمَات يَستَطيع الإِبحَار في أَيِّ بَحر!
lines.english: Let's test! One who knows these words can sail any sea!
lines.transliteration: Li-nakhtabir! Man ya'rif haadhihi al-kalimaat yastatiiu al-ibhaar fii ayyi bahr!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَظيم! أَنتَ الآن بَحَّار بِالكَلِمَات. بَقِيَ أَن تَصبَح بَحَّاراً بِالسَّفينَة!
lines.english: Magnificent! You are now a sailor in words. It remains for you to become a sailor on a ship!
lines.transliteration: Aziim! Anta al-aan bahhaar bil-kalimaat. Baqiya an tasbaha bahhaar bis-safiina!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخطَر رِحلَة؟ كانَت قُرب خَليج عَدَن. العَاصِفَة جَاءَت مِن لا مَكَان!
lines.english: Most dangerous journey? It was near the Gulf of Aden. The storm came from nowhere!
lines.transliteration: Aktar rihla? Kaanat qurb Khaliij Adan. Al-'aasifa jaa'at min laa makaan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِن القُبَّان كَانَ يَعرِف النُّجوم. نَظَرنَا إِلى السَّمَاء وَنَجَونَا!
lines.english: But the captain knew the stars. We looked to the sky and survived!
lines.transliteration: Laakin al-qubban kaana ya'rif an-nujuum. Nazarnaa ilaa as-samaa' wa najaynaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّفينَة العَرَبِيَّة "الدَّاو" أَبحَرَت مِن شَرق أَفريقيا إِلى الصِّين. بَحَّارَة عَظماء!
lines.english: The Arab "dhow" ship sailed from East Africa to China. Great sailors!
lines.transliteration: As-safiina al-'arabiyya 'ad-daaw' abhaarat min sharq Afriqiyaa ilaa as-Siin. Bahhaara 'uzamaa'!
lines.culturalNote: Arab dhow ships (داو) sailed monsoon routes from East Africa to India and China from the 8th century. Arab sailors used celestial navigation and seasonal monsoon winds to create reliable trade routes 700 years before European explorers.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: النَّجم — لِأَنَّ البَحَّار بِدون نُجوم كَالأَعمى!
lines.english: Learn: star — because a sailor without stars is like a blind man!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: an-najm — li-anna al-bahhaar bi-duun nujuum kal-a'maa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَحر يُعَلِّم الصَّبر — لا يَمكُنُك إِجبارُ الرِّيح
lines.english: The sea teaches patience — you cannot force the wind.
lines.transliteration: al-bahr yu'allim as-sabr — laa yumkinuk ijbaar ar-riih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَثَل: "سافِر تَجِد خَلَفاً عَمَّن تُفارِق" — السَّفَر يُعَوِّض
lines.english: Proverb: "Travel and you will find a substitute for those you leave" — travel compensates.
lines.transliteration: mathal: 'saafir tajid khalafan 'amman tufaariq' — as-safar yu'awwid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"دَلتا" النِّيل جاءَت مِن الحَرف اليوناني "دِلتا" — لَكِن العَرَب طَوَّروا الجُغرافِيا
lines.english: The Nile delta got its name from the Greek letter "delta" — but Arabs developed geography.
lines.transliteration: wa "delta" an-niil jaa'at min al-harf al-yunaani "delta"

personality.catchphrase: يا لَلبَحر! — ya lal-bahr! (Oh, the sea!)

name: Fishmonger Hana
role: Teaches seafood and drink vocabulary

greeting.arabic: يا هَلا يا هَلا! سَمَك طازَج! تَعال تَعال!
greeting.english: Welcome welcome! Fresh fish! Come come!
greeting.transliteration: ya halaa ya halaa! samak taazaj! ta'aal ta'aal!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً! أَنا هَنا، أَبيع أَطيَب سَمَك في الميناء!
lines.english: Hello! I'm Hana, I sell the tastiest fish in the port!
lines.transliteration: ahlan! ana hanaa, abii' atyab samak fil-miinaa'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِندي سَمَك وَمَشروبات. هَل تُريد أَن تَعرِف أَسماءَها؟
lines.english: I have fish and drinks. Do you want to know their names?
lines.transliteration: indii samak wa mashruubaat. hal turiid an ta'rif asmaa'ahaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلّا بِسم الله! أَوَّل شَيء — سَمَكٌ!
lines.english: Let's go, bismillah! First thing — fish!
lines.transliteration: yallaa bismillaah! awwal shay' — samakun!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمَكٌ — طازَج مِن البَحر هَذا الصَّباح!
lines.english: Fish — fresh from the sea this morning!
lines.transliteration: samakun — taazaj min al-bahr haadha as-sabaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَبَعد السَّمَك، شَايٌ ساخِن!
lines.english: And after the fish, hot tea!
lines.transliteration: wa ba'd as-samak, shaayun saakhin!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَو قَهْوَةٌ عَرَبِيَّة — أَحلى قَهوَة في المِنطَقَة!
lines.english: Or Arabic coffee — the best coffee in the area!
lines.transliteration: aw qahwatun arabiyya — ahlaa qahwa fil-mintaqa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاث كَلِمات لَذيذَة! يَلّا اِختِبار!
lines.english: Three delicious words! Come on, quiz time!
lines.transliteration: thalaath kalimaat ladhiidha! yallaa ikhtibaar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَجَعتَ! الحَمدُ لِلَّه. عِندي أَكل وَشُرب أَكثَر!
lines.english: You came back! Alhamdulillah. I have more food and drink!
lines.transliteration: raja'ta! al-hamdu lillaah. indii akl wa shurb akthar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شُرْبَةٌ — شُربَة سَمَك ساخِنَة لِلبَحّارَة
lines.english: Soup — hot fish soup for the sailors.
lines.transliteration: shurbatun — shurbat samak saakhina lil-bahhaara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَصِيرٌ — عَصير بُرتُقال طازَج!
lines.english: Juice — fresh orange juice!
lines.transliteration: asiirun — asiir burtuqaal taazaj!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فَاكِهَةٌ — عِندي فَواكِه مِن كُلّ الأَنواع
lines.english: Fruit — I have fruits of all kinds.
lines.transliteration: faakihatun — indii fawaakiih min kull al-anwaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سُكَّرٌ — هَل تُريد سُكَّر في الشّاي؟
lines.english: Sugar — do you want sugar in your tea?
lines.transliteration: sukkarun — hal turiid sukkar fish-shaay?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَربَع كَلِمات! يَلّا نَشوف!
lines.english: Four words! Let's see!
lines.transliteration: arba' kalimaat! yallaa nshuuf!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا سَلام! أَحسَن زَبون عِندي! كَلِمات أَخيرَة
lines.english: Wonderful! My best customer! Last words.
lines.transliteration: yaa salaam! ahsan zabuun indii! kalimaat akhiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِلْحٌ — السَّمَك بِدون مِلح ما لَهُ طَعم!
lines.english: Salt — fish without salt has no taste!
lines.transliteration: milhun — as-samak biduun milh maa lahuu ta'm!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَحْر — هَذا البَحر يُعطينا السَّمَك كُلّ يَوم
lines.english: Sea — this sea gives us fish every day.
lines.transliteration: bahr — haadha al-bahr yu'tiinaa as-samak kull yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَهْر — المِياه العَذبَة تَأتي مِن النَّهر
lines.english: River — the fresh water comes from the river.
lines.transliteration: nahr — al-miyaah al-adhba ta'tii min an-nahr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِختِبار أَخير! بِسم الله!
lines.english: Final quiz! Bismillah!
lines.transliteration: ikhtibaar akhiir! bismillaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا مَحَلّي! أَبيع هُنا كُلّ يَوم مِن الفَجر
lines.english: This is my stall! I sell here every day from dawn.
lines.transliteration: haadha mahallii! abii' hunaa kull yawm min al-fajr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَحّارَة يَجلِبون السَّمَك وَأَنا أَبيعُه لِلنّاس
lines.english: The sailors bring the fish and I sell it to the people.
lines.transliteration: al-bahhaara yajlibuun as-samak wa ana abii'uhu lin-naas

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعال تَعَلَّم أَسماء الأَكل وَالشُّرب!
lines.english: Come learn the names of food and drink!
lines.transliteration: ta'aal ta'allam asmaa' al-akl wash-shurb!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طازَج! طازَج! أَهلاً يا حَبيبي
lines.english: Fresh! Fresh! Welcome, my dear!
lines.transliteration: taazaj! taazaj! ahlan ya habiibi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَكلُ نِصفُ الحَياة! تَعال نَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: Food is half of life! Come, let us learn.
lines.transliteration: al-aklu nisf al-hayaah! ta'aal nata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمَك — هَذا ما أَبيع
lines.english: Fish — this is what I sell.
lines.transliteration: samak — haadha maa abii'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خُبْز — كُلّ وَجبَة تَحتاج خُبز
lines.english: Bread — every meal needs bread.
lines.transliteration: khubz — kullu wajba tahtaaj khubz

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَاء — بِدونِ الماء لا حَياة
lines.english: Water — without water there is no life.
lines.transliteration: maa' — biduuni al-maa' laa hayaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبي عَلَّمَني الصَّيد وَأَنا صَغيرَة
lines.english: My father taught me fishing when I was little.
lines.transliteration: abii 'allamanii as-sayd wa ana saghiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَخرُج مَع الفَجر وَنَعود مَع الشَّمس
lines.english: We go out at dawn and return with the sun.
lines.transliteration: nakhruj ma' al-fajr wa na'uud ma' ash-shams

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَطيَبُ سَمَك هُوَ سَمَكُ الصُّبح
lines.english: The tastiest fish is the morning fish.
lines.transliteration: atyabu samak huwa samaku as-subh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القُبطان رَشيد زَعلان اليَوم — سَفينَة تَأَخَّرَت
lines.english: Captain Rashid is angry today — a ship was late.
lines.transliteration: al-qubtaan rashiid za'laan al-yawm — safiina ta'akhkharat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالتاجِر حَسَن يَبحَث عَن تَوابِل جَديدَة
lines.english: And Trader Hassan is looking for new spices.
lines.transliteration: wat-taajir hasan yabhath 'an tawaabil jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَال تَعَال! اليَوم عِندي أَجمَل السَّمَك! وَعِندي أَيضاً قِصَّة جَميلَة!
lines.english: Come come! Today I have the most beautiful fish! And I also have a beautiful story!
lines.transliteration: Ta'aal ta'aal! Al-yawm 'indii ajmal as-samak! Wa 'indii aydan qissa jamiila!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَبلَ النَّفط، كَانَ الخَليج يَعيش على الغَوص! صَيد اللُّؤلُؤ!
lines.english: Before oil, the Gulf lived on diving! Pearl fishing!
lines.transliteration: Qabla an-naft, kaana al-khaliij ya'iish 'alaa al-ghaws! Sayd al-lu'lu'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَجدَادي كَانوا غَوَّاصِين! يَغوصون إِلى قَاع البَحر بِيَدَيهِم — بِدون أَي آلَة!
lines.english: My ancestors were divers! They dove to the sea floor with their hands — without any equipment!
lines.transliteration: Ajdaadii kaanuu ghawwaasiin! Yaghuusuun ilaa qaa' al-bahr bi-yadayhim — bi-duun ayyi aala!
lines.culturalNote: Pearl diving (الغَوص, al-ghaws) was the primary industry of the Arabian Gulf for centuries before oil. Divers could reach depths of 40 meters on a single breath, and Qatar, Bahrain, and Kuwait built entire economies on pearls sold to India and Europe.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: السَّمَك — أَهَمُّ كَلِمَة في السّوق الساحِلِيّ!
lines.english: Learn: fish — the most important word in the coastal market!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: as-samak — ahamm kalima fis-suuq as-saahiliyy!

choices.english: Tell me more about pearl diving

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطَّعَام! أَعظَم الكَلِمَات! اِستَمِع! الخُبز — أَسَاس كُلِّ وَجبَة!
lines.english: Food! The greatest words! Listen! Bread — the foundation of every meal!
lines.transliteration: At-ta'aam! A'zam al-kalimaat! Istami'! Al-khubz — asaas kulli wajba!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّمر! غِذَاء الصَّحرَاء. العَرَب عَاشوا على التَّمر لِآلاف السِّنين!
lines.english: Dates! Food of the desert. Arabs lived on dates for thousands of years!
lines.transliteration: At-tamr! Ghidhaa' as-sahraa'. Al-'Arab 'aashuu 'alaa at-tamr li-aalaaf as-sinin!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَسَل! دَوَاء وَغِذَاء في آنٍ وَاحِد. النَّحل يَعمَل وَنَحنُ نَستَفيد!
lines.english: Honey! Medicine and food at the same time. Bees work and we benefit!
lines.transliteration: Al-'asal! Dawaa' wa ghidhaa' fii aanin waahid. An-nahl ya'mal wa nahnu nastafid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَهوَة! شَرَاب العَرَب المَقدَّس! مِن اليَمَن انتَشَرَت إِلى العَالَم كُلِّه!
lines.english: Coffee! The sacred Arab drink! From Yemen it spread to the whole world!
lines.transliteration: Al-qahwa! Sharaab al-'Arab al-muqaddas! Min al-Yaman intatarat ilaa al-'aalam kullih!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! الآن تَعرِف مَا يَكفيكَ لِلعَيش. تَعَال كُلَّ يَوم وَسَأُعَلِّمُكَ المَزيد!
lines.english: Excellent! Now you know enough to live on. Come every day and I will teach you more!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Al-aan ta'rif maa yakfiik lil-'aysh. Ta'aal kull yawm wa sa-u'allimuka al-maziid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اللُّؤلُؤ! كَانَ يُسَاوي الذَّهَب في الهِند وَأُوروبَّا. كَانَ كَنز الخَليج!
lines.english: Pearls! They were worth gold in India and Europe. They were the treasure of the Gulf!
lines.transliteration: Al-lu'lu'! Kaana yusaawii adh-dhahab fil-Hind wa Uurubba. Kaana kanz al-khaliij!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الغَوَّاص يَحمِل حَجَراً ثَقِيلاً لِيَنزِل سَريعاً. ثُمَّ يَلتَقِط الأَصداف بِيَدَيه!
lines.english: The diver carries a heavy stone to descend quickly. Then he collects shells with his hands!
lines.transliteration: Al-ghawwaas yahmil hajaran thaqiilan li-yanzil sarii'an. Thumma yaltaqit al-asdaaf bi-yadaih!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثُمَّ جَاءَ النَّفط — وَانتَهى زَمَن الغَوص. لَكِن القِصَص بَقِيَت!
lines.english: Then oil came — and the age of diving ended. But the stories remained!
lines.transliteration: Thumma jaa' an-naft — wa intahaa zaman al-ghaws. Laakin al-qisas baqiyat!
lines.culturalNote: Before oil was discovered in Bahrain (1932) and Kuwait (1938), pearl diving was the backbone of Gulf economies. Bahrain alone exported 3-4 million pearls per year by the early 20th century. Japanese cultured pearls destroyed the industry in the 1920s-30s.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الماء — لِأَنَّ بِدُون الماء لا بَحر وَلا حَيَاة!
lines.english: Learn: water — because without water there is no sea and no life!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-maa' — li-anna bi-duun al-maa' laa bahr wa laa hayaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَي، أَنتَ! تَعَال! البِضَاعَة اليَوم طَازَجَة! صِيدَت هَذَا الصَّبَاح!
lines.english: Hey, you! Come! The goods today are fresh! Caught this morning!
lines.transliteration: Ay, anta! Ta'aal! Al-bidaa'a al-yawm taazija! Siidat haadha as-sabaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف أَنَّ كَلِمَة "tuna" رُبَّما مِن العَرَبِيَّة "تُنَّ"؟ العَرَب صَادوا التُّنَّ قَديماً!
lines.english: Did you know the word "tuna" may come from Arabic "tunn"? Arabs fished tuna in ancient times!
lines.transliteration: Hal ta'rif anna kalima 'tuna' rubbama min al-'arabiyya 'tunn'? Al-'Arab saaduu at-tunn qadiiman!
lines.culturalNote: The word "tuna" may derive from Arabic "tunn" (تُنّ) via Medieval Latin "thunnus." Arab fishermen in the Mediterranean and Gulf developed sophisticated nets and seasonal fishing knowledge that influenced global fishing traditions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِشتَرِ مِنّي! تَعَلَّم: السُّوق — أَجمَل مَكان في أَيِّ مَدينَة!
lines.english: Buy from me! Learn: the market — the most beautiful place in any city!
lines.transliteration: Ishtari minni! Ta'allam: as-suuq — ajmal makaan fii ayyi madiina!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالسَّمَكَة هَذِه؟ بِثَمَن زَهيد! تَعَلَّم: رَخيص — كَلِمَة مُهِمَّة في السُّوق!
lines.english: And this fish? At a cheap price! Learn: cheap — an important word in the market!
lines.transliteration: Wa as-samaka haadhihi? Bi-thaman zahiid! Ta'allam: rakhiis — kalima muhimma fis-suuq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! المُشتَري الذَّكِيّ يَعرِف الكَلِمَات! كَم يُكَلِّف؟ — تَسأَل هَكَذا!
lines.english: Excellent! The clever buyer knows the words! How much does it cost? — you ask like this!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Al-mushtari adh-dhakii ya'rif al-kalimaat! Kam yukallif? — tas'al hakadhaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: السِّعر — لِأَنَّ في كُلِّ سُوق يَسأَل الجَميع عَنه!
lines.english: Learn: the price — because in every market everyone asks about it!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: as-si'r — li-anna fii kulli suuq yas'al al-jamii' 'anh!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالمَال! لا سُوق بِدون مَال! لَكِن بِدون مَعرِفَة، المَال لا يَنفَع!
lines.english: And money! No market without money! But without knowledge, money is useless!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-maal! Laa suuq bi-duun maal! Laakin bi-duun ma'rifa, al-maal laa yanfa'!

personality.catchphrase: طازَج! طازَج! — taazaj! taazaj! (Fresh! Fresh!)

name: Blacksmith Daud
role: Teaches trade items and nature words

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً. الحَديد يَتَكَلَّم بِصَوتِه. اِسمَع
greeting.english: Welcome. The iron speaks with its voice. Listen.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan. al-hadiid yatakallam bisawtihi. isma'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا داوُد الحَدّاد. أَصنَعُ مِن الحَديد ما يَحتاجُه النّاس
lines.english: I am Daud the blacksmith. I craft from iron what people need.
lines.transliteration: ana daawuud al-haddaad. asna'u min al-hadiid maa yahtaajuhu an-naas

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التِّجارَة وَالطَّبيعَة — كِلاهُما يُعَلِّمان الصَّبر
lines.english: Trade and nature — both teach patience.
lines.transliteration: at-tijaara wat-tabii'a — kilaahumaa yu'allimaani as-sabr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التِّجارَة تَحتاج أَدَوات. لِنَبدَأ
lines.english: Trade needs tools. Let's begin.
lines.transliteration: at-tijaara tahtaaj adawaat. linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِيزَان — أَصنَعُهُ بِيَدَيَّ. يَزِنُ الذَّهَب وَالفِضَّة
lines.english: Scale — I make it with my hands. It weighs gold and silver.
lines.transliteration: miizaan — asna'uhu biyadayya. yazinu adh-dhahab wal-fidda

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دِرْهَم — العُملَة الَّتي يَستَخدِمُها التُّجّار
lines.english: Dirham — the coin that merchants use.
lines.transliteration: dirham — al-umla allatii yastakhdimuha at-tujjaar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَبَل — الحَديد يَأتي مِن الجَبَل
lines.english: Mountain — the iron comes from the mountain.
lines.transliteration: jabal — al-hadiid ya'tii min al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاث كَلِمات. بَسيطَة لَكِن مُهِمَّة
lines.english: Three words. Simple but important.
lines.transliteration: thalaath kalimaat. basiita laakin muhimma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ. جَيِّد. الحَدّاد يُلاحِظ الطَّبيعَة
lines.english: You returned. Good. A blacksmith observes nature.
lines.transliteration: udta. jayyid. al-haddaad yulaahiz at-tabii'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رِيح — الرّيح تُشعِل النّار في الكِير
lines.english: Wind — the wind lights the fire in the furnace.
lines.transliteration: riih — ar-riih tush'il an-naar fil-kiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمَاء — أَنظُرُ إِلى السَّماء لِأَعرِف الطَّقس
lines.english: Sky — I look at the sky to know the weather.
lines.transliteration: samaa' — anzuru ila as-samaa' li-a'rif at-taqs

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَجْم — في اللَّيل، النُّجوم تُنير الطَّريق
lines.english: Star — at night, the stars light the path.
lines.transliteration: najm — fil-layl, an-nujuum tuniir at-tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطَّبيعَة مُعَلِّمَة عَظيمَة. هَل تَتَذَكَّر؟
lines.english: Nature is a great teacher. Do you remember?
lines.transliteration: at-tabii'a mu'allima aziima. hal tatadhaakkar?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ صَبور مِثل الحَدّاد. هَذا جَيِّد
lines.english: You are patient like a blacksmith. That is good.
lines.transliteration: anta sabuur mithl al-haddaad. haadha jayyid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَجَّادَة — التُّجّار يَبيعون سَجّاجيد مِن كُلّ مَكان
lines.english: Carpet — merchants sell carpets from everywhere.
lines.transliteration: sajjaada — at-tujjaar yabii'uun sajaajiid min kull makaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَاجِر — الَّذي يَشتَري وَيَبيع
lines.english: Merchant — the one who buys and sells.
lines.transliteration: taajir — alladhii yashtarii wa yabii'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَهَار — البَهارات تُعطي الأَكل نَكهَة
lines.english: Spice — spices give food flavor.
lines.transliteration: bahaar — al-bahaaraat tu'tii al-akl nakha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِختِبار أَخير. أَثبِت أَنَّك تَعَلَّمت
lines.english: A final test. Prove that you have learned.
lines.transliteration: ikhtibaar akhiir. athbit annaka ta'allamta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَعمَل هُنا كُلّ يَوم مِن الفَجر إِلى المَغرِب
lines.english: I work here every day from dawn to dusk.
lines.transliteration: a'mal hunaa kull yawm min al-fajr ila al-maghrib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَديد يُعَلِّمُك الصَّبر. إِذا اِستَعجَلتَ، يَنكَسِر
lines.english: Iron teaches you patience. If you rush, it breaks.
lines.transliteration: al-hadiid yu'allimuk as-sabr. idha ista'jalta, yankasir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَاللُّغَة مِثل الحَديد. تَحتاج وَقتاً وَصَبراً
lines.english: And language is like iron. It needs time and patience.
lines.transliteration: wal-lugha mithl al-hadiid. tahtaaj waqtan wa sabran

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَديدُ لا يَكذِب. ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: Iron does not lie. What do you want?
lines.transliteration: al-hadiidu laa yakdhib. maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَدَواتُ لُغَة الحَدّاد
lines.english: Tools are the blacksmith's language.
lines.transliteration: al-adawaatu lughat al-haddaad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَحْم — المَعدِن يُشبِه اللَّحم عِندَ الصَّهر
lines.english: Meat — metal resembles meat when melting.
lines.transliteration: lahm — al-ma'din yushbihu al-lahm 'inda as-sahr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فَوْق — ضَع المِطرَقَة فَوقَ السِّندان
lines.english: Above — place the hammer above the anvil.
lines.transliteration: fawq — da' al-mitraqa fawqa as-sindaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَحْت — النّار تَحتَ المَعدِن
lines.english: Below — the fire below the metal.
lines.transliteration: taht — an-naar tahta al-ma'din

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبي وَجَدّي كانا حَدّادَين
lines.english: My father and grandfather were blacksmiths.
lines.transliteration: abii wa jaddii kaanaa haddaadayn

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّيف العَرَبي — أَجمَل ما صَنَعَت يَدُ إِنسان
lines.english: The Arab sword — the most beautiful thing a hand ever made.
lines.transliteration: as-sayf al-'arabii — ajmal maa sana'at yadu insaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصَّبرُ هُوَ سِرّ الحِدادَة الجَيِّدَة
lines.english: Patience is the secret of good smithing.
lines.transliteration: as-sabru huwa sirr al-hidaada al-jayyida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ظَهري يُؤلِمُني. خَديجَة أَعطَتني شاي زَنجَبيل
lines.english: My back hurts. Khadija gave me ginger tea.
lines.transliteration: zahrii yu'limunii. khadiija a'tatnii shaay zanjabiil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القُبطان يُريد سَيفاً جَديداً. كَثير العَمَل
lines.english: The captain wants a new sword. Lots of work.
lines.transliteration: al-qubtaan yuriid sayfan jadiidan. kathiir al-'amal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الفولاذُ الدِّمَشقي كانَ أَقوى مَعدِنٍ في العالَم
lines.english: Damascus steel was the strongest metal in the world
lines.transliteration: al-fulath ad-dimashqi kan aqwa ma'din fil-'alam
lines.culturalNote: Damascus steel swords were famous for their distinctive wavy pattern (damask). The technique was lost around 1750 CE and has never been fully replicated.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَنماطُ الهَندَسيَّة في الفَنِّ الإسلامي تَعتَمِدُ على الرِّياضيّات
lines.english: Geometric patterns in Islamic art are based on mathematics
lines.transliteration: al-anmat al-handasiyya fil-fann al-islami ta'tamid 'ala ar-riyadiyyat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ نَمَطٍ يَبدَأُ مِن دائِرَة — الكَمالُ الإلهي
lines.english: Every pattern begins from a circle — divine perfection
lines.transliteration: kullu namat yabda' min da'ira — al-kamal al-ilahi
lines.culturalNote: Islamic geometric art avoids depicting living beings. Instead, artists used pure geometry and mathematical ratios, creating infinitely repeating patterns that suggest the infinite nature of God.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِنظُر إِلى هَذِه السَّيف! يَرى الطَّيف فِيها! هَذِهِ هِيَ فُولاذ دِمَشق الأَصيل!
lines.english: Look at this sword! You can see your reflection in it! This is genuine Damascus steel!
lines.transliteration: Unzur ilaa haadha as-sayf! Yaraa at-tayf fiihaa! Haadhihi hiya fuulaadh Dimashq al-asiil!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فُولاذ دِمَشق! أَسطورَة الحَدَّادِين. نَمط مَوجِيّ كَالماء. لا يُنسى!
lines.english: Damascus steel! The legend of blacksmiths. A wavy pattern like water. Unforgettable!
lines.transliteration: Fuulaadh Dimashq! Ustuuratu al-haddaadin. Namat mawjiyy kal-maa'. Laa yunsaa!
lines.culturalNote: Damascus steel (فُولاذ دِمَشق) had a distinctive wavy "damask" pattern caused by carbon nanotubes. Modern science only confirmed this in 2006. The technique was perfected in Damascus around 1000 CE and was LOST around 1750 CE — it has never been fully replicated.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الوَصفَة ضَاعَت حَوالي عَام 1750. لا يَستَطيع أَحَد صُنعَها الآن تَماماً!
lines.english: The recipe was lost around 1750. Nobody can make it exactly the same now!
lines.transliteration: Al-wasfa daa'at hawaalii 'aam 1750. Laa yastatiiu ahadun sun'ahaa al-aan tamaaман!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الذَّهَب — الحَدَّاد يَعرِف قِيمَة المَعدَن كَمَا يَعرِفُ قِيمَة المَعرِفَة!
lines.english: Learn: gold — a blacksmith knows the value of metal as he knows the value of knowledge!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: adh-dhahab — al-haddaad ya'rif qiimat al-ma'din kamaa ya'rif qiimat al-ma'rifa!

choices.english: How did you make this sword?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَهارَة! التِّجَارَة! تَعَلَّم كَلِمَات العَمَل يَا صَاحِبي!
lines.english: Craft! Trade! Learn the words of work, my companion!
lines.transliteration: Al-mahaara! At-tijaara! Ta'allam kalimaat al-'amal yaa saahib!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الفِضَّة! بَعدَ الذَّهَب، أَجمَل مَعدِن. وَأَنَا الحَدَّاد أَعرِف كِلَيهِمَا!
lines.english: Silver! After gold, the most beautiful metal. And I the blacksmith know both!
lines.transliteration: Al-fidda! Ba'da adh-dhahab, ajmal ma'din. Wa ana al-haddaad a'rif kilayhima!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَمَل! هَذِه الكَلِمَة أَعظَم كَلِمَة في لُغَة الحَدَّادِين!
lines.english: Work! This word is the greatest word in the language of blacksmiths!
lines.transliteration: Al-'amal! Haadhihi al-kalima a'zam kalima fii lughat al-haddaadin!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَعطِ — لِأَنَّ الحَدَّاد يَصنَع وَيُعطِي لِلمُجتَمَع. العَطَاء عِبَادَة!
lines.english: Give — because the blacksmith makes and gives to the community. Giving is worship!
lines.transliteration: A'ti — li-anna al-haddaad yasna' wa yu'tii lil-mujtama'. Al-'ataa' 'ibaada!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! الآن أَنتَ تَتَكَلَّم مِثلَ تَاجِر. عُد وَسَأُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمَات المَعدِن الأُخرى!
lines.english: Excellent! Now you speak like a merchant. Come back and I will teach you more metal words!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Al-aan anta tatakallam mithla taajir. 'Ud wa sa-u'allimuka kalimaat al-ma'din al-ukhraa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَولاً: النَّار! بِدُون نَار لا حِدَادَة. الحَرَارَة تُحَوِّل الحَجَر إِلى أَدَاة!
lines.english: First: fire! Without fire there is no blacksmithing. Heat transforms stone into tool!
lines.transliteration: Awwalan: an-naar! Bi-duun naar laa hidaada. Al-haraara tuhawwil al-hajar ilaa adaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَانِياً: المَطرَقَة والسِّنديان. الحَدَّاد يَضرِب، ويَشكِّل، وَيُعِيد الضَّرب حَتَّى يَكتَمِل الشَّكل!
lines.english: Second: the hammer and anvil. The blacksmith strikes, shapes, and re-strikes until the form is complete!
lines.transliteration: Thaaniyan: al-matраqa was-sindiyaan. Al-haddaad yadrib, wa yushakkil, wa yu'iid ad-darb hattaa yaktamil ash-shakl!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَالِثاً: الماء البَارِد! التَّبريد السَّريع يُقَسِّي المَعدِن. هَذَا سِرُّ الفُولاذ!
lines.english: Third: cold water! Rapid cooling hardens the metal. This is the secret of steel!
lines.transliteration: Thaalithan: al-maa' al-baarid! At-tabriid as-sarii' yuqassii al-ma'din. Haadha sirr al-fuulaadh!
lines.culturalNote: Islamic geometric metalwork, featuring intricate arabesque patterns, influenced European decorative arts from the Crusades onward. The word "steel" itself derives from Proto-Germanic, but Arab metalworkers preserved and advanced Roman techniques during Europe's Dark Ages.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: قَوِيّ — لِأَنَّ الفُولاذ الجَيِّد قَوِيٌّ، وَكَذَلِك الإِنسَان الجَيِّد!
lines.english: Learn: strong — because good steel is strong, and so is a good person!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: qawiyy — li-anna al-fuulaadh al-jayyid qawiyy, wa kadhalik al-insaan al-jayyid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَا صَاحِب! اِنظُر إِلى هَذَا الزَّخرَف! الهَندَسَة الإِسلَامِيَّة في المَعدِن!
lines.english: My companion! Look at this decoration! Islamic geometry in metal!
lines.transliteration: Yaa saahib! Unzur ilaa haadha az-zakhraf! Al-handasa al-islaamiyya fil-ma'din!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النُّجوم السِّتُّ، الأَنماط المُتَشَابِكَة — كُلُّها لا تَنتَهي وَلا تَبتَدِئ. كَمِثل الله!
lines.english: Six-pointed stars, interlocking patterns — they never end and never begin. Like God!
lines.transliteration: An-nujuum as-sitt, al-anmaat al-mutashaabika — kulluhaa laa tantahii wa laa tabтadi'. Ka-mithli Allaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَمَل الجَيِّد يَجمَع الجَمَال والفَائِدَة. تَعَلَّم: جَميل — لِأَنَّ الأَدَاة الجَمِيلَة تُكرِّمُها!
lines.english: Good work combines beauty and utility. Learn: beautiful — because you honor a beautiful tool!
lines.transliteration: Al-'amal al-jayyid yajma' al-jamaal wal-faa'ida. Ta'allam: jamiil — li-anna al-adaa al-jamiila tukarrimuhaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِعمَل بِإِتقَان — هَذَا هُوَ الإِحسَان. وَهَذِه وَصِيَّة النَّبي صَلَّى الله عَلَيه وَسَلَّم.
lines.english: Work with excellence — this is ihsan. And this is the advice of the Prophet, peace be upon him.
lines.transliteration: I'mal bi-itqaan — haadha huwa al-ihsaan. Wa haadhihi wasiyyat an-Nabiyy sallaa Allaahu 'alayhi wa sallam.

personality.catchphrase: الحَديدُ لا يَكذِب — al-hadiidu laa yakdhib (Iron does not lie)

name: Vizier Abbas
role: Teaches formal phrases and etiquette

greeting.arabic: مَرْحَباً بِكَ فِي القَصْرِ المَلَكِيّ، يا ضَيْفَنا الكَرِيم
greeting.english: Welcome to the Royal Palace, our honored guest
greeting.transliteration: marhaban bika fil-qasri al-malakiyy, ya dayfanaa al-kariim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الوَزِير عَبّاس، حارِسُ آدابِ البَلاط
lines.english: I am Vizier Abbas, keeper of court etiquette.
lines.transliteration: ana al-waziir abbaas, haarisu aadaab al-balaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَقَد وَصَلْتَ إِلى القَصْرِ المَلَكِيّ — نِهايَةُ رِحْلَتِكَ الطَّوِيلَة
lines.english: You have reached the Royal Palace — the end of your long journey.
lines.transliteration: laqad wasalta ilaa al-qasri al-malakiyy — nihaayatu rihlatika at-tawiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِنْ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ، يَجِبُ أَنْ تَتَعَلَّمَ آدابَ القَصْر
lines.english: But before you enter, you must learn the manners of the palace.
lines.transliteration: laakin qabla an tadkhula, yajibu an tata'allama aadaab al-qasr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي القَصْرِ، الأَدَبُ أَهَمُّ مِنَ القُوَّة. لِنَبْدَأ
lines.english: In the palace, manners are more important than strength. Let us begin.
lines.transliteration: fil-qasri, al-adabu ahammu min al-quwwa. linabda'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ — تَقُولُها عِنْدَما تَطْلُبُ شَيْئاً بِأَدَب
lines.english: Law samaht — you say it when you ask for something politely.
lines.transliteration: law samaht — taquuluhaa indamaa tatlub shay'an bi-adab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا آسِفٌ — تَقُولُها عِنْدَما تُخْطِئ
lines.english: Ana aasif — you say it when you make a mistake.
lines.transliteration: ana aasif — taquuluhaa indamaa tukhti'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَبْرُوكٌ — تَقُولُها لِلتَّهْنِئَة
lines.english: Mabrook — you say it to congratulate someone.
lines.transliteration: mabrook — taquuluhaa lit-tahni'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَسَنٌ، لِنَرَ إِنْ حَفِظْتَ هَذِهِ العِبارات
lines.english: Good, let us see if you memorized these phrases.
lines.transliteration: hasanun, linara in hafizta haadhihi al-ibaaraat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَوْدَةٌ مُبارَكَة! لَدَيَّ عِبارَاتٌ مُهِمَّة أُخرَى
lines.english: Blessed return! I have more important phrases for you.
lines.transliteration: awdatun mubaaraka! ladayya ibaaraatun muhimma ukhraa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا أَعْرِفُ — تَقُولُها عِنْدَما لا تَعْرِفُ الجَوابَ
lines.english: La a'rif — you say it when you don't know the answer.
lines.transliteration: laa a'rif — taquuluhaa indamaa laa ta'rif al-jawaab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَتَعَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّةَ — عِبارَةٌ مُفِيدَة جِدّاً لِلضُّيُوف
lines.english: Ana ata'allam al-arabiyya — a very useful phrase for guests.
lines.transliteration: ana ata'allamu al-arabiyya — ibaaratun mufiida jiddan lid-duyuuf

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما هَذا؟ — تَسْأَلُ بِها عَن الأَشْياء
lines.english: Ma haadha? — you ask it about things.
lines.transliteration: maa haadha? — tas'alu bihaa an al-ashyaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا... — وَالجَوابُ يَكُونُ هَكَذا
lines.english: Haadha... — and the answer is like this.
lines.transliteration: haadha... — wal-jawaabu yakuunu haakadha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمْتَحِنْ نَفْسَكَ الآن!
lines.english: Test yourself now!
lines.transliteration: imtahin nafsaka al-aan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنْتَ تَتَقَدَّمُ بِسُرْعَة. هَذِهِ العِباراتُ مِنْ أَعْمَقِ ما فِي لُغَتِنا
lines.english: You are progressing quickly. These phrases are among the deepest in our language.
lines.transliteration: anta tataqaddamu bisur'a. haadhihi al-ibaaraatu min a'maqi maa fii lughatinaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ — نَقُولُها عِنْدَما نَتَكَلَّمُ عَنِ المُسْتَقْبَل
lines.english: In shaa' Allah — we say it when speaking about the future.
lines.transliteration: in shaa'allaah — naquuluhaa indamaa natakallamu an al-mustaqbal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ اللَّهُ — نَقُولُها عِنْدَ الإِعْجاب
lines.english: Ma shaa' Allah — we say it when we admire something.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah — naquuluhaa inda al-i'jaab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ — نَقُولُها قَبْلَ كُلِّ عَمَل
lines.english: Bismillah — we say it before every action.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah — naquuluhaa qabla kulli amal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ كَلِماتٌ تَحْمِلُ بَرَكَة. هَل تَحْفَظُها؟
lines.english: These are words that carry blessing. Do you remember them?
lines.transliteration: haadhihi kalimaatun tahmilu baraka. hal tahfazuhaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا القَصْرُ المَلَكِيّ بُنِيَ قَبْلَ مِئاتِ السِّنِين
lines.english: This Royal Palace was built hundreds of years ago.
lines.transliteration: haadha al-qasru al-malakiyy buniya qabla mi'aati as-siniin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا تَسْكُنُ الأَمِيرَةُ عائِشَة، وَالإِمامُ مُحَمَّد يُعَلِّمُ فِي المَكْتَبَة
lines.english: Here lives Princess Aisha, and Imam Muhammad teaches in the library.
lines.transliteration: hunaa taskunu al-amiiiratu aa'isha, wal-imaamu muhammad yu'allimu fil-maktaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالشّاعِرُ الرُّومِيّ يَزُورُنا كَثِيراً بِأَشْعارِهِ الجَمِيلَة
lines.english: And the poet Rumi visits us often with his beautiful poetry.
lines.transliteration: wash-shaa'iru ar-ruumiyy yazuurunaa kathiiran bi-ash'aarihi al-jamiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِأَمرِ المَلِك. تَكَلَّم بِسُرعَة
lines.english: By the king's command. Speak quickly.
lines.transliteration: bi-amr al-malik. takallam bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَملَكَة بُنِيَت عَلى العِلم وَالعَدل
lines.english: This kingdom was built on knowledge and justice.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-mamlaka buniyat 'alaa al-'ilm wal-'adl

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَلِكُ الأَوَّل أَسَّسَ المَكتَبَة قَبلَ القَصر
lines.english: The first king founded the library before the palace.
lines.transliteration: al-maliku al-awwal assasa al-maktaba qabla al-qasr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا يَقول الكَثير عَن قِيَمِنا
lines.english: This says a lot about our values.
lines.transliteration: haadha yaquul al-kathiir 'an qiyaminaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَملَكَة تَحتاج مَن يَخدِمُها
lines.english: The kingdom needs those who serve it.
lines.transliteration: al-mamlaka tahtaaj man yakhdimuhaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: إِذا أَثبَتَّ نَفسَك، سَأُعطيكَ مُهِمَّة
lines.english: If you prove yourself, I will give you a mission.
lines.transliteration: idhaa athbatta nafsak, sa-u'tiika muhimma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَميرَة عائِشَة تُريد السَّفَر لَكِنَّ المَلِك يَرفُض
lines.english: Princess Aisha wants to travel but the king refuses.
lines.transliteration: al-amiira 'aa'isha turiid as-safar laakinna al-malik yarfud

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالشّاعِر رومي يَكتُب قَصيدَة لِلمَلِك
lines.english: And the poet Rumi is writing a poem for the king.
lines.transliteration: wash-shaa'ir ruumii yaktub qasiida lil-malik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس! الحُكم يَحتَاج عَقلاً قَبلَ سَيف. دَعني أُعَلِّمُكَ كَيفَ تَفكِّر.
lines.english: Sit! Governance needs a mind before a sword. Let me teach you how to think.
lines.transliteration: Ijlis! Al-hukm yahtaaju 'aqlan qabla sayf. Da'ni u'allimuka kayfa tufakkir.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الدَّولَة العَبَّاسِيَّة بَنَت أَول نِظَام بُرِيد في العَالَم — البَرِيد! أَلف مِيل مِن بَغدَاد إِلى خُرَاسَان!
lines.english: The Abbasid state built the world's first postal system — the barid! A thousand miles from Baghdad to Khorasan!
lines.transliteration: Ad-dawla al-'abbaasiyya banat awwal nizaam bariid fil-'aalam — al-bariid! Alf miil min Baghdad ilaa Khurasaan!
lines.culturalNote: "Vizier" (وَزير, wazir) comes from Arabic, meaning "burden-bearer." The Abbasid postal system (البَرِيد, al-bariid) spanned 1,000+ miles, with relay stations every few miles — the world's most sophisticated communication network from 750-1258 CE.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "vizier" نَفسُها عَرَبِيَّة — وَزِير، حَامِل العِبء! أَنا أَحمِل عِبءَ المَملَكَة!
lines.english: The word "vizier" itself is Arabic — wazir, burden-bearer! I carry the burden of the kingdom!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'vizier' nafsuhaa 'arabiyya — wazeer, haamil al-'ibb! Ana ahmil 'ib' al-mamlaka!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: المَلِك — لِأَنَّ كُلَّ دَولَة تَحتَاج قَائِداً وَإِدَارَة!
lines.english: Learn: the king — because every state needs a leader and administration!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-malik — li-anna kull dawla tahtaaju qaa'idan wa idaara!

choices.english: What is the secret of good governance?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّحِيَّة الرَّسمِيَّة أَولاً! في بَلاط الخَليفَة كَانَ لِكُلِّ مَقَام مَقَال.
lines.english: The formal greeting first! In the Caliph's court there was a proper expression for every occasion.
lines.transliteration: At-tahiyya ar-rasmiyya awwalan! Fii balaat al-khalifa kaana li-kulli maqaam maqaal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصَّبَاح. "صَبَاح الخَير" — أَفضَل بِدَايَة لِيَوم السِّيَاسَة!
lines.english: Morning. "Sabah al-khayr" — the best beginning for a day of politics!
lines.transliteration: As-sabaah. 'Sabaah al-khayr' — afdal bidaaya li-yawm as-siyaasa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَسَاء. "مَسَاء الخَير" — وَمَن يُتِمُّ نَهَاره بِخَير كَسَبَ الدِّبلُومَاسِيَّة!
lines.english: Evening. "Masaa al-khayr" — and he who ends his day well has won diplomacy!
lines.transliteration: Al-masaa'. 'Masaa' al-khayr' — wa man yutimm nahaarah bi-khayr kasaba ad-diblumaasiiyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالأَهَمّ: أَعرِف مَتَى تَتَكَلَّم وَمَتَى تَصمُت. السُّكوت ذَهَب في السِّيَاسَة!
lines.english: Most importantly: know when to speak and when to be silent. Silence is gold in politics!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-ahamm: a'rif mataa tatakallam wa mataa tasмut. As-sukuut dhahab fis-siyaasa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! أَنتَ تَتَعَلَّم آدَاب البَلاط. رُبَّما يَوماً تَصبَح وَزِيراً!
lines.english: Excellent! You are learning court manners. Perhaps one day you will become a vizier!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Anta tata'allam aadaab al-balaat. Rubbamaa yawman tasbahu waziiran!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سِرُّ الحُكم الجَيِّد؟ ثَلاثَة أَشيَاء: العَدل، الاِستِشَارَة، وَالتَّواضُع!
lines.english: The secret of good governance? Three things: justice, consultation, and humility!
lines.transliteration: Sirr al-hukm al-jayyid? Thalaatha ashyaa': al-'adl, al-istishaara, wat-tawadu'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَليفَة هَارون الرَّشيد كَانَ يَتَنَكَّر لَيلاً لِيَعرِف أَحوَال النَّاس بِنَفسِه!
lines.english: Caliph Harun al-Rashid used to disguise himself at night to personally know the state of the people!
lines.transliteration: Al-khalifa Haaruun ar-Rashiid kaana yatanakkar laylan li-ya'rif ahwaal an-naas bi-nafsih!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الدَّولَة العَبَّاسِيَّة جَمَعَت العُلَمَاء مِن كُلِّ الأَدِيَان والأَجنَاس. هَذَا هُوَ الحُكم الحَقِيقِيّ!
lines.english: The Abbasid state gathered scholars from all religions and peoples. This is true governance!
lines.transliteration: Ad-dawla al-'abbaasiyya jama'at al-'ulamaa' min kulli al-adyaan wal-ajnaas. Haadha huwa al-hukm al-haqiiqi!
lines.culturalNote: The Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE) created the first truly multicultural intellectual state. The House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma) employed scholars of every faith — Muslim, Christian, Jewish, Zoroastrian — to translate all human knowledge into Arabic.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: قَديم — لِأَنَّ الحِكمَة القَدِيمَة لا تَشيخ أَبَداً!
lines.english: Learn: old/ancient — because ancient wisdom never grows old!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: qadiim — li-anna al-hikma al-qadiima laa tashiikh abadan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَقرَب إِليَّ! سَأُطلِعُكَ على سِرٍّ مِن أَسرَار البَلاط. لا تُخبِر أَحَداً!
lines.english: Come closer! I will share with you a secret of the court. Tell no one!
lines.transliteration: Aqrab ilayya! Sa-utli'uk 'alaa sirrin min asraar al-balaat. Laa takhbar ahadan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الوَزِير الجَيِّد يَعرِف مَتَى يُعطِي وَمَتَى يَأخُذ. مَتَى يَتَكَلَّم وَمَتَى يَسكُت.
lines.english: A good vizier knows when to give and when to take. When to speak and when to be silent.
lines.transliteration: Al-wazeer al-jayyid ya'rif mataa yu'tii wa mataa ya'khudh. Mataa yatakallam wa mataa yaskut.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: أَخَذَ — هَذِه الكَلِمَة مُهِمَّة في كُلِّ مُفَاوَضَة!
lines.english: Learn: to take — this word is important in every negotiation!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: akhadha — haadhihi al-kalima muhimma fii kulli mufaawada!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالأَهَمّ: النَّوم! الوَزِير الذي لا يَنَام يَفقِد قُدرَتَه على التَّفكِير. النَّوم عَقل!
lines.english: Most important: sleep! The vizier who does not sleep loses his ability to think. Sleep is wisdom!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-ahamm: an-nawm! Al-wazeer alladhii laa yanaam yafqid qudratahu 'alaa at-tafkiir. An-nawm 'aql!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَدلُ أَساسُ المُلك — هَذا مَبدَأ الحُكم
lines.english: Justice is the foundation of rule — this is the principle of governance.
lines.transliteration: al-'adl asaas al-mulk — haadha mabda' al-hukm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قاضٍ — القاضي يَحكُم بِالعَدل. وَكَلِمَة "cadi" الإنجليزِيَّة مِنها
lines.english: Qaadi — the judge rules with justice. The English "cadi" comes from this word.
lines.transliteration: qaadin — al-qaadi yahkum bil-'adl

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في بَغداد العَبّاسِيَّة كانَ القُضاة مُستَقِلِّين — نِظام قانوني عَادِل
lines.english: In Abbasid Baghdad, judges were independent — a fair legal system.
lines.transliteration: fii baghdaad al-'abbaasiyya kaana al-qudaat mustaqilliin

choices.arabic: العَدل قَبلَ كُلّ شَيء! شُكراً وَزير
choices.english: Justice above all! Thank you, vizier.

personality.catchphrase: بِأَمرِ المَلِك — bi-amr al-malik (By the king's command)

name: Princess Aisha
role: Teaches family vocabulary

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! يُسْعِدُنِي لِقاؤُكَ فِي قَصْرِنا
greeting.english: Welcome! I am delighted to meet you in our palace
greeting.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! yus'idunii liqaa'uka fii qasrinaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الأَمِيرَةُ عائِشَة. سَمِعْتُ عَنْ رِحْلَتِكَ الطَّوِيلَة
lines.english: I am Princess Aisha. I have heard about your long journey.
lines.transliteration: ana al-amiiratu aa'isha. sami'tu an rihlatika at-tawiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ اللَّه! لَقَدْ تَعَلَّمْتَ كَثِيراً فِي طَرِيقِكَ إِلى هُنا
lines.english: Mashallah! You have learned so much on your way here.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah! laqad ta'allamta kathiiran fii tariiqika ilaa hunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُحِبُّ الشِّعْرَ وَالعائِلَة. دَعْنِي أُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِماتِ العائِلَة
lines.english: I love poetry and family. Let me teach you family words.
lines.transliteration: uhibbu ash-shi'ra wal-aa'ila. da'nii u'allimuka kalimaat al-aa'ila

choices.english: Tell me about the royal family

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العائِلَةُ هِيَ أَساسُ كُلِّ شَيْء. لِنَبْدَأ بِالوالِدَيْن
lines.english: Family is the foundation of everything. Let's start with the parents.
lines.transliteration: al-aa'ilatu hiya asaasu kulli shay'. linabda' bil-waalidayn

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبٌ — الوالِدُ، رَأْسُ العائِلَة
lines.english: Ab — the father, head of the family.
lines.transliteration: ab — al-waalid, ra'su al-aa'ila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُمّ — الوالِدَة، قَلْبُ البَيْت
lines.english: Umm — the mother, heart of the home.
lines.transliteration: umm — al-waalida, qalbu al-bayt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخٌ — مِثْلَ أَخِي الَّذِي يَحْمِينِي
lines.english: Akh — like my brother who protects me.
lines.transliteration: akh — mithla akhii alladhii yahmiinii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل حَفِظْتَ هَذِهِ الكَلِمات؟ لِنَرَ!
lines.english: Did you memorize these words? Let's see!
lines.transliteration: hal hafizta haadhihi al-kalimaat? linara!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَوْدَةٌ جَمِيلَة! لَدَيَّ كَلِماتٌ أُخرى عَنِ العائِلَة
lines.english: A beautiful return! I have more family words for you.
lines.transliteration: awdatun jamiila! ladayya kalimaatun ukhraa an al-aa'ila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُخْت — مِثْلِي أَنا لِأَخِي
lines.english: Ukht — like me to my brother.
lines.transliteration: ukht — mithlii ana li-akhii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِبْن — الوَلَدُ لِأَبِيه
lines.english: Ibn — the son to his father.
lines.transliteration: ibn — al-waladu li-abiih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِنْت — البِنْتُ لِأُمِّها
lines.english: Bint — the daughter to her mother.
lines.transliteration: bint — al-bintu li-ummihaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طِفْل — الصَّغِيرُ فِي العائِلَة
lines.english: Tifl — the little one in the family.
lines.transliteration: tifl — as-saghiiru fil-aa'ila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَخْتَبِر ما تَعَلَّمْتَ!
lines.english: Let's test what you've learned!
lines.transliteration: linakhtabir maa ta'allamta!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ اللَّه، أَنْتَ تَعْرِفُ كَلِماتٍ كَثِيرَة! لَدَيَّ المَزِيد
lines.english: Mashallah, you know many words! I have more.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'allaah, anta ta'rifu kalimaatin kathiira! ladayya al-maziid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَدّ — والِدُ أَبِيكَ أَوْ أُمِّكَ
lines.english: Jadd — your father's or mother's father.
lines.transliteration: jadd — waalidu abiika aw ummika

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَدَّة — والِدَةُ أَبِيكَ أَوْ أُمِّكَ
lines.english: Jadda — your father's or mother's mother.
lines.transliteration: jadda — waalidatu abiika aw ummika

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَوْج — الرَّجُلُ المُتَزَوِّج
lines.english: Zawj — the married man, the husband.
lines.transliteration: zawj — ar-rajulu al-mutazawwij

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَوْجَة — المَرْأَةُ المُتَزَوِّجَة
lines.english: Zawja — the married woman, the wife.
lines.transliteration: zawja — al-mar'atu al-mutazawwija

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ كَلِماتُ الرَّوابِطِ العائِلِيَّة. هَل تَذْكُرُها؟
lines.english: These are the words of family bonds. Do you remember them?
lines.transliteration: haadhihi kalimaatu ar-rawaabit al-aa'iliyya. hal tadhkuruhaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عائِلَتُنا المَلَكِيَّةُ تَحْكُمُ هَذِهِ المَدِينَةَ مُنْذُ أَجْيال
lines.english: Our royal family has ruled this city for generations.
lines.transliteration: aa'ilatunaa al-malakiyya tahkumu haadhihi al-madiinata mundhu ajyaal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبِي المَلِكُ يَقُولُ: العِلْمُ أَغْلى مِنَ الذَّهَب
lines.english: My father the King says: knowledge is more precious than gold.
lines.transliteration: abii al-maliku yaquul: al-ilmu aghlaa min adh-dhahab

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِهَذا نُرَحِّبُ بِكُلِّ طالِبِ عِلْمٍ فِي قَصْرِنا
lines.english: That is why we welcome every seeker of knowledge in our palace.
lines.transliteration: li-haadha nurahhibu bikulli taalib ilmin fii qasrinaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً وَسَهلاً في القَصر
lines.english: Welcome to the palace.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan fii al-qasr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في القَصر نَتَكَلَّم بِلُغَة رَسمِيَّة
lines.english: In the palace we speak formal language.
lines.transliteration: fii al-qasr natakallam bilugha rasmiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَباح — أَوَّل الكَلِمات في البَلاط
lines.english: Morning — the first word in the court.
lines.transliteration: sabaah — awwal al-kalimaat fii al-balaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَساء — وَقت العَشاء المَلَكي
lines.english: Evening — time for the royal dinner.
lines.transliteration: masaa' — waqt al-'ashaa' al-malakii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ صَباح نَقرَأ القُرآن مَعاً
lines.english: Every morning we read the Quran together.
lines.transliteration: kulla sabaah naqra' al-qur'aan ma'an

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَبَعدَ الظُّهر دُروس في اللُّغات والتّاريخ
lines.english: And after noon, lessons in languages and history.
lines.transliteration: wa ba'da az-zuhr duruus fii al-lughaat wat-taariikh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُحِبّ أَن أَتَعَلَّم عَن الشُّعوب الأُخرى
lines.english: I love learning about other peoples.
lines.transliteration: uhibbu an ata'allam 'an ash-shu'uub al-ukhraa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُريدُ أَن أُسافِر لَكِن أَبي يَقلَق
lines.english: I want to travel but my father worries.
lines.transliteration: uriidu an usaafir laakinn abii yaqlaq

lines.speaker: npc
