lines.arabic: الوَزير عَبّاس دائِماً يُراقِبُني
lines.english: Vizier Abbas always watches me.
lines.transliteration: al-waziir 'abbaas daa'iman yuraaqibunii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحتاج مَن يُوصِل رِسالَة إِلى المَكتَبَة
lines.english: I need someone to deliver a message to the library.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaj man yuusil risaala ilaa al-maktaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل يُمكِنُك مُساعَدَتي؟
lines.english: Can you help me?
lines.transliteration: hal yumkinuk musaa'adatii?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فاطِمَةُ الفِهريَّة أَسَّسَت أَقدَمَ جامِعَةٍ في العالَم
lines.english: Fatima al-Fihri founded the oldest university in the world
lines.transliteration: fatima al-fihriyya assasat aqdam jami'a fil-'alam
lines.culturalNote: Fatima al-Fihri founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco in 859 CE. UNESCO and Guinness World Records recognize it as the oldest continuously operating educational institution.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشّاعِراتُ العَرَبيّاتُ كَتَبنَ شِعراً يَفوقُ كَثيراً مِنَ الرِّجال
lines.english: Arab women poets wrote verse surpassing many men
lines.transliteration: ash-sha'irat al-arabiyyat katabna shi'ran yafuqu kathiran min ar-rijal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَشَهرَزاد — أَقوى شَخصيَّةٍ أَدَبيَّة: أَنقَذَت حَياتَها بالقِصَص
lines.english: And Scheherazade — the most powerful literary character: she saved her life through stories
lines.transliteration: wa shahrazad — aqwa shakhsiyya adabiyya: anqadhat hayataha bil-qisas
lines.culturalNote: In One Thousand and One Nights, Scheherazade tells stories for 1,001 nights to delay her execution. She represents the power of narrative — stories as survival.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَتَعرِف فَاطِمَة الفِهرِيَّة؟ مَرَأَة مُسلِمَة أَسَّسَت أَقدَم جَامِعَة في العَالَم!
lines.english: Do you know Fatima al-Fihri? A Muslim woman who founded the oldest university in the world!
lines.transliteration: Ata'rif Faatima al-Fihriyya? Imra'a muslima assasat aqdam jaami'a fil-'aalam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَامِعَة القَرَوِيِّين في فَاس، المَغرِب — عَام 859 مِيلادِيّ. اليونِسكو تَعتَرِف بِها كَأَقدَم جَامِعَة!
lines.english: Al-Qarawiyyin University in Fez, Morocco — 859 CE. UNESCO recognizes it as the oldest university!
lines.transliteration: Jaami'at al-Qarawiyyiin fii Faas, al-Maghrib — 'aam 859 miilaadiiyy. Al-Yuunisku ta'tarif bihaa ka-aqdam jaami'a!
lines.culturalNote: Fatima al-Fihri founded al-Qarawiyyin University in Fez, Morocco in 859 CE — recognized by UNESCO and Guinness World Records as the world's oldest continuously operating educational institution. She used her entire inheritance to build it.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَلُبنى القُرطُبِيَّة — رِيَاضِيَّة وَشَاعِرَة وَمَكتَبِيَّة في بَلاط قُرطُبَة. امرَأَة عَظيمَة!
lines.english: And Lubna of Cordoba — mathematician, poet, and librarian in the Cordoba court. A great woman!
lines.transliteration: Wa Lubna al-Qurtubiyya — riyaadiyya wa shaа'ira wa maktabiyya fii balaat Qurtuba. Imra'a 'aziima!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الأُمّ — لِأَنَّ فَاطِمَة الفِهرِيَّة كَانَت أُمَّ التَّعلِيم الإِسلَامِيّ!
lines.english: Learn: mother — because Fatima al-Fihri was the mother of Islamic education!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-umm — li-anna Faatima al-Fihriyya kaanat umm at-ta'liim al-islaamiyy!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَائِلَة — أَهَمُّ مَؤسَّسَة في الحَضَارَة الإِسلَامِيَّة. كُلُّ شَيء يَبدَأ مِن البَيت!
lines.english: Family — the most important institution in Islamic civilization. Everything begins from the home!
lines.transliteration: Al-'aa'ila — ahamm mu'assasa fil-hadaara al-islaamiyya. Kull shay' yabda' min al-bayt!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَب! أَوَّل كَلِمَة تَعلَّمَها كُلُّ طِفل في كُلِّ لُغَة!
lines.english: The father! The first word every child learns in every language!
lines.transliteration: Al-ab! Awwal kalima ta'allamahaa kull tifl fii kulli lugha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَخ! الأَخوَّة في الإِسلَام تَمتَدُّ لِتَشمَل كُلَّ مُسلِم — لِتَكن أَخاً لِلجَميع!
lines.english: The brother! Brotherhood in Islam extends to include every Muslim — be a brother to all!
lines.transliteration: Al-akh! Al-ukhuwwa fil-islaam tamtaddu li-tashmila kull muslim — liyakun akhaan lil-jamii'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأُخت! وَالنِّسَاء في الإِسلَام كانَ لَهُنَّ حُقوق قَبلَ أُوروبَّا بِألف سَنَة!
lines.english: The sister! And women in Islam had rights a thousand years before Europe!
lines.transliteration: Al-ukht! Wa an-nisaa' fil-islaam kaana lahunna huquuq qabla Uurubba bi-alf sana!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! تَعلَّمتَ العَائِلَة. بِدُونَ عَائِلَة لا حَضَارَة — تَذكَّر هَذا دَائِماً!
lines.english: Well done! You learned family. Without family there is no civilization — remember this always!
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Ta'allamta al-'aa'ila. Bi-duun 'aa'ila laa hadaara — tadhakkar haadha daa'iman!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَتَعَلَّم الرِّيَاضِيَّات والفَلسَفَة والشِّعر! لِمَاذَا تَتَعَجَّب؟
lines.english: I am studying mathematics, philosophy, and poetry! Why are you surprised?
lines.transliteration: Ana ata'allam ar-riyaadiyaat wal-falsafa wash-shi'r! Li-maadha tata'ajjab?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في زَمَن الحَضَارَة الإِسلَامِيَّة، النِّسَاء كُنَّ عَالِمَات وَشَاعِرَات وَطَبيبَات!
lines.english: In the age of Islamic civilization, women were scholars, poets, and physicians!
lines.transliteration: Fii zaman al-hadaara al-islaamiyya, an-nisaa' kunna 'aalimaat wa shaа'iraat wa tabibaat!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلم لا جِنس لَه وَلا لَون. هَذَا ما أَقوله وَمَا تُؤكِّدُه التَّارِيخ!
lines.english: Knowledge has no gender and no color. This is what I say and what history confirms!
lines.transliteration: Al-'ilm laa jins lahu wa laa lawn. Haadha maa aquuluh wa maa tu'akkiduh at-taariikh!
lines.culturalNote: Lubna of Cordoba (d. 984 CE) was a renowned mathematician and librarian who managed the royal library of Caliph al-Hakam II — a collection of 400,000 volumes. She was his personal secretary and one of the leading intellectuals of 10th-century Spain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: جَديد — لِأَنَّ كُلَّ فِكرَة جَديدَة تَفتَح بَاباً جَديداً!
lines.english: Learn: new — because every new idea opens a new door!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: jadiid — li-anna kull fikra jadiida taftah baaban jadiiidan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف أَنَّ النِّساء العَرَبِيّات كُنَّ عالِمات كَبيرات؟
lines.english: Did you know that Arab women were great scholars?
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rif anna an-nisaa' al-arabiyyaat kunna 'aalimaat kabiraat?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خَيزُران — أُمّ هارون الرَّشيد — كانَت مِن أَقوَى النِّساء في التّاريخ
lines.english: Khayzuran — mother of Harun al-Rashid — was one of the most powerful women in history.
lines.transliteration: khayzuraan — umm haaroon ar-rashiid — kaanat min aqwaa an-nisaa' fit-taariikh
lines.culturalNote: Khayzuran (d. 789 CE), mother of Harun al-Rashid, wielded enormous political power in the Abbasid caliphate. Lubna of Cordoba (d. 984) ran the royal library of 400,000 volumes. Fatima al-Fihri (d. 880) founded al-Qarawiyyin — the world's oldest continuously operating university.

personality.catchphrase: بِإِذنِ الله وَبِقُوَّة المَعرِفَة — bi-idhn allaah wa bi-quwwat al-ma'rifa (By God's permission and the power of knowledge)

name: Poet Rumi
role: Teaches colors and beautiful adjectives

greeting.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكَ يا مُسافِر. الجَمالُ فِي كُلِّ مَكان
greeting.english: Peace be upon you, traveler. Beauty is everywhere
greeting.transliteration: as-salaamu alayka ya musaafir. al-jamaalu fii kulli makaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الشّاعِرُ الرُّومِيّ. أَرى العالَمَ بِالأَلْوانِ وَالكَلِمات
lines.english: I am the Poet Rumi. I see the world in colors and words.
lines.transliteration: ana ash-shaa'iru ar-ruumiyy. araa al-aalama bil-alwaani wal-kalimaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رِحْلَتُكَ كانَتْ طَوِيلَة، لَكِنَّ كُلَّ خُطْوَةٍ رَسَمَتْ لَوْناً فِي قَلْبِكَ
lines.english: Your journey was long, but every step painted a color in your heart.
lines.transliteration: rihlatuka kaanat tawiila, laakinna kulla khutwatin rasamat lawnan fii qalbika

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دَعْنِي أُعَلِّمُكَ أَلْوانَ القَصْر — فَهِيَ أَلْوانُ الحَياة
lines.english: Let me teach you the colors of the palace — they are the colors of life.
lines.transliteration: da'nii u'allimuka alwaan al-qasr — fahiya alwaanu al-hayaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَلْوانُ هِيَ لُغَةُ الرُّوح. اِسْمَعْ وَتَعَلَّمْ
lines.english: Colors are the language of the soul. Listen and learn.
lines.transliteration: al-alwaanu hiya lughatu ar-ruuh. isma' wa ta'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بُرْتُقالِيّ — كَلَوْنِ الشَّمْسِ عِنْدَ الغُرُوب
lines.english: Burtuqaaliyy — like the color of the sun at sunset.
lines.transliteration: burtuqaaliyy — kalawni ash-shamsi inda al-ghuruub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَرْدِيّ — كَلَوْنِ الوَرْدِ فِي حَدِيقَةِ القَصْر
lines.english: Wardiyy — like the color of roses in the palace garden.
lines.transliteration: wardiyy — kalawni al-wardi fii hadiiqati al-qasr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَنَفْسَجِيّ — كَلَوْنِ السَّماءِ بَعْدَ المَغْرِب
lines.english: Banafsajiyy — like the color of the sky after sunset.
lines.transliteration: banafsajiyy — kalawni as-samaa'i ba'da al-maghrib

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الآنَ أَخْبِرْنِي: هَلْ حَفِظَ قَلْبُكَ هَذِهِ الأَلْوان؟
lines.english: Now tell me: has your heart memorized these colors?
lines.transliteration: al-aana akhbirnii: hal hafiza qalbuka haadhihi al-alwaan?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدْتَ! كَالقَمَرِ الَّذِي يَعُودُ كُلَّ لَيْلَة. لَدَيَّ أَلْوانٌ وَصِفاتٌ جَدِيدَة
lines.english: You returned! Like the moon that returns every night. I have new colors and descriptions.
lines.transliteration: udta! kal-qamari alladhii ya'uudu kulla layla. ladayya alwaanun wa sifaatun jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بُنِّيّ — كَلَوْنِ الأَرْضِ الطَّيِّبَة
lines.english: Bunniyy — like the color of the good earth.
lines.transliteration: bunniyy — kalawni al-ardi at-tayyiba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَمادِيّ — كَلَوْنِ الغُيُومِ قَبْلَ المَطَر
lines.english: Ramaadiyy — like the color of clouds before rain.
lines.transliteration: ramaadiyy — kalawni al-ghuyuumi qabla al-matar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَمِيلٌ — وَهَذا ما أَراهُ فِي كُلِّ شَيْء
lines.english: Jamiil — and this is what I see in everything.
lines.transliteration: jamiil — wa haadha maa araahu fii kulli shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَبِيحٌ — عَكْسُ الجَمال، لَكِنَّ الشّاعِرَ يَرى الجَمالَ حَتّى فِيه
lines.english: Qabiih — the opposite of beauty, but a poet sees beauty even in it.
lines.transliteration: qabiih — aksu al-jamaal, laakinna ash-shaa'ira yaraa al-jamaala hattaa fiih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَتَذَكَّرَ هَذِهِ الكَلِمات؟
lines.english: Can you remember these words?
lines.transliteration: hal tastatiiu an tatadkakkara haadhihi al-kalimaat?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنْتَ الآنَ كَالنَّهْرِ الَّذِي يَعْرِفُ طَرِيقَهُ. لَدَيَّ كَلِماتٌ مِنَ القَلْب
lines.english: You are now like a river that knows its path. I have words from the heart.
lines.transliteration: anta al-aana kan-nahri alladhii ya'rifu tariiqahu. ladayya kalimaatun min al-qalb

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَعِيدٌ — كَالشَّمْسِ عِنْدَما تُشْرِق
lines.english: Sa'iid — like the sun when it rises.
lines.transliteration: sa'iid — kash-shamsi indamaa tushriq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَزِينٌ — كَالمَطَرِ الَّذِي يَبْكِي عَلى الأَرْض
lines.english: Haziiin — like the rain that cries upon the earth.
lines.transliteration: haziiin — kal-matari alladhii yabkii alaa al-ard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَبِيرٌ — كَالحُلْمِ الَّذِي لا يَنْتَهِي
lines.english: Kabiir — like a dream that never ends.
lines.transliteration: kabiir — kal-hulmi alladhii laa yantahii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ كَلِماتٌ تَعَلَّمْتَها فِي رِحْلَتِكَ. هَل ما زِلْتَ تَذْكُرُها؟
lines.english: These are words you learned on your journey. Do you still remember them?
lines.transliteration: haadhihi kalimaatun ta'allamtahaa fii rihlatika. hal maa zilta tadhkuruhaa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِسْمَعْ يا صَدِيقِي:
lines.english: Listen, my friend:
lines.transliteration: isma' ya sadiiqii:

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سافَرْتَ بَعِيداً وَتَعَلَّمْتَ كَثِيراً
lines.english: You traveled far and learned much,
lines.transliteration: saafarta ba'iidan wa ta'allamta kathiiran

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ نُورٌ، وَكُلُّ حَرْفٍ طَرِيق
lines.english: Every word is a light, and every letter is a path.
lines.transliteration: kullu kalimatin nuur, wa kullu harfin tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَللُّغَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ بَحْرٌ عَمِيق، وَأَنْتَ غَوّاصٌ شُجاع
lines.english: The Arabic language is a deep sea, and you are a brave diver.
lines.transliteration: al-lughatu al-arabiyyatu bahrun amiiq, wa anta ghawwaasun shujaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكَلِمَة نور! أَهلاً بِصَديق الشِّعر
lines.english: The word is light! Welcome, friend of poetry.
lines.transliteration: al-kalima nuur! ahlan bisadiiq ash-shi'r

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصِّفاتُ هِيَ أَلوان اللُّغَة
lines.english: Adjectives are the colors of language.
lines.transliteration: as-sifaatu hiya alwaan al-lugha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحْمَر — لَونُ الوَردَة في الحَديقَة
lines.english: Red — the color of the rose in the garden.
lines.transliteration: ahmar — lawnu al-warda fii al-hadiiqa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخْضَر — لَونُ الأَشجار وَالأَمَل
lines.english: Green — the color of trees and hope.
lines.transliteration: akhdar — lawnu al-ashjaar wal-amal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَزْرَق — لَونُ السَّماء الَّتي تُلهِمُني
lines.english: Blue — the color of the sky that inspires me.
lines.transliteration: azraq — lawnu as-samaa' allatii tulhimunii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشِّعرُ العَرَبي أَقدَم مِن الكِتابَة
lines.english: Arabic poetry is older than writing itself.
lines.transliteration: ash-shi'r al-'arabii aqdam min al-kitaaba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُعَلَّقاتُ السَّبع كانَت تُعَلَّق عَلى الكَعبَة
lines.english: The Seven Mu'allaqat were hung on the Kaaba.
lines.transliteration: al-mu'allaqaat as-sab' kaanat tu'allaq 'alaa al-ka'ba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ بَيت شِعر هُوَ نافِذَة إِلى الرّوح
lines.english: Every verse of poetry is a window to the soul.
lines.transliteration: kullu bayt shi'r huwa naafidha ilaa ar-ruuh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيلى حارِسَة الحَديقَة تُحِبّ الشِّعر سِرّاً
lines.english: Leila the garden keeper secretly loves poetry.
lines.transliteration: laylaa haarisat al-hadiiqa tuhibb ash-shi'r sirran

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَنا أَكتُب قَصيدَة لِلمَلِك — لَكِن لا تُخبِر أَحَداً
lines.english: And I am writing a poem for the king — but tell no one.
lines.transliteration: wa ana aktub qasiida lil-malik — laakin laa tukhbir ahadan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَصيدَةُ العَرَبيَّة لَها قَوافٍ مُعَقَّدَة — البَحرُ الطَّويل، الكامِل، الوافِر
lines.english: Arabic poetry has complex meters — Tawil, Kamil, Wafir
lines.transliteration: al-qasida al-arabiyya laha qawafi mu'aqqada — al-bahr at-tawil, al-kamil, al-wafir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نِظامُ الجُذورِ الثُّلاثيَّة يَجعَلُ التَّلاعُبَ بالأَلفاظِ فَنّاً
lines.english: The trilateral root system makes wordplay an art form
lines.transliteration: nizam al-judhur ath-thulathiyya yaj'al at-tala'ub bil-alfaz fannan
lines.culturalNote: Arabic's root system means a skilled poet can play with dozens of words sharing the same three-letter root, creating layers of meaning impossible in other languages.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخَطُّ العَرَبي نَفسُهُ شِعر — كُلُّ حَرفٍ رَقصَة
lines.english: Arabic calligraphy itself is poetry — every letter a dance
lines.transliteration: al-khatt al-arabi nafsuhu shi'r — kullu harf raqsa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس مَعِي. سَأُرِيكَ أَعجَب شَيء في اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة — الجُذور الثُّلَاثِيَّة!
lines.english: Sit with me. I will show you the most wondrous thing in Arabic — the trilateral roots!
lines.transliteration: Ijlis ma'i. Sa-uriika a'jab shay' fil-lugha al-'arabiyya — al-judhuур ath-thulaathiyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ك-ت-ب: ثَلاثَة حُروف فَقَط. لَكِن مِنها: كَتَبَ، كِتَاب، كَاتِب، مَكتَبَة، مَكتوب!
lines.english: K-T-B: only three letters. But from them: wrote, book, writer, library, written!
lines.transliteration: K-T-B: thalaathat huruuf faqat. Laakin minhaa: kataba, kitaab, kaatib, maktaba, maktуub!
lines.culturalNote: Arabic's trilateral root system means three consonants generate a whole family of related words. The root ك-ت-ب (K-T-B) gives: كَتَبَ (wrote), كِتَاب (book), كَاتِب (writer), مَكتَبَة (library), مَكتوب (written/fate). A skilled poet plays with all these at once.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشَّاعِر العَرَبي يَلعَب بِعَشَرَات الكَلِمَات مِن جَذرٍ وَاحِد في بَيتٍ وَاحِد!
lines.english: An Arab poet plays with dozens of words from one root in a single verse!
lines.transliteration: Ash-shaa'ir al-'arabiyy yal'ab bi-'asharaat al-kalimaat min jidhr waahid fii bayt waahid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: صَغير — لِأَنَّ الكَلِمَة الصَّغيرَة تَحمِل أَحياناً أَكبَر مَعنى!
lines.english: Learn: small — because the small word sometimes carries the biggest meaning!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: sagjiir — li-anna al-kalima as-saghiira tahmilu ahyaanan akbar ma'naa!

choices.english: Tell me about Arabic poetry forms

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشُّعور! أَعمَق مَا في الإِنسَان! الشَّاعِر يُعَبِّر عَمَّا لا يَستَطيع غَيرُه قَوله!
lines.english: Feelings! The deepest part of being human! The poet expresses what others cannot say!
lines.transliteration: Ash-shu'uur! A'maq maa fil-insaan! Ash-shaa'ir yu'abbir 'ammaa laa yastatiiu ghayruhu qawluh!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَعيد — أَجمَل كَلِمَة في كُلِّ اللُّغَات. تَقُولها وَتَشعُر بِها في نَفس الوَقت!
lines.english: Happy — the most beautiful word in all languages. You say it and feel it at the same time!
lines.transliteration: Sa'iid — ajmal kalima fii kulli al-lughaat. Taquuluhaa wa tash'ur bihaa fii nafs al-waqt!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَزين — ضِدُّ سَعيد. الشَّاعِر يَحتَاج كِلتَا الكَلِمَتَين لِيُعَبِّر عَن الحَيَاة!
lines.english: Sad — the opposite of happy. The poet needs both words to express life!
lines.transliteration: Haziiin — diddu sa'iid. Ash-shaa'ir yahtaaju kiltaa al-kalimatayn liyu'abbir 'an al-hayaah!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَميل وَقَبيح! نُور وَظَلام! الشِّعر يَعيش في المَسَافَة بَينَهُما!
lines.english: Beautiful and ugly! Light and dark! Poetry lives in the distance between them!
lines.transliteration: Jamiil wa qabiih! Nuur wa zalaam! Ash-shi'r ya'iish fil-masaafa baynahumaa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! أَنتَ الآن تَمتَلِك المُفرَدَات لِتُعَبِّر عَن نَفسِك. هَذا هُوَ بِداية الشِّعر!
lines.english: Well done! You now have the vocabulary to express yourself. This is the beginning of poetry!
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Anta al-aan tamtalik al-mufradaat litu'abbir 'an nafsik. Haadha huwa bidaayat ash-shi'r!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: القَصِيدَة العَرَبِيَّة! الشَّكل الشِّعرِيّ الأَعظَم. وَزن وَقَافِيَة وَمَعنى في آنٍ وَاحِد!
lines.english: The Arabic qasida! The greatest poetic form. Meter, rhyme, and meaning all at once!
lines.transliteration: Al-qasiida al-'arabiyya! Ash-shakl ash-shi'riyy al-a'zam. Wazn wa qaafiya wa ma'naa fii aanin waahid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِلم العَروض — عِلم أَوزَان الشِّعر. الخَليل بن أَحمَد وَضَعَه في القَرن الثَّامِن!
lines.english: The science of arood — the science of poetic meters. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad established it in the 8th century!
lines.transliteration: Ilm al-'aruud — 'ilm awzaan ash-shi'r. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad wada'ahu fil-qarn ath-thaamin!
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi (c.718-786 CE) systematized Arabic poetic meters (علم العروض, 'ilm al-'aruud), identifying 16 meters still used today. He also compiled the first Arabic dictionary. This mathematical approach to poetry is unique among world literary traditions.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشِّعر العَرَبيّ يَخدِم ذَاكِرَتَك — إِذَا حَفِظتَ شِعراً، حَفِظتَ اللُّغَة!
lines.english: Arabic poetry serves your memory — if you memorize poetry, you memorize the language!
lines.transliteration: Ash-shi'r al-'arabiyy yakhdim dhaakiratik — idhaa hafizta shi'ran, hafizta al-lugha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: صَعب — لِأَنَّ الشِّعر صَعبٌ وَلَكِن جَائِزَتُه أَعظَم جَائِزَة!
lines.english: Learn: difficult — because poetry is difficult but its reward is the greatest reward!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: sa'b — li-anna ash-shi'r sa'bun wa laakin jaa'izatuhu a'zam jaa'iza!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! الشِّعرُ يَنتَظِرُك. لِنَتَكَلَّم عَن الأَلفاظ
lines.english: You're back! Poetry awaits you. Let's talk about words.
lines.transliteration: 'udta! ash-shi'r yantaziruk. linatakallamm 'an al-alfaaz

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: "risk" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن العَرَبِيَّة "رِزق" — الرَّزق الَّذي يُقَسِّمُه الله
lines.english: The English "risk" came from Arabic "rizq" — the provision God distributes.
lines.transliteration: "risk" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-arabiyya "rizq"
lines.culturalNote: The English word "risk" traces to Arabic rizq (رِزق), meaning livelihood or God's provision. Arab traders in the medieval Mediterranean used it for the chance of maritime loss — European merchants adopted the term along with the trade practices.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"check" في البَنك جاءَت مِن "صَكّ" العَرَبِيَّة — وَثيقَة مالِيَّة
lines.english: And bank "check" came from Arabic "sakk" — a financial document.
lines.transliteration: wa "check" fil-bank jaa'at min "sakk" al-arabiyya — wathiiqa maaliyya

choices.english: Words travel like us! Thank you.

personality.catchphrase: الكَلِمَة نور — al-kalima nuur (The word is light)

name: Imam Muhammad
role: Teaches verbs of knowledge and final review phrases

greeting.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ. أَهْلاً بِطالِبِ العِلْم
greeting.english: In the name of God. Welcome, seeker of knowledge
greeting.transliteration: bismillaah. ahlan bi-taalib al-ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الإِمامُ مُحَمَّد، أُعَلِّمُ فِي مَكْتَبَةِ القَصْر
lines.english: I am Imam Muhammad. I teach in the palace library.
lines.transliteration: ana al-imaamu muhammad, u'allimu fii maktabati al-qasr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمِعْتُ أَنَّكَ قَطَعْتَ رِحْلَةً طَوِيلَةً لِتَصِلَ إِلى هُنا
lines.english: I heard that you made a long journey to reach here.
lines.transliteration: sami'tu annaka qata'ta rihlatan tawiila litasila ilaa hunaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَلْعِلْمُ نُورٌ. وَأَنتَ حَمَلْتَ هَذا النُّورَ مَعَكَ طُولَ الطَّرِيق
lines.english: Knowledge is light. And you have carried this light with you the whole way.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu nuur. wa anta hamalta haadha an-nuura ma'aka tuula at-tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دَعْنِي أُعَلِّمُكَ أَفْعالَ العِلْمِ — أَهَمُّ الأَفْعالِ فِي حَياتِنا
lines.english: Let me teach you the verbs of knowledge — the most important verbs in our lives.
lines.transliteration: da'nii u'allimuka af'aala al-ilmi — ahammu al-af'aali fii hayaatinaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّه. لِنَبْدَأ بِأَفْعالِ العِلْم
lines.english: In the name of God. Let us begin with the verbs of knowledge.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah. linabda' bi-af'aali al-ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَرَأَ — أَوَّلُ كَلِمَةٍ نَزَلَتْ مِنَ السَّماء
lines.english: Qara'a — the first word that came down from the heavens.
lines.transliteration: qara'a — awwalu kalimatin nazalat min as-samaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَتَبَ — بِالقَلَمِ يُحْفَظُ العِلْم
lines.english: Kataba — with the pen, knowledge is preserved.
lines.transliteration: kataba — bil-qalami yuhfazu al-ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّمَ — وَهَذا ما تَفْعَلُهُ أَنتَ الآن
lines.english: Ta'allama — and this is what you are doing right now.
lines.transliteration: ta'allama — wa haadha maa taf'aluhu anta al-aan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ أَساسُ كُلِّ عِلْم. لِنَرَ إِنْ فَهِمْتَ
lines.english: These are the foundation of all knowledge. Let us see if you understood.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi asaasu kulli ilm. linara in fahimta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّه، عُدْتَ لِلتَّعَلُّم. لَدَيَّ أَفْعالٌ جَدِيدَة
lines.english: Thank God, you returned to learn. I have new verbs.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah, udta lit-ta'allum. ladayya af'aalun jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَرَفَ — العِلْمُ يَبْدَأُ بِالمَعْرِفَة
lines.english: Arafa — knowledge begins with knowing.
lines.transliteration: arafa — al-ilmu yabda'u bil-ma'rifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَعْطى — خَيْرُ النّاسِ مَنْ يُعْطِي
lines.english: A'taa — the best of people are those who give.
lines.transliteration: a'taa — khayru an-naasi man yu'tii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ساعَدَ — وَالمُؤْمِنُ يُساعِدُ أَخاه
lines.english: Saa'ada — and the believer helps his brother.
lines.transliteration: saa'ada — wal-mu'minu yusaa'idu akhaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَمِلَ — فَالعَمَلُ عِبادَة
lines.english: Amila — for work is worship.
lines.transliteration: amila — fal-amalu ibaada

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَسَنٌ. لِنَخْتَبِرْ هَذِهِ الأَفْعال
lines.english: Good. Let us test these verbs.
lines.transliteration: hasanun. linakhtabir haadhihi al-af'aal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا بُنَيَّ، هَذا هُوَ دَرْسُكَ الأَخِير
lines.english: My child, this is your final lesson.
lines.transliteration: ya bunayya, haadha huwa darsuka al-akhiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَقَدْ تَعَلَّمْتَ الكَثِير. مِنَ الحُرُوفِ إِلى الكَلِماتِ إِلى الجُمَل
lines.english: You have learned so much. From letters to words to sentences.
lines.transliteration: laqad ta'allamta al-kathiir. min al-huruufi ilaa al-kalimaati ilaa al-jumal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ — قُلْها دائِماً عِنْدَ النِّعْمَة
lines.english: Alhamdulillah — say it always when blessed.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah — qulhaa daa'iman inda an-ni'ma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَعَ السَّلامَةِ — لِلوَداع
lines.english: Ma'a as-salaama — for farewell.
lines.transliteration: ma'a as-salaama — lil-wadaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَراكَ لاحِقاً — فَالعِلْمُ لا يَنْتَهِي
lines.english: Araaka laahiqan — for knowledge never ends.
lines.transliteration: araaka laahiqan — fal-ilmu laa yantahii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا لَيْسَ نِهايَةَ رِحْلَتِكَ. هَذِهِ بِدايَةٌ جَدِيدَة. اِخْتِبارٌ أَخِير!
lines.english: This is not the end of your journey. This is a new beginning. One final test!
lines.transliteration: haadha laysa nihaayata rihlatika. haadhihi bidaayatun jadiida. ikhtibaarun akhiir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَكْتَبَةُ فِيها آلافُ الكُتُبِ بِالعَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: This library contains thousands of books in Arabic.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-maktabatu fiihaa aalaaf al-kutubi bil-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَنْ يَقْرَأُ يَفْتَحُ أَبْوابَ العالَم
lines.english: Whoever reads opens the doors of the world.
lines.transliteration: man yaqra'u yaftahu abwaab al-aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ كِتابٍ هُنا كَنْزٌ. وَأَنتَ الآنَ تَمْلِكُ المِفْتاحَ — اللُّغَةَ العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Every book here is a treasure. And you now hold the key — the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: kullu kitaabin hunaa kanzun. wa anta al-aana tamliku al-miftaaha — al-lughata al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمدُ لِلَّه. مَرحَباً يا بُنَيّ
lines.english: Praise be to God. Welcome, my child.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah. marhaban ya bunayy

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الوَقتُ نِعمَة مِن الله. لِنَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: Time is a blessing from God. Let us learn.
lines.transliteration: al-waqtu ni'ma min allaah. linata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَوْم — كُلّ يَوم فيهِ خَمس صَلَوات
lines.english: Day — every day has five prayers.
lines.transliteration: yawm — kullu yawm fiihi khams salawaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيْل — وَقتُ السُّكون وَالتَّأَمُّل
lines.english: Night — a time of stillness and reflection.
lines.transliteration: layl — waqtu as-sukuun wat-ta'ammul

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَباح — وَقتُ صَلاة الفَجر
lines.english: Morning — time for the dawn prayer.
lines.transliteration: sabaah — waqtu salaat al-fajr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَسجِد هُوَ قَلبُ القَريَة
lines.english: The mosque is the heart of the village.
lines.transliteration: al-masjid huwa qalbu al-qarya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا نُصَلّي وَنَتَعَلَّم وَنَجتَمِع
lines.english: Here we pray, learn, and gather.
lines.transliteration: hunaa nusallii wa nata'allam wa najtami'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ فَريضَة عَلى كُلّ مُسلِم
lines.english: Knowledge is an obligation for every Muslim.
lines.transliteration: al-'ilmu fariida 'alaa kulli muslim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُزارِع عُمَر يَحتاج مُساعَدَة في الحَصاد
lines.english: Farmer Omar needs help with the harvest.
lines.transliteration: al-muzaari' 'umar yahtaaj musaa'ada fii al-hasaad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالشَّيخ يوسُف يُعِدّ دَرساً جَديداً
lines.english: And Sheikh Yusuf is preparing a new lesson.
lines.transliteration: wash-shaykh yuusuf yu'idd darsan jadiidan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّجويدُ حَفِظَ النُّطقَ العَرَبيَّ لِأَكثَرَ مِن أَلفِ عام
lines.english: Tajweed preserved Arabic pronunciation for over a thousand years
lines.transliteration: at-tajwid hafiza an-nutq al-arabi li-akthar min alf 'am
lines.culturalNote: Tajweed (تجويد) is the science of Quranic recitation. Its rules standardized Arabic pronunciation so precisely that Classical Arabic sounds almost identical today to how it sounded in the 7th century.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَفهومُ الفَصاحَة — البَلاغَةُ هِيَ أَعلى فُنونِ اللُّغَة
lines.english: The concept of fasaha — eloquence is the highest art of language
lines.transliteration: mafhum al-fasaha — al-balagha hiya a'la funun al-lugha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبيَّةُ لُغَةُ الضّاد — الحَرفُ الَّذي لا يوجَدُ في أَيِّ لُغَةٍ أُخرى
lines.english: Arabic is the language of Daad — a letter found in no other language
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya lughat ad-daad — al-harf alladhi la yujad fi ayy lugha ukhra
lines.culturalNote: Arabic is called 'lughat ad-Daad' (language of the Daad) because the letter ض is unique to Arabic — no other language has this exact sound.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً، يَا وَلَدي. هَل تَعرِف لِمَاذَا يُسمُّون العَرَبِيَّة "لُغَة الضَّاد"؟
lines.english: Welcome, my child. Do you know why Arabic is called "the language of the Daad"?
lines.transliteration: Ahlan, yaa waladii. Hal ta'rif li-maadha yusammun al-'arabiyya 'lughat ad-daad'?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَرف الضَّاد فَريد في اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة — لا يوجَد في أَيِّ لُغَة أُخرى بِنَفس الطَّريقَة!
lines.english: The letter Daad is unique to Arabic — it does not exist in any other language in the same way!
lines.transliteration: Harf ad-daad fariid fil-lugha al-'arabiyya — laa yujad fii ayyi lugha ukhraa bi-nafs at-tariqa!
lines.culturalNote: Arabic is called "Lughat ad-Daad" (لُغَة الضَّاد) — the language of the letter Daad — because this emphatic consonant is unique to Arabic. The science of tajweed (تَجويد) preserves the exact Quranic pronunciation as taught by the Prophet, creating an unbroken oral chain of 1,400 years.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِلم التَّجويد يَحفَظ النُّطق القُرآنِيَّ كَمَا عَلَّمَه النَّبيّ. سِلسِلَة لا تَنقَطِع!
lines.english: The science of tajweed preserves Quranic pronunciation as the Prophet taught it. An unbroken chain!
lines.transliteration: Ilm at-tajwiid yahfaz an-nutq al-qur'aaniyy kamaa 'allamahu an-Nabiyy. Silsila laa tanqati'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الصَّلاة — كَلِمَة تَربِط العَبد بِرَبِّه. خَمسَ مَرَّات كُلَّ يَوم!
lines.english: Learn: prayer — a word that connects the servant to his Lord. Five times every day!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: as-salaah — kalima tarbit al-'abd bi-rabbih. Khamsa marraat kull yawm!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسُرور، يَا وَلَدي. الكَلِمَات الدِّينِيَّة هِيَ أَساس اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة.
lines.english: With pleasure, my child. Religious words are the foundation of the Arabic language.
lines.transliteration: Bi-suruur, yaa waladii. Al-kalimaat ad-diiniyya hiya asaas al-lugha al-'arabiyya.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلام عَلَيكُم — أَعظَم تَحِيَّة. نَتَمَنَّى السَّلامَة لِبَعضِنا البَعض في كُلِّ لِقَاء!
lines.english: As-salaamu alaykum — the greatest greeting. We wish safety upon each other in every meeting!
lines.transliteration: As-salaamu 'alaykum — a'zam tahiyya. Natamanna as-salaama li-ba'dinaa al-ba'd fii kulli liqaa'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشُّكر — نِصف الإِيمَان. الشَّاكِر يَرى النِّعمَة في كُلِّ شَيء!
lines.english: Thanks — half of faith. The grateful one sees blessing in everything!
lines.transliteration: Ash-shukr — nisf al-iimaan. Ash-shaakir yaraa an-ni'ma fii kulli shay'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالصَّبر — أَعظَم فَضِيلَة. قَال الله: "إِنَّ اللهَ مَع الصَّابِرين".
lines.english: And patience — the greatest virtue. God said: "Indeed God is with the patient."
lines.transliteration: Was-sabr — a'zam fadiila. Qaala Allaah: 'Inna Allaaha ma'a as-saabirin'.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحسَنتَ! اللُّغَة والإِيمَان يَسيران مَعاً في الإِسلَام. تَعَلَّم اللُّغَة وَاِفهَم الدِّين أَعمَق.
lines.english: Well done! Language and faith walk together in Islam. Learn the language and understand religion more deeply.
lines.transliteration: Ahsanta! Al-lugha wal-iimaan yasiiraani ma'an fil-islaam. Ta'allam al-lugha wa ifham ad-diin a'maq.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: التَّجويد مِن "جَوَّد" — أَي أَحسَنَ وَأَتقَنَ. هُوَ عِلم إِتقَان النُّطق القُرآنِيّ.
lines.english: Tajweed is from "jawwada" — meaning to perfect and excel. It is the science of mastering Quranic recitation.
lines.transliteration: At-tajwiid min 'jawwada' — ay ahsana wa atqana. Huwa 'ilm itqaan an-nutq al-qur'aaniyy.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ حَرف لَه مَخرَج مُعَيَّن — مِن الحَلق أَو اللِّسَان أَو الشَّفَتَين. العِلم الدَّقيق!
lines.english: Every letter has a specific point of articulation — from the throat, tongue, or lips. A precise science!
lines.transliteration: Kullu harf lahu makhraj mu'ayyan — min al-halq aw al-lisaan aw ash-shafatayn. Al-'ilm ad-daqiiq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُقرِئون حَفِظوا النُّطق الأَصلِيَّ لِأَربَعَة عَشَر قَرناً — تَسَلسُل شَفَهِيّ مُذهِل!
lines.english: The Quran reciters preserved the original pronunciation for fourteen centuries — a remarkable oral chain!
lines.transliteration: Al-muqri'uun hafizuu an-nutq al-asliyy li-arba'ata 'ashar qarnan — tasalsul shafawiyy mudhil!
lines.culturalNote: "Allah" is the only word that uses every point of Arabic articulation — from the back of the throat to the lips. Quranic reciters train for years to perfect each sound. The science of tajweed has preserved Classical Arabic pronunciation unchanged since the 7th century CE.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: الصَّوت — لِأَنَّ الصَّوت الجَميل يَنفُذ إِلى القَلب قَبلَ المَعنى!
lines.english: Learn: the sound/voice — because a beautiful voice reaches the heart before meaning does!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: as-sawt — li-anna as-sawt al-jamiil yanfudh ilaa al-qalb qabla al-ma'naa!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً، يَا وَلَدي. كَيفَ حَالُكَ؟ هَل تَعَلَّمتَ كَلِمَات جَديدَة اليَوم؟
lines.english: Welcome, my child. How are you? Have you learned new words today?
lines.transliteration: Ahlan, yaa waladii. Kayfa haaluk? Hal ta'allamta kalimaat jadiida al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلُّم اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة عِبَادَة. كُلُّ كَلِمَة تَعلَّمتَها خَطوَة نَحو فَهم القُرآن.
lines.english: Learning Arabic is an act of worship. Every word you learn is a step toward understanding the Quran.
lines.transliteration: Ta'allum al-lugha al-'arabiyya 'ibaada. Kullu kalima ta'allamtahaa khatwa nahwa fahm al-qur'aan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: اليَوم — لِأَنَّ كُلَّ يَوم هُوَ فُرصَة جَديدَة لِلتَّعلُّم!
lines.english: Learn: today — because every day is a new opportunity to learn!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: al-yawm — li-anna kull yawm huwa fursa jadiida lit-ta'allum!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالغَد — لِأَنَّ ما لَم تَتَعلَّمه اليَوم، فَرصَتُكَ غَداً. لا تُؤَجِّل!
lines.english: And tomorrow — because what you did not learn today, there is your chance tomorrow. Do not delay!
lines.transliteration: Wa al-ghad — li-anna maa lam tata'allamhu al-yawm, fursat اُk ghadan. Laa tu'ajjil!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبِيَّة لُغَة الضَّاد — حَرف الضَّاد فَريد في العَرَبِيَّة وَحدَها
lines.english: Arabic is the language of the Daad — the Daad letter is unique to Arabic alone.
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya lughat ad-daad — harf ad-daad fariid fil-arabiyya wahdaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا تَوجَد في أَيّ لُغَة أُخرى — هَذا يَجعَل العَرَبِيَّة فَريدَة
lines.english: It exists in no other language — this makes Arabic unique.
lines.transliteration: laa tujad fii ayy lugha ukhraa — haadha yaj'al al-arabiyya fariida

choices.english: Language of the Daad! Proud to learn it.

personality.catchphrase: الحَمدُ لِلَّه — al-hamdu lillaah (Praise be to God)

name: Baker Yasmin
role: Teaches food vocabulary through baking

personality.catchphrase: بِسْمِ الله — bismillaah (In God's name)

greeting.arabic: أَهلاً! ريحَة الخُبز الطّازَج أَحلى شَيء
greeting.english: Hello! The smell of fresh bread is the sweetest thing.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan! riihat al-khubz at-taazaj ahlaa shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا ياسمين الخَبّازَة. مَرحَباً!
lines.english: I am Yasmin the baker. Welcome!
lines.transliteration: ana yasmiin al-khabbazza. marhaban!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخبُزُ مُنذُ طُفولَتي. الخُبزُ يَجمَع النّاس
lines.english: I have been baking since childhood. Bread brings people together.
lines.transliteration: akhbuzu mundhu tufuulatii. al-khubzu yajma' an-naas

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسْمِ الله! ماذا نَطبُخ اليَوم؟
lines.english: In God's name! What shall we cook today?
lines.transliteration: bismillaah! maadha natbukh al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَطبَخ مَدرَسَة! لِنَتَعَلَّم
lines.english: The kitchen is a school! Let us learn.
lines.transliteration: al-matbakh madrasa! linata'allam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرُزّ — نَأكُلُهُ مَع كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Rice — we eat it with everything.
lines.transliteration: aruzz — na'kuluhu ma' kulli shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: دَجاج — الطَّبَق المُفَضَّل في الواحَة
lines.english: Chicken — the favorite dish in the oasis.
lines.transliteration: dajaaj — at-tabaq al-mufaddal fii al-waaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُمّي عَلَّمَتني الخَبز وَأَنا صَغيرَة
lines.english: My mother taught me baking when I was little.
lines.transliteration: ummii 'allamatnii al-khabz wa ana saghiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في رَمَضان نَخبُز طُوال اللَّيل لِلجيران
lines.english: In Ramadan we bake all night for the neighbors.
lines.transliteration: fii ramadaan nakhbuz tuwaal al-layl lil-jiiraan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الإِمام مُحَمَّد يُحِبّ خُبزي بِالزَّعتَر
lines.english: Imam Muhammad loves my za'atar bread.
lines.transliteration: al-imaam muhammad yuhibb khubzii biz-za'tar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَالعَشّابَة خَديجَة تَطلُب خُبزاً بِدون مِلح
lines.english: And Herbalist Khadija orders bread without salt.
lines.transliteration: wal-'ashhaaba khadiija tatlub khubzan biduun milh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً ثانِيَة! اليَوم نَتَعَلَّم الحَلَويّات
lines.english: Welcome back! Today we learn sweets.
lines.transliteration: marhaban thaaniya! al-yawm nata'allam al-halawiyyaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سُكَّر — وَكَلِمَة "sugar" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن "sukkar" العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: Sukkar — sugar. The English word "sugar" came from Arabic "sukkar".
lines.transliteration: sukkar — wa kalima "sugar" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min "sukkar" al-arabiyya
lines.culturalNote: "Sugar" traces through Arabic sukkar (سُكَّر) from Sanskrit sharkara. Arab merchants introduced sugar refining to Europe in the medieval period. The word "candy" also comes from Arabic qand (قَنْد, crystallized sugar).

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَلوى — كُلّ شَيء حُلو! مِن "حَلال" وَ"حَلاوَة"
lines.english: Halwa — sweets! Related to halaal and halaawa (sweetness).
lines.transliteration: halwaa — kull shay' hulw! min "halaal" wa "halaawa"

choices.english: My tongue wants sweets now! Thank you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! الفُرن ساخِن وَعِندي دَرس جَديد
lines.english: Welcome again! The oven is hot and I have a new lesson.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marra thaaniya! al-furn saakhin wa 'indii dars jadiid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَهوَة — المَشروب المُقَدَّس في العالَم العَرَبي
lines.english: Qahwa — coffee, the sacred drink in the Arab world.
lines.transliteration: qahwa — al-mashrob al-muqaddas fil-'aalam al-'arabii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "coffee" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن "قَهوَة" العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: The English word "coffee" came from Arabic "qahwa".
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "coffee" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min "qahwa" al-arabiyya
lines.culturalNote: "Coffee" derives from Arabic qahwa (قَهوَة). Coffee originated in Ethiopia but Arab merchants popularized it worldwide from 15th century Yemen. The first coffeehouses (qahwakhaana) opened in Mecca around 1450 CE, creating the world's first "café culture".

choices.english: Now I want coffee! Thank you, Yasmin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف "رَمَضان"؟ شَهر الصِّيام وَالعَطاء
lines.english: Do you know "Ramadan"? The month of fasting and giving.
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rif "ramadaan"? shahr as-siyaam wal-'ataa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فِي رَمَضان نَأكُل "سُحور" قَبلَ الفَجر وَ"إِفطار" عِندَ الغُروب
lines.english: In Ramadan we eat "suhoor" before dawn and "iftar" at sunset.
lines.transliteration: fii ramadaan na'kul "suhoor" qabl al-fajr wa "iftaar" 'inda al-ghuroob

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "مُهمَّش" تَعني الحَرَكات فَوق الحُروف — مِنها جاءَت harakat
lines.english: Vowel marks in Arabic are called harakat — "movements" over letters.
lines.transliteration: harakat al-huroof — harakaat — "movements" fawq al-huroof

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخُبز في العَرَبِيَّة — "عَيْش" في مِصر — أَي "حَياة"
lines.english: Bread in Egypt is called "aysh" — meaning "life".
lines.transliteration: al-khubz fil-arabiyya — "'aysh" fii misr — ay "hayaat"

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَفي الخَليج "خُبز" — نَفس الجَذر لِلعَيش وَالحَياة
lines.english: And in the Gulf "khubz" — the same root as 'aysh meaning life.
lines.transliteration: wa fil-khalij "khubz" — nafs al-jadhr lil-'aysh wal-hayaat

choices.english: Bread is life! Thank you, Yasmin.

name: Astronomer Zain
role: Teaches number and sky vocabulary through astronomy

personality.catchphrase: النُّجومُ لا تَكذِب — an-nujuumu laa takdhib (The stars do not lie)

greeting.arabic: النُّجومُ لا تَكذِب. مَرحَباً يا مُتَعَلِّم
greeting.english: The stars do not lie. Welcome, learner.
greeting.transliteration: an-nujuumu laa takdhib. marhaban ya muta'allim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا زَين. أَدرُسُ النُّجوم مُنذُ عِشرين سَنَة
lines.english: I am Zain. I have studied the stars for twenty years.
lines.transliteration: ana zayn. adrusu an-nujuum mundhu 'ishriina sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ أَعطَوا النُّجومَ أَسماءَها
lines.english: The Arabs gave the stars their names.
lines.transliteration: al-'arabu a'taw an-nujuuma asmaa'ahaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: النُّجومُ لا تَكذِب! ماذا نَدرُس؟
lines.english: The stars do not lie! What shall we study?
lines.transliteration: an-nujuumu laa takdhib! maadha nadrus?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرقامُ أَساسُ الفَلَك
lines.english: Numbers are the foundation of astronomy.
lines.transliteration: al-arqaamu asaas al-falak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَجْم — كُلّ نَجم لَهُ اِسم عَرَبي
lines.english: Star — every star has an Arabic name.
lines.transliteration: najm — kullu najm lahu ism 'arabii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَمَر — القَمَرُ يُنير لَيالينا
lines.english: Moon — the moon illuminates our nights.
lines.transliteration: qamar — al-qamaru yuniir layaaliinaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَمْس — مَركَزُ كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Sun — the center of everything.
lines.transliteration: shams — markazu kulli shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الخوارِزمي اِبتَكَر الجَبر
lines.english: Al-Khwarizmi invented algebra.
lines.transliteration: al-khwaarizmii ibtakara al-jabr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "algorithm" جاءَت مِن اِسمِه
lines.english: And the word "algorithm" came from his name.
lines.transliteration: wa kalimat algorithm jaa'at min ismihi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبُ حَفِظوا عِلمَ اليونان وَزادوا عَلَيه
lines.english: The Arabs preserved Greek science and added to it.
lines.transliteration: al-'arabu hafizuu 'ilm al-yuunaan wa zaaduu 'alayhi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اللَّيلَة القَمَر مُكتَمِل!
lines.english: Tonight the moon is full!
lines.transliteration: al-layla al-qamar muktamil!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحتاجُ مَن يُساعِدُني في رَصد النُّجوم
lines.english: I need someone to help me observe the stars.
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju man yusaa'idunii fii rasd an-nujuum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! هُنا أَسماء النُّجوم العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: You're back! Here are Arabic star names.
lines.transliteration: 'udta! hunaa asmaa' an-nujoom al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الدَّبَران — النَّجم البُرتُقالي في الثَّور. بِالإنجليزِيَّة "Aldebaran"
lines.english: Al-Dabaraan — the orange star in Taurus. In English: "Aldebaran".
lines.transliteration: ad-dabaraan — an-najm al-burtuqaalii fit-thawr. bil-injliiziyya "Aldebaran"
lines.culturalNote: Over 200 star names in modern astronomy come from Arabic: Aldebaran (الدَّبَران), Betelgeuse (يَد الجَوزاء), Rigel (رِجْل الجَبّار), Deneb (ذَنَب), Altair (الطّائِر). Arab astronomers mapped and named the sky from the 8th century onward.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"Betelgeuse" جاءَت مِن "يَد الجَوزاء" — يَد الجَبّار
lines.english: And "Betelgeuse" came from "yad al-jawzaa'" — the giant's hand.
lines.transliteration: wa "Betelgeuse" jaa'at min "yad al-jawzaa'" — yad al-jabbaar

choices.english: The stars speak Arabic! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ يا طالِب! النُّجوم تَنتَظِر دَراسَتَنا
lines.english: You returned, student! The stars await our study.
lines.transliteration: 'udta yaa taalib! an-nujoom tantazir diraasatanaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَبر — اِبتَكَرَه الخَوارِزمي في بَغداد سَنَة ٨٣٠ مِيلادِيَّة
lines.english: Jabr — algebra, invented by al-Khwarizmi in Baghdad in 830 CE.
lines.transliteration: jabr — ibtakarahu al-khawaarizmi fii baghdaad sana 830 miilaadiyya
lines.culturalNote: Al-Khwarizmi's book "Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar fi Hisab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala" (830 CE) gave us both "algebra" (from al-jabr) and the word "algorithm" (from his Latinized name Algoritmi). His work formed the basis of all modern mathematics.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "algorithm" جاءَت مِن اِسمِه — الخَوارِزمي يُلفَظ بِاللّاتينِيَّة "Algoritmi"
lines.english: "Algorithm" came from his name — al-Khwarizmi was pronounced "Algoritmi" in Latin.
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "algorithm" jaa'at min ismihi — al-khawaarizmi yulafaz bil-laatiiniyya "Algoritmi"

choices.english: Algebra and algorithms! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الإِسطِرلاب — أَداة المُنَجِّمين العَرَب لِقياس النُّجوم
lines.english: Al-Istirllab — the astrolabe, the Arab astronomers' tool for measuring stars.
lines.transliteration: al-istirllab — adaatu al-munajjimiin al-arab liqiyaas an-nujoom
lines.culturalNote: The astrolabe (الإِسطِرلاب, from Greek) was perfected by Arab astronomers. By the 9th century, Muslim scholars had built astrolabes with 1,000+ star positions. It solved problems of time, prayer direction (qibla), and navigation — a pocket-sized computer of the medieval world.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِالإِسطِرلاب يُمكِنُك مَعرِفَة وَقت الصَّلاة أَينَما كُنتَ في العالَم
lines.english: With the astrolabe you can know prayer time wherever you are in the world.
lines.transliteration: bil-istirllab yumkinuka ma'rifat waqt as-salaa aynamaa kunta fil-'aalam

choices.arabic: عِلم وَدين في آنٍ مَعاً! شُكراً زَين
choices.english: Science and faith together! Thank you, Zain.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَقت — هَذِهِ الكَلِمَة مُهِمَّة لِلفَلَكي
lines.english: Waqt — time. This word is essential for the astronomer.
lines.transliteration: waqt — haadhihi al-kalima muhimma lil-falakii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَب قَسَّموا اللَّيل إلى سَاعات وَالسّاعَة إلى دَقائِق — قَبلَ أَوروبّا بِقُرون
lines.english: Arabs divided the night into hours and the hour into minutes — centuries before Europe.
lines.transliteration: al-arab qassamuu al-layl ilaa saa'aat was-saa'a ilaa daqaa'iq — qabl urubbaa bi-quroon

choices.english: Time is a science! Thank you, Zain.

name: Carpet Seller Jamal
role: Teaches color vocabulary through carpet trading

personality.catchphrase: يا سلام! — ya salaam! (Oh wow!)

greeting.arabic: يا سلام! تَعال شوف السَّجّاد الجَميل
greeting.english: Oh wow! Come see the beautiful carpets!
greeting.transliteration: ya salaam! ta'aal shuuf as-sajjaad al-jamiil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا جَمال! أَبيعُ أَجمَل سَجّاد في المَملَكَة
lines.english: I am Jamal! I sell the most beautiful carpets in the kingdom!
lines.transliteration: ana jamaal! abii' ajmal sajjaad fii al-mamlaka

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا سلام! عِندي سَجّاد جَديد اليَوم
lines.english: Oh wow! I have new carpets today!
lines.transliteration: ya salaam! 'indii sajjaad jadiid al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّجّادُ يُعَلِّمُك الأَلوان
lines.english: Carpets teach you colors!
lines.transliteration: as-sajjaadu yu'allimuk al-alwaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَصْفَر — لَونُ الذَّهَب وَالشَّمس
lines.english: Yellow — the color of gold and sun.
lines.transliteration: asfar — lawnu adh-dhahab wash-shams

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبْيَض — لَونُ النَّقاء وَالسَّلام
lines.english: White — the color of purity and peace.
lines.transliteration: abyad — lawnu an-naqaa' was-salaam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ سَجّادَة تَحكي قِصَّة
lines.english: Every carpet tells a story.
lines.transliteration: kullu sajjaada tahkii qissa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأُنثوذاتُ تُنسَج بِأَيدي النِّساء في القُرى
lines.english: The patterns are woven by women in the villages.
lines.transliteration: al-unthuzaat tunsaj bi-aydii an-nisaa' fii al-quraa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيلى بائِعَة التَّوابِل رَفَعَت الأَسعار!
lines.english: Layla the spice seller raised her prices!
lines.transliteration: laylaa baa'i'at at-tawaabil rafa'at al-as'aar!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِن عِندي أَسعار أَحسَن. يا سلام!
lines.english: But I have better prices. Oh wow!
lines.transliteration: laakin 'indii as'aar ahsan. ya salaam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً! لِنَتَعَلَّم أَلواناً أَكثَر مِن السَّجّادات
lines.english: Welcome! Let's learn more colors from the carpets.
lines.transliteration: marhaban! linata'allam alwaanan akthar min as-sajjaadaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَحمَر — لَونُ الدَّم وَالرُّمّان وَالشَّجاعَة
lines.english: Ahmar — red, the color of blood, pomegranate, and courage.
lines.transliteration: ahmar — lawnul-dam war-rummaan wash-shajaa'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَزرَق — لَونُ السَّماء وَالبَحر. وَ"أُزَيرِق" اِسم لِلأَزرَق الفاتِح
lines.english: Azraq — blue, the color of sky and sea.
lines.transliteration: azraq — lawnus-samaa' wal-bahr.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخضَر — لَونُ الجَنَّة في الإِسلام وَالنَّباتات
lines.english: Akhdar — green, the color of paradise in Islam and plants.
lines.transliteration: akhdar — lawnal-janna fil-islam wan-nabaataat
lines.culturalNote: Green (أَخضَر, akhdar) holds special significance in Islam — it is the color associated with paradise (al-janna). The Prophet's banner was green, and many mosque domes are painted green.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً وَسَهلاً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! اليَوم نَتَعَلَّم التِّجارَة
lines.english: Welcome back! Today we learn trade vocabulary.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan marra thaaniya! al-yawm nata'allam at-tijaara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سِعر — كَم سِعره؟ هَذا السُّؤال في كُلّ سوق
lines.english: Si'r — price. How much is it? This question is in every market.
lines.transliteration: si'r — kam si'ruh? haadha as-su'aal fii kull suuq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "tariff" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن العَرَبِيَّة "تَعريفَة" — رُسوم التِّجارَة
lines.english: The English word "tariff" came from Arabic "ta'rifa" — trade fees.
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "tariff" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-arabiyya "ta'rifa"
lines.culturalNote: "Tariff" traces to Arabic ta'rifa (تَعرِفَة, price list/notification). Arab merchants in the medieval Mediterranean standardized many trade practices that European merchants then adopted — including the use of written contracts (sakk, which became "cheque/check").

choices.english: You taught me much! Thank you, Jamal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَسيج — فِعل النَّسج. وَمِنهُ جاءَت "magazine" بِالإنجليزِيَّة؟
lines.english: Nasij — the act of weaving. And from this came "magazine" in English?
lines.transliteration: nasiij — fi'l an-nasj.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لا! "magazine" جاءَت مِن العَرَبِيَّة "مَخزَن" — مَكان لِتَخزين الأَشياء
lines.english: No! "Magazine" came from Arabic "makhzan" — a storage place.
lines.transliteration: laa! "magazine" jaa'at min al-arabiyya "makhzan" — makaan litakhziil al-ashyaa'
lines.culturalNote: "Magazine" derives from Arabic makhzan (مَخزَن, warehouse/storage), via Italian magazzino. The same root gives us "Maghreb" (al-Maghrib, the west) and the French word "magasin" (store). The publishing use — "magazine" as a repository of articles — preserves the storage metaphor.

choices.english: The warehouse became a magazine! Thank you, Jamal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ سَجّادَة هِيَ رِياضِيّات! مَثَّلَث، مُرَبَّع، دائِرَة
lines.english: Every carpet is mathematics! Triangle, square, circle.
lines.transliteration: kull sajjaada hiya riyaadiyyaat! muthalath, murabba', daa'ira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: "algebra" و"algorithm" مِن العَرَبِيَّة — العَرَب أَعطَونا الرِّياضِيّات الحَديثَة
lines.english: "Algebra" and "algorithm" come from Arabic — Arabs gave us modern mathematics.
lines.transliteration: "algebra" wa "algorithm" min al-arabiyya — al-arab a'atawna ar-riyaadiyyaat al-hadiitha

name: Dockmaster Nadia
role: Teaches direction vocabulary through port management

personality.catchphrase: بِنِظام! — bi-nizaam! (In order!)

greeting.arabic: بِنِظام! مَن أَنت وَماذا تُريد؟
greeting.english: In order! Who are you and what do you want?
greeting.transliteration: bi-nizaam! man anta wa maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا نادِيَة، رَئيسَة المِيناء. كُلّ شَيء يَمُرّ عَبري
lines.english: I am Nadia, dockmaster. Everything passes through me.
lines.transliteration: ana naadiya, ra'iisat al-miinaa'. kullu shay' yamurr 'abrii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِنِظام! عِندي وَقت قَليل
lines.english: In order! I have little time.
lines.transliteration: bi-nizaam! 'indii waqt qaliil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في المِيناء يَجِب أَن تَعرِف الاتِّجاهات
lines.english: In the port you must know directions.
lines.transliteration: fii al-miinaa' yajib an ta'rif al-ittijaahaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فَوْق — البِضاعَة فَوقَ السَّفينَة
lines.english: Above — the cargo above the ship.
lines.transliteration: fawq — al-bidaa'a fawqa as-safiina

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَحْت — المَخزَن تَحتَ الأَرض
lines.english: Below — the warehouse below ground.
lines.transliteration: taht — al-makhzan tahta al-ard

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذا المِيناء عُمرُه ثَلاثمائَة سَنَة
lines.english: This port is three hundred years old.
lines.transliteration: haadha al-miinaa' 'umruhu thalaathmi'at sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن هُنا خَرَجَت سُفُن إِلى الهِند وَالصّين
lines.english: From here ships departed to India and China.
lines.transliteration: min hunaa kharajat sufun ilaa al-hind was-siin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُناكَ سَفينَة بِدون تَصريح. اِذهَب وَتَحَقَّق
lines.english: There is a ship without a permit. Go and check.
lines.transliteration: hunaaka safiina biduun tasriih. idhhab wa tahaqqaq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! هُنا دَرس جَديد عَن البَحر
lines.english: You're back! Here's a new lesson about the sea.
lines.transliteration: 'udta! hunaa dars jadiid 'an al-bahr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بَحْر — هُوَ المَعنى الأَصلي لِكَلِمَة "الجَوف"
lines.english: Bahr — the sea. The word also gives us "bahrain" (two seas).
lines.transliteration: bahr — huwa al-ma'naa al-aslii. "al-bahrayn" ta'nii al-bahrayn
lines.culturalNote: "Bahrain" (البَحرَيْن) literally means "two seas" in Arabic — referring to the freshwater springs that well up through the Gulf's saltwater floor. Arab merchants knew this geography precisely for navigation.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "admiral" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن "أَمير البَحر"
lines.english: And the English word "admiral" came from Arabic "amir al-bahr" (prince of the sea).
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "admiral" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min "amiir al-bahr"

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! مِيناؤنا مَشغول اليَوم
lines.english: Welcome again! Our port is busy today.
lines.transliteration: marhaban marra thaaniya! miinaau'naa mashghool al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَشَرَة سُفُن في المِيناء — عَشَرَة هُوَ رَقم مُهِمّ في التِّجارَة
lines.english: Ten ships in the port — ten is an important number in trade.
lines.transliteration: 'ashara sufun fil-miinaaa' — 'ashara huwa raqm muhimm fit-tijaara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرقامُ العَرَبِيَّة التي تَستَخدِمُها أَوروبّا جاءَت مِن العَرَب
lines.english: The Arabic numerals Europe uses came from the Arabs.
lines.transliteration: al-arqaamu al-arabiyya allati tastakhdimuha urubbaa jaa'at min al-arab
lines.culturalNote: Arabic numerals (١٢٣...) were adopted by Europe in the 10th-12th centuries through Arab scholars in Andalusia, particularly Al-Khwarizmi's "On Hindu-Arabic Numerals." Before this, Europe used Roman numerals (I, V, X...) — nearly impossible for complex calculation.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَفينَة — أَجمَل كَلِمَة في المِيناء. كَم سَفينَة تَرى؟
lines.english: Safiina — the most beautiful word in the port. How many ships do you see?
lines.transliteration: safiina — ajmal kalima fil-miinaaa. kam safiina taraa?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَركَب العَرَبي "الدّاو" أَبحَرَ مِن أَفريقيا إلى الصّين وَعادَ — ١٠٠٠ سَنَة قَبلَ كولومبوس
lines.english: The Arab "dhow" ship sailed from Africa to China and back — 1,000 years before Columbus.
lines.transliteration: al-markab al-arabii "ad-daaw" abhara min afriqia ilaa as-siin wa 'aada
lines.culturalNote: The Arab dhow (داو) was the dominant vessel of the Indian Ocean trade network from the 8th-19th centuries. Arab navigator Ahmad ibn Majid (15th c.) wrote 40+ navigation treatises — and guided Vasco da Gama to India in 1498.

choices.english: Arabs were great sailors! Thank you.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: آخِر دَرس! كَيف تُحَيِّي البَحّارَة؟
lines.english: Final lesson! How do you greet sailors?
lines.transliteration: aakhir dars! kayf tuhayiii al-bahhaarah?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً — أَصلُها "رَحب" أَي سَعَة وَفُسحَة — أَهلاً بِك
lines.english: Marhaban — from rahb, meaning wide space — you are welcome here.
lines.transliteration: marhaban — asluha "rahb" ay sa'a wa fusha — ahlan bik

name: Mountain Hermit Idris
role: Teaches nature vocabulary through mountain wisdom

personality.catchphrase: الجَبَلُ يَعلَم — al-jabalu ya'lam (The mountain knows)

greeting.arabic: الجَبَلُ يَعلَم مَن يَأتي. تَعال اِجلِس
greeting.english: The mountain knows who comes. Come, sit.
greeting.transliteration: al-jabalu ya'lam man ya'tii. ta'aal ijlis

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا إِدريس. أَعيشُ هُنا وَحدي مُنذُ سَنَوات
lines.english: I am Idris. I have lived here alone for years.
lines.transliteration: ana idriis. a'iishu hunaa wahdii mundhu sanawaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَلُ مُعَلِّمي وَصَديقي
lines.english: The mountain is my teacher and my friend.
lines.transliteration: al-jabalu mu'allimii wa sadiiqii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَلُ يَعلَم... ماذا تَبحَث عَنه؟
lines.english: The mountain knows... what do you seek?
lines.transliteration: al-jabalu ya'lam... maadha tabhath 'anhu?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطَّبيعَةُ لُغَة بِلا كَلِمات. لَكِن نَحتاج كَلِمات أَيضاً
lines.english: Nature is a language without words. But we need words too.
lines.transliteration: at-tabii'atu lugha bilaa kalimaat. laakin nahtaaj kalimaat aydan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَمْل — الصَّحراء تَتَكَلَّم بِالرَّمل
lines.english: Sand — the desert speaks with sand.
lines.transliteration: raml — as-sahraa' tatakallam bir-raml

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَجَرَة — الصَّبر كَالشَّجَرَة، يَنمو بِبُطء
lines.english: Tree — patience is like a tree, it grows slowly.
lines.transliteration: shajara — as-sabr kash-shajara, yanmuu bibu't'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولون أَنَّ في هَذا الجَبَل كَنزاً مَخفِيّاً
lines.english: They say there is a hidden treasure in this mountain.
lines.transliteration: yaquuluun anna fii haadha al-jabal kanzan makhfiyyan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِنَّ الكَنز الحَقيقي هُوَ المَعرِفَة
lines.english: But the real treasure is knowledge.
lines.transliteration: laakinna al-kanz al-haqiiqii huwa al-ma'rifa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَل يَختَبِر مَن يَدخُل
lines.english: The mountain tests those who enter.
lines.transliteration: al-jabal yakhtabir man yadkhul

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: إِذا عَرَفتَ الكَلِمات، سَتَجِد الطَّريق
lines.english: If you know the words, you will find the way.
lines.transliteration: idhaa 'arafta al-kalimaat, satajid at-tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ. الجَبَلُ لا يَنسى مَن طَلَبَ الحِكمَة
lines.english: You returned. The mountain never forgets those who sought wisdom.
lines.transliteration: 'udta. al-jabal laa yansaa man talaba al-hikma

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَبر — الصَّبرُ مِفتاحُ الفَرَج. كَلِمَة عَظيمَة
lines.english: Sabr — patience is the key to relief. A great word.
lines.transliteration: sabr — as-sabru miftaahu al-faraj. kalima 'aziima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَقَولُ المَثَل: "الصَّبرُ مِفتاحُ الفَرَج" — بِالعَرَبِيَّة يُصبِح شِعراً
lines.english: And the proverb: "Patience is the key to relief" — in Arabic it becomes poetry.
lines.transliteration: wa qawlu al-mathal: "as-sabru miftaahu al-faraj" — bil-arabiyya yusbih shi'ran
lines.culturalNote: Arabic proverbs (أَمثال, amthaal) are a cornerstone of classical learning. The proverb "الصَّبرُ مِفتاحُ الفَرَج" (patience is the key to relief) appears in Imam al-Ghazali's 12th-century Ihya Ulum al-Din.

choices.english: Wisdom lives here. Thank you, Idris.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَل يَرحَّب بِك مَرَّة أُخرى. لِنَتَأَمَّل
lines.english: The mountain welcomes you again. Let us reflect.
lines.transliteration: al-jabal yurahahib bik marra ukhraa. linata'ammal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حِكمَة — وَكَلِمَة "حَكيم" تَعني الحَكيم أَو الطَّبيب في العَرَبِيَّة القَديمَة
lines.english: Hikma — wisdom. And "hakim" means wise man or physician in classical Arabic.
lines.transliteration: hikma — wa kalima "hakiim" ta'nii al-hakiim aw at-tabiib fil-arabiyya al-qadiima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ابن سينا لَقَّبوه "الشَّيخ الرَّئيس" — رَئيس الحُكَماء
lines.english: Ibn Sina was titled "al-Shaykh al-Ra'is" — Chief of the Wise.
lines.transliteration: ibn siinaa laqqabuuh "ash-shaykh ar-ra'iis" — ra'iis al-hukamaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَ"elixir" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن الكيمياء العَرَبِيَّة "الإِكسير"
lines.english: And English "elixir" came from Arabic alchemy: "al-iksir".
lines.transliteration: wa "elixir" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-kiimyaa' al-arabiyya "al-iksir"
lines.culturalNote: "Elixir" derives from Arabic al-iksir (الإِكسير), itself from Greek xerion. Arab alchemists like Jabir ibn Hayyan (8th c.) developed systematic chemistry — the word "alchemy" itself comes from Arabic al-kimiya (الكيمياء), from Coptic kemi (black earth/Egypt).

choices.arabic: العِلمُ العَرَبي في كُلّ مَكان! شُكراً إِدريس
choices.english: Arabic science is everywhere! Thank you, Idris.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الكِتابَة العَرَبِيَّة تَسير مِن اليَمين إلى اليَسار — كَالشَّمس تَغرُب
lines.english: Arabic writing goes from right to left — like the sun setting.
lines.transliteration: al-kitaaba al-arabiyya tasiir min al-yamiin ilaa al-yasaar — kashams taghrub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَذر "ك-ت-ب": كَتَبَ — يَكتُب — كِتاب — كاتِب — مَكتَبَة — مَكتَب
lines.english: Root K-T-B: kataba (he wrote) — yaktub (he writes) — kitaab (book) — kaatib (writer) — maktaba (library) — maktab (office).
lines.transliteration: jadhr k-t-b: kataba — yaktub — kitaab — kaatib — maktaba — maktab
lines.culturalNote: The Arabic trilateral root K-T-B (ك-ت-ب) demonstrates the system's power: from three letters, the language generates dozens of related words. Learning one root unlocks a whole vocabulary family — this is why Arabic learners say "once you see the roots, the language opens up."

choices.english: Roots open the world! Thank you, Idris.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس. خُذ نَفَساً. "تَفَكَّر" — العَقل يَحتاج الهُدوء
lines.english: Sit. Take a breath. "Tafakkar" — the mind needs quiet.
lines.transliteration: ijlis. khudh nafasan. "tafakkar" — al-'aql yahtaaj al-huduu'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "تَفَكَّر" تَعني التَّأَمُّل العَميق — فِكر عَميق
lines.english: "Tafakkar" means deep reflection — profound thought.
lines.transliteration: kalima "tafakkar" ta'nii at-ta'ammul al-'amiiq — fikr 'amiiq

name: Stable Master Yara
role: Teaches animal vocabulary through horse care

personality.catchphrase: هَيّا يا حُصان! — hayyaa ya husaan! (Come on, horse!)

greeting.arabic: هَيّا يا حُصان! أَهلاً يا مُسافِر!
greeting.english: Come on, horse! Hello, traveler!
greeting.transliteration: hayyaa ya husaan! ahlan ya musaafir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا يارا. أَعتَني بِالخُيول مُنذُ صِغَري
lines.english: I am Yara. I have cared for horses since I was small.
lines.transliteration: ana yaaraa. a'tanii bil-khuyuul mundhu sigharii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَيّا! الخُيول تَنتَظِر. ماذا تُريد؟
lines.english: Let's go! The horses are waiting. What do you want?
lines.transliteration: hayyaa! al-khuyuul tantazir. maadha turiid?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَيَوانات أَصدِقاؤنا! لِنَتَعَلَّم أَسماءَها
lines.english: Animals are our friends! Let us learn their names.
lines.transliteration: al-hayawaanaat asdiqaa'unaa! linata'allam asmaa'ahaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حِصان — أَنبَل الحَيَوانات
lines.english: Horse — the noblest of animals.
lines.transliteration: hisaan — anbal al-hayawaanaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَمَل — سَفينَة الصَّحراء
lines.english: Camel — the ship of the desert.
lines.transliteration: jamal — safiinat as-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَيْر — حُرّ في السَّماء
lines.english: Bird — free in the sky.
lines.transliteration: tayr — hurr fis-samaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِصانُ العَرَبي أَجمَل سُلالَة في العالَم
lines.english: The Arabian horse is the most beautiful breed in the world.
lines.transliteration: al-hisaanu al-'arabii ajmal sulaala fii al-'aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولون أَنَّ الله خَلَقَهُ مِن الرّيح
lines.english: They say God created it from the wind.
lines.transliteration: yaquuluun anna allaah khalaqahu min ar-riih

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قافِلَة جَديدَة وَصَلَت مِن الجَبَل
lines.english: A new caravan arrived from the mountain.
lines.transliteration: qaafila jadiida wasalat min al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَقولون إِنَّ الطَّريق خَطير هَذِهِ الأَيّام
lines.english: They say the road is dangerous these days.
lines.transliteration: yaquuluun inna at-tariiq khatiir haadhihi al-ayyaam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً! الخُيول تَفرَح بِرُجوعِك
lines.english: Welcome! The horses are happy at your return.
lines.transliteration: marhaban! al-khuyuul tafrahu bi-rujooo'ik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قافِلَة — مَجموعَة مِن الجِمال وَالتُّجّار
lines.english: Qaafila — a caravan, a group of camels and traders.
lines.transliteration: qaafila — majmoo'a min al-jimaal wat-tujjaar

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "caravan" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن الفارِسِيَّة عَن طَريق العَرَبِيَّة: "قَرواَن"
lines.english: "Caravan" in English came through Arabic from Persian: "qirwaan".
lines.transliteration: "caravan" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-faarisiyya 'an tariiq al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: طَريق الحَرير كانَ أَطوَل طَريق تِجاري في التّاريخ — مِن الصّين إلى الأَندَلُس
lines.english: The Silk Road was the longest trade route in history — from China to Andalusia.
lines.transliteration: tariiq al-hariir kaana atwal tariiq tijaarii fit-taariikh — min as-siin ilaa al-andalus
lines.culturalNote: The Silk Road (طَريق الحَرير) connected China to Andalusia. Arab merchants were its backbone from the 8th-13th centuries, carrying silk, spices, paper, and knowledge — along with Arabic vocabulary that remains in dozens of languages today.

choices.english: I want to travel someday! Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَباً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! الإِسطَبل مَكان يُعَلِّم
lines.english: Welcome again! The stable is a place that teaches.
lines.transliteration: marhaban marra thaaniya! al-istab al-makaan yu'allim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحِصان العَرَبي الأَصيل — أَسرَع خَيل في العالَم القَديم
lines.english: The Arabian thoroughbred — the fastest horse in the ancient world.
lines.transliteration: al-hisaan al-arabii al-asiil — asra' khayl fil-'aalam al-qadiim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة عِندَها مِئَة اِسم لِلحِصان وَخَمسِمِئَة لِلأَسَد
lines.english: Arabic has one hundred names for the horse and five hundred for the lion.
lines.transliteration: al-lugha al-arabiyya 'indahaa mi'a ism lil-hisaan wa khamsumi'a lil-asad
lines.culturalNote: Classical Arabic's richness of vocabulary is legendary: reportedly 1,000+ words for camel and its states, 500+ for lion, 200+ for snake. This reflects the Bedouin oral tradition of precision in describing the natural world upon which survival depended.

choices.arabic: اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة غَنِيَّة جِدَّاً! شُكراً يارا
choices.english: Arabic is so rich! Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَمَل — سَفينَة الصَّحراء — يُخزِّن الدَّهن في سَنامِه لَيسَ الماء
lines.english: The camel — ship of the desert — stores fat in its hump, not water.
lines.transliteration: al-jamal — safinat as-sahraa' — yukhazzin ad-dahn fii sanamih laysa al-maa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَب سَمَّوا الجَمَل "سَفينَة الصَّحراء" — وَهُوَ وَسيلَة نَقلِهِم لِأَلفَي سَنَة
lines.english: Arabs called the camel "ship of the desert" — their transport for two thousand years.
lines.transliteration: al-arab sammaaw al-jamal "safinat as-sahraa'" — wa huwa wasiilat naqlihim li-alfay sana
lines.culturalNote: The camel's domestication around 3000 BCE transformed the Arabian peninsula. Classical Arabic has reportedly over 1,000 words related to camels and their states — reflecting the animal's centrality to Bedouin survival.

choices.english: The camel is a miracle! Thank you, Yara.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: "الجَزيرَة العَرَبِيَّة" تَعني: الجَزيرَة — الأَرض المُحاطَة بِالماء
lines.english: "Al-Jazira al-Arabiyya" means: jazira — land surrounded by water (peninsula).
lines.transliteration: "al-jazira al-arabiyya" ta'nii: al-jaziira — al-ard al-muhaata bil-maa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: "الجَزيرَة" أَيضاً اِسم قَناة الأَخبار — مَعناها "الجَزيرَة"
lines.english: "Al-Jazeera" is also the news channel name — it means "The Island/Peninsula".
lines.transliteration: "al-jazeera" aydan ism qanaat al-akhbaar — ma'naaha "al-jaziira"

choices.english: Al-Jazeera! I understand now. Thank you, Yara.

name: Garden Keeper Leila
role: Teaches nature and plant vocabulary

personality.catchphrase: الحَديقَة جَنَّة — al-hadiiqa janna (The garden is paradise)

greeting.arabic: الحَديقَة جَنَّة! مَرحَباً يا زائِر
greeting.english: The garden is paradise! Welcome, visitor.
greeting.transliteration: al-hadiiqa janna! marhaban ya zaa'ir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا لَيلى. أَعتَني بِهَذِهِ الحَديقَة مُنذُ عَشر سَنَوات
lines.english: I am Leila. I have tended this garden for ten years.
lines.transliteration: ana laylaa. a'tanii bihaadhihi al-hadiiqa mundhu 'ashr sanawaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَديقَة جَنَّة! ماذا نَكتَشِف اليَوم؟
lines.english: The garden is paradise! What shall we discover today?
lines.transliteration: al-hadiiqa janna! maadha naktashif al-yawm?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الطَّبيعَة مُعَلِّمَة عَظيمَة
lines.english: Nature is a great teacher.
lines.transliteration: at-tabii'a mu'allima 'aziima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَمْس — النَّباتات تَحتاج الشَّمس لِتَنمو
lines.english: Sun — plants need the sun to grow.
lines.transliteration: shams — an-nabaataat tahtaaj ash-shams litanmuu

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَاء — وَالماء أَيضاً ضَروري
lines.english: Water — and water is also essential.
lines.transliteration: maa' — wal-maa' aydan daruurii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ الحَديقَة بَناها المَلِكُ الأَوَّل
lines.english: The first king built this garden.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-hadiiqa banaahaa al-maliku al-awwal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كانَ يَقول: الحَديقَة تُريح النَّفس وَتُنَقّي الرّوح
lines.english: He used to say: the garden soothes the soul and purifies the spirit.
lines.transliteration: kaana yaquul: al-hadiiqa turiih an-nafs wa tunaqqii ar-ruuh

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الشّاعِر رومي يَجلِس هُنا كُلّ يَوم وَيَكتُب
lines.english: The poet Rumi sits here every day and writes.
lines.transliteration: ash-shaa'ir ruumii yajlis hunaa kulla yawm wa yaktub

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَحياناً يَقرَأ لي قَصائِدَهُ. هِيَ جَميلَة
lines.english: And sometimes he reads me his poems. They are beautiful.
lines.transliteration: wa ahyaanan yaqra' lii qasaa'idahu. hiya jamiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً! لِنَتَعَلَّم أَسماء النَّباتات اليَوم
lines.english: Welcome! Let's learn plant names today.
lines.transliteration: ahlan! linata'allam asmaa' an-nabaataat al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَرد — الزَّهرَة الأَجمَل. وَكَلِمَة "ward" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِنها
lines.english: Ward — rose, the most beautiful flower.
lines.transliteration: ward — az-zahra al-ajmal.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: نَخيل — شَجَرَة التَّمر. غِذاء الصَّحراء مُنذُ آلاف السِّنين
lines.english: Nakheeel — the date palm. Desert food for thousands of years.
lines.transliteration: nakhiil — shajarat at-tamr. ghidha' as-sahraa' mundhu alaaf as-siniin
lines.culturalNote: The date palm (نَخيل) was so essential to desert life that classical Arabic has over 360 words for different types of dates and stages of palm development. It provided food, timber, fiber, and shade.

choices.english: Nature is beautiful! Thank you Leila.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ يا صَديقي! الفُصول تَتَغَيَّر وَالحَديقَة تَتَجَدَّد
lines.english: You returned, my friend! The seasons change and the garden renews.
lines.transliteration: 'udta yaa sadiiqii! al-fusool tataghayar wal-hadiqa tatajaddad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَبيع — فَصلُ الأَزهار وَالأَمَل
lines.english: Rabia — spring, the season of flowers and hope.
lines.transliteration: rabiia — faslu al-azhaar wal-amal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَيف — الحَرارَة وَالعَمَل. شِتاء — المَطَر وَالرّاحَة
lines.english: Sayf — summer, heat and work. Shitaa' — winter, rain and rest.
lines.transliteration: sayf — al-haraara wal-'amal. shitaa' — al-matar war-raaha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "monsoon" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن العَرَبِيَّة "مَوسِم" — المَوسِم
lines.english: The English word "monsoon" came from Arabic "mawsim" — the season.
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "monsoon" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-arabiyya "mawsim"
lines.culturalNote: "Monsoon" derives from Arabic mawsim (مَوسِم, season). Arab sailors in the Indian Ocean used the seasonal monsoon winds to navigate between Arabia, India, and East Africa — mastering these patterns by the 8th century CE.

choices.english: The seasons are like life. Thank you, Leila.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الماء حَياة! "ماء" — أَقصَر الكَلِمات وَأَهَمُّها
lines.english: Water is life! "Maa'" — the shortest word and the most important.
lines.transliteration: al-maa' hayaat! "maa'" — aqsar al-kalimaat wa ahammuha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَناة — العَرَب بَنوا قَنوات الري في الأَندَلُس — لا تَزال تَعمَل
lines.english: Qanaat — the Arabs built irrigation canals in Andalusia — still working.
lines.transliteration: qanaah — al-arab banaw qanawaat ar-ray fii al-andalus — laa tazaal ta'mal
lines.culturalNote: The Arab Agricultural Revolution (8th-13th c.) transformed Spain: the Arabs introduced sophisticated irrigation systems (qanat, نهر), new crops (citrus, cotton, rice, sugarcane), and agricultural manuals. Andalusian gardens like the Generalife in Granada preserve this legacy.

choices.english: Water connects humanity! Thank you, Leila.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَديقَة تُعَلِّمُك الصَّبر — النَّباتات لا تَستَعجِل
lines.english: The garden teaches patience — plants do not hurry.
lines.transliteration: al-hadiqa tu'allimuk as-sabr — an-nabaataat laa tasta'jil

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قُل: "الطَّبيعَة جَميلَة" — أَربَع كَلِمات تَعلَّمتَها اليَوم
lines.english: Say: "Nature is beautiful" — four words you learned today.
lines.transliteration: qul: "at-tabi'a jamiila" — arba' kalimaat ta'allamtaha al-yawm

choices.english: Nature is beautiful! Thank you, Leila.

name: Guide Amira
role: Mentor and guide for new travelers

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً يا مُسافِر! أَنا أَميرَة
greeting.english: Welcome, traveler! I am Amira.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan ya musaafir! ana amiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَبا! أَهْلاً بِكَ في قَرية الواحَة!
lines.english: Marhaba! Welcome to Oasis Village!
lines.transliteration: marhaba! ahlan bika fii qaryat al-waaha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا أَميرَة، مُرشِدَتُك. سَأُساعِدُكَ في تَعَلُّم العَرَبِيَّة
lines.english: I'm Amira, your guide. I'll help you learn Arabic.
lines.transliteration: ana amiira, murshidatuk. sa-usaa'iduka fii ta'allum al-arabiyya

lines.speaker: npc
