lines.arabic: هَذا المَكان مَليءٌ بِالنّاس الذينَ يُريدونَ مُساعَدَتَك — تَكَلَّم مَعَهُم وَتَعَلَّم!
lines.english: This place is full of people who want to help you — talk to them and learn!
lines.transliteration: haadha al-makaan malii'un bin-naas alladhiina yuriduuna musaa'adatak — takallam ma'ahum wa ta'allam!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَبدَأ بِأَوَّلِ كَلِمَة: مَرْحَبا — تَعني 'أَهلاً'!
lines.english: Let me teach you your first word: marhaba — it means 'hello'!
lines.transliteration: linabda' bi-awwal kalima: marhaba — ta'nii 'ahlan'!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! الآن اِذهَب إلى الشَّيْخ يوسُف في المَكتَبَة — عِندَهُ الكَثير لِيُعَلِّمَك
lines.english: Excellent! Now go find Scholar Yusuf at the library. He has much to teach you.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! al-aan idh-hab ilaa ash-shaykh yuusuf fil-maktaba — indahu al-kathiir liyu'allimak

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِمشِ إلى النّاس وَاِضغَط مَسافَة لِلتَّكَلُّم. يَلّا!
lines.english: Just walk up to people and press SPACE to talk. Yalla!
lines.transliteration: imshi ilan-naas wa-idghat masaafa lit-takallum. yalla!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَباً مِن جَديد! كَيفَ حالُكَ يا مُسافِر؟
lines.english: Hello again! How are you, traveler?
lines.transliteration: marhaban min jadiid! kayfa haaluka ya musaafir?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَيفَ أَستَطيعُ مُساعَدَتَك؟
lines.english: How can I help you?
lines.transliteration: kayfa astatii'u musaa'adatak?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَكَلَّم مَعَ سُكّانِ القَرية — كُلُّ شَخصٍ يُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِماتٍ جَديدَة
lines.english: Talk to the village residents — each person teaches you new words.
lines.transliteration: takallam ma'a sukkaan al-qarya — kullu shakhsin yu'allimuka kalimaat jadiida

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَكمِل المَهامّ لِتَكسِبَ خِبرَة وَدَراهِم
lines.english: Complete quests to earn XP and dirhams.
lines.transliteration: akmil al-mahaamm litaksib khibra wa daraahim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلَّما تَعَلَّمتَ كَلِماتٍ أَكثَر، فُتِحَت مَناطِقُ جَديدَة!
lines.english: The more words you learn, the more zones open up!
lines.transliteration: kullama ta'allamta kalimaat akthar, futihat manaatiqu jadiida!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِستَخدِم WASD أَو الأَسهُم لِلتَّحَرُّك. اِضغَط Shift لِلرَّكض!
lines.english: Use WASD or arrow keys to move. Hold Shift to sprint!
lines.transliteration: istakhdim WASD aw al-ashum lit-taharruk. idghat Shift lir-rakd!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِضغَط مَسافَة لِلتَّكَلُّم مَعَ النّاس. اِضغَط Q لِقائِمَة المَهامّ
lines.english: Press Space to talk to people. Press Q for the quest log.
lines.transliteration: idghat masaafa lit-takallum ma'a an-naas. idghat Q li-qaa'imat al-mahaamm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِضغَط M لِفَتح الخَريطَة وَ ESC لِلقائِمَة الرَّئيسِيَّة
lines.english: Press M to open the map and ESC for the main menu.
lines.transliteration: idghat M lifath al-khariita wa ESC lil-qaa'ima ar-ra'iisiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: واحَةُ الحُروف عالَمٌ سِحرِيٌّ حَيثُ تَتَعَلَّمُ العَرَبِيَّة مِن أَهلِها
lines.english: The Oasis of Letters is a magical world where you learn Arabic from its people.
lines.transliteration: waahat al-huruuf aalamun sihriyyun haythu tata'allamu al-arabiyya min ahlihaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَخطوطَة قَديمَة نَقَلَتكَ إلى هُنا — وَلِكَي تَعودَ يَجِبُ أَن تُتقِنَ اللُّغَة
lines.english: An ancient manuscript brought you here — and to return, you must master the language.
lines.transliteration: makhtootatun qadiima naqalatka ilaa hunaa — wa likay ta'uuda yajib an tutqina al-lugha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِستَكشِف ثَمانِيَة مَناطِق، تَعَلَّم مِن ثَلاثينَ مُعَلِّماً، وَأَكمِل رِحلَتَك!
lines.english: Explore eight zones, learn from thirty teachers, and complete your journey!
lines.transliteration: istakshif thamaaniyat manaatiq, ta'allam min thalaathiin mu'alliman, wa akmil rihlatak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرى أَنَّكَ بَدَأتَ تَستَكشِف! كُلُّ مِنطَقَة تُعَلِّمُكَ مَوضوعاً مُختَلِفاً
lines.english: I see you've started exploring! Each zone teaches you a different topic.
lines.transliteration: araa annaka bada'ta tastakshif! kullu mintaqa tu'allimuka mawduu'an mukhtalifan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَكتَبَة تُعَلِّم الأَعداد وَالأَلوان، وَالسّوق يُعَلِّم التِّجارَة وَالطَّعام
lines.english: The library teaches numbers and colors, and the market teaches trade and food.
lines.transliteration: al-maktaba tu'allim al-a'daad wal-alwaan, was-suuq yu'allim at-tijaara wat-ta'aam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ما شاءَ اللَّه! أَنتَ تَتَقَدَّمُ بِسُرعَة
lines.english: Wonderful! You are progressing quickly.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa'a allaah! anta tataqaddamu bisur'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: واصِل هَكَذا — الطَّريقُ طَويلٌ وَلَكِنَّكَ قادِر
lines.english: Keep it up — the path is long but you are capable.
lines.transliteration: waasil haakadha — at-tariiqu tawiilun wa laakinnaka qaadir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبيَّةُ يَتَحَدَّثُها أَكثَرُ مِن ٤٠٠ مِليون شَخص
lines.english: Arabic is spoken by over 400 million people
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya yatahadathuha akthar min 400 milyun shakhs

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الفُصحى تَجمَعُ ٢٢ دَولَة — مِن المَغرِب إلى العِراق
lines.english: Fusha unites 22 countries — from Morocco to Iraq
lines.transliteration: al-fusha tajma' 22 dawla — min al-maghrib ila al-'iraq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ بَلَدٍ لَهُ لَهجَة لكِنَّ الفُصحى هِيَ اللُّغَةُ المُشتَرَكَة
lines.english: Each country has a dialect but Fusha is the shared language
lines.transliteration: kullu balad lahu lahja lakinna al-fusha hiya al-lugha al-mushtaraka
lines.culturalNote: Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha) is understood across all Arabic-speaking countries. It's the language of news, literature, and formal speech — the common thread connecting 400+ million people.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً مُجَدَّداً! كَيفَ تَسير رِحلَتُكَ؟ أَتَعلَّمتَ كَلِمَات كَثيرَة؟
lines.english: Welcome back! How is your journey going? Have you learned many words?
lines.transliteration: Ahlan mujaddadan! Kayfa tasir rihlatuk? Ata'allamta kalimaat kathiira?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! تَذكَّر: كُلُّ كَلِمَة عَرَبِيَّة تَتَعلَّمُها هِيَ مِفتَاح لِفَهم حَضَارَة عَظيمَة!
lines.english: Excellent! Remember: every Arabic word you learn is a key to understanding a great civilization!
lines.transliteration: Mumtaaz! Tadhakkar: kullu kalima 'arabiyya tata'allamuhaa hiya miftaah li-fahm hadaara 'aziima!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَلِمَة "يَلَّا"! أَكثَر كَلِمَة عَرَبِيَّة تَسمَعُها حَول العَالَم — مِن "يَا الله"!
lines.english: The word "yalla"! The most heard Arabic word around the world — from "ya Allah" (O God)!
lines.transliteration: Kalima 'yalla'! Akthar kalima 'arabiyya tasma'uhaa hawl al-'aalam — min 'yaa Allaah'!
lines.culturalNote: "Yalla" (يَلَّا) is used worldwide by Arabic speakers to mean "let's go / hurry up." It comes from "yaa Allah" (يَا اللّه), an exclamation to God. It is the single most widely recognized Arabic expression across all dialects and cultures.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَلَّا! اِذهَب وَتَكَلَّم مَع الجَميع! كُلُّ شَخص يُعَلِّمُكَ شَيئاً جَديداً!
lines.english: Yalla! Go and talk to everyone! Every person teaches you something new!
lines.transliteration: Yalla! Idh-hab wa takallam ma'a al-jamii'! Kull shakhs yu'allimuka shay'an jadiidan!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَم تَزُر يوسُف بَعد؟ اِذهَب إِليه! يُعَلِّمُكَ القَواعِد والنَّحو.
lines.english: Have you not visited Yusuf yet? Go to him! He teaches grammar and syntax.
lines.transliteration: Lam tazur Yuusuf ba'd? Idh-hab ilayh! Yu'allimuka al-qawaa'id wan-nahw.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَفَاطِمَة التَّاجِرَة تُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمَات السُّوق. لَيلى تُعَلِّمُكَ التَّوابِل والعُطور!
lines.english: And Merchant Fatima teaches you market words. Layla teaches you spices and perfumes!
lines.transliteration: Wa Faatima at-taajira tu'allimuka kalimaat as-suuq. Layla tu'allimuka at-tawaabil wal-'utuur!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَليّ الرَّحَّالَة في المُخَيَّم البَدَوي يُعَلِّمُكَ أَفعَال السَّفَر. اِذهَب إِليه!
lines.english: Wanderer Ali at the Bedouin camp teaches you travel verbs. Go to him!
lines.transliteration: Aliyy ar-rahhaala fil-mukhayyam al-badawiyy yu'allimuka af'aal as-safar. Idh-hab ilayh!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكُلَّمَا تَعَلَّمتَ كَلِمَة جَديدَة، اِرجِع إِليَّ! أَنا هُنا دَائِماً لَك.
lines.english: And whenever you learn a new word, come back to me! I am always here for you.
lines.transliteration: Wa kullamaa ta'allamta kalima jadiida, irji' ilayya! Ana hunaa daa'iman lak.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف كُلَّ التَّحِيَّات؟ هِيَ أَهَمُّ كَلِمَات العَرَبِيَّة!
lines.english: Do you know all the greetings? They are the most important Arabic words!
lines.transliteration: Hal ta'rif kull at-tahiyyaat? Hiya ahamm kalimaat al-'arabiyya!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرحَبا — قُلناها أَوَّل مَرَّة! وَيُمكِنُكَ قَولُها لِأَيِّ شَخص في أَيِّ وَقت!
lines.english: Marhaba — we said it the first time! And you can say it to anyone at any time!
lines.transliteration: Marhaba — qulnaahaa awwal marra! Wa yumkinuka qawluhaa li-ayyi shakhs fii ayyi waqt!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَصَبَاح الخَير في الصَّبَاح. وَمَسَاء الخَير في المَسَاء. بَسيط لَكِن مُؤَثِّر!
lines.english: And sabah al-khayr in the morning. And masaa al-khayr in the evening. Simple but impactful!
lines.transliteration: Wa sabaaH al-khayr fis-sabaah. Wa masaa' al-khayr fil-masaa'. Basiit laakin mu'aththir!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَأَهلاً وَسَهلاً — تَعني "أَنتَ مِن أَهلِنا وَالأَرض سَهلَة لَك"! ما أَجمَلَ اللُّغَة!
lines.english: And ahlan wa sahlan — it means "you are of our family and the ground is easy beneath you"! What a beautiful language!
lines.transliteration: Wa ahlan wa sahlan — ta'nii 'anta min ahlinaa wal-ard sahla lak'! Maa ajmal al-lugha!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَائِع! الآن أَنتَ تَعرِف كَيفَ تُحَيِّي أَيَّ شَخص بِالعَرَبِيَّة. يَلَّا، اِذهَب وَجَرِّب!
lines.english: Wonderful! Now you know how to greet anyone in Arabic. Yalla, go and try!
lines.transliteration: Raa'i'! Al-aan anta ta'rif kayfa tuhayyi ayya shakhs bil-'arabiyya. Yalla, idh-hab wa jarrib!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ تَتَقَدَّم بِسُرعَة! أَنا فَخورَة بِكَ!
lines.english: You are progressing quickly! I am proud of you!
lines.transliteration: Anta tataqaddam bi-sur'a! Ana fakhuurah bik!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلُّم اللُّغَة العَرَبِيَّة لَيسَ سَهلاً — لَكِنَّكَ لَستَ وَحدَكَ. كُلُّ نَاس هُنا يُحِبُّونَكَ.
lines.english: Learning Arabic is not easy — but you are not alone. Everyone here loves you.
lines.transliteration: Ta'allum al-lugha al-'arabiyya laysa sahlan — laakinnak lasta wahdak. Kull naas hunaa yuhibbuunak.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلُّ يَوم قَليلاً — هَذا سِرُّ النَّجاح. لا تَتَعجَّل وَلا تَستَسلِم!
lines.english: A little every day — that is the secret of success. Do not rush and do not give up!
lines.transliteration: Kull yawm qaliiilan — haadha sirr an-najaah. Laa tata'ajjal wa laa tastasлim!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعَلَّم: صَعب — لِأَنَّكَ تَعرِف بالفِعل أَنَّ التَّعلُّم صَعب. لَكِن أَنتَ تَفعَلُه!
lines.english: Learn: difficult — because you already know that learning is hard. But you are doing it!
lines.transliteration: Ta'allam: sa'b — li-annaka ta'rif bil-fi'l anna at-ta'allum sa'b. Laakin anta taf'aluh!

name: Scholar Yusuf
role: Teaches advanced greetings and formal expressions

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ في مَكتَبَتي الخاصَّة
greeting.english: Welcome to my private study.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan bika fii maktabatii al-khaassa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً! لَقَد دَخَلتَ مَكاناً خاصّاً
lines.english: Welcome! You have entered a special place.
lines.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan! laqad dakhalta makaanan khaassan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا أَحتَفِظُ بِأَثمَنِ الكُتُبِ وَالمَخطوطات
lines.english: Here I keep my most precious books and manuscripts.
lines.transliteration: hunaa ahtafizu bi-athmani al-kutubi wal-makhtootaat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَتَعَلَّم التَّحِيّاتِ الرَّسمِيَّة
lines.english: Let us learn formal greetings.
lines.transliteration: linata'allam at-tahiyyaati ar-rasmiyya

choices.english: I want to look around first

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ مَرَّة أُخرى! هَل تُريدُ أَن نُكمِل؟
lines.english: You're back again! Shall we continue?
lines.transliteration: udta marratan ukhraa! hal turiidu an nukmil?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العِلمُ لا يَنتَهي أَبَداً
lines.english: Knowledge never ends.
lines.transliteration: al-ilmu laa yantahii abadan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَوَّلاً: تَشَرَّفنا — عِندَ المُقابَلَة الأولى
lines.english: First: tasharrafnaa — when meeting for the first time.
lines.transliteration: awwalan: tasharrafnaa — inda al-muqaabala al-uulaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثانِياً: حَيّاكَ الله — تَحِيَّة كَريمَة
lines.english: Second: hayyaaka allaah — a noble greeting.
lines.transliteration: thaaniyan: hayyaaka allaah — tahiyyatun kariima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مُمتاز! تَعَلَّمتَ تَحِيّاتٍ رَسمِيَّة
lines.english: Excellent! You have learned formal greetings.
lines.transliteration: mumtaaz! ta'allamta tahiyyaatin rasmiyya

name: Merchant Fatima
role: Teaches family-related vocabulary

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً! تَعالَ اِجلِس مَعَنا
greeting.english: Hello! Come sit with us.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan! ta'aala ijlis ma'anaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَباً في بَيتي! هُنا أَعيشُ مَعَ عائِلَتي
lines.english: Welcome to my home! I live here with my family.
lines.transliteration: marhaban fii baytii! hunaa a'iishu ma'a 'aa'ilatii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف كَلِمات العائِلَة بِالعَرَبِيَّة؟
lines.english: Do you know family words in Arabic?
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rif kalimaat al-'aa'ila bil-'arabiyya?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعالَ أُعَلِّمك!
lines.english: Come, let me teach you!
lines.transliteration: ta'aala u'allimak!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً مَرَّة ثانِيَة! العائِلَة هِيَ كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Welcome again! Family is everything.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marratan thaaniya! al-'aa'ila hiya kullu shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل نَتَعَلَّم كَلِمات جَديدَة؟
lines.english: Shall we learn new words?
lines.transliteration: hal nata'allam kalimaat jadiida?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُمّ — هَذِهِ أَغلى كَلِمَة
lines.english: Umm — this is the most precious word (mother).
lines.transliteration: umm — haadhihi aghlaa kalima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَب — الرَّجُل الكَبير في البَيت
lines.english: Ab — the elder man of the house (father).
lines.transliteration: ab — ar-rajul al-kabiir fil-bayt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَخ — مِثل صَديق لَكِن مِنَ الدَّم
lines.english: Akh — like a friend but from blood (brother).
lines.transliteration: akh — mithl sadiiq laakin mina ad-dam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُخت — البِنت مِن نَفس العائِلَة
lines.english: Ukht — the girl from the same family (sister).
lines.transliteration: ukht — al-bint min nafs al-'aa'ila

name: Librarian Ibrahim
role: Teaches numbers and counting in the archives

greeting.arabic: مَرْحَباً في الأَرشيف القَديم
greeting.english: Welcome to the ancient archives.
greeting.transliteration: marhaban fil-arshiif al-qadiim

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنتَ هُنا أَخيراً! قَليلونَ يَصِلونَ إلى هَذا المَكان
lines.english: You are here at last! Few reach this place.
lines.transliteration: anta hunaa akhiiran! qaliiluna yasiluuna ilaa haadha al-makaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرشيف يَحتَوي عَلى عُلومِ الأَرقام
lines.english: The archives contain the science of numbers.
lines.transliteration: al-arshiif yahtawii alaa 'uluumi al-arqaam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن تَتَعَلَّمَ العَدّ؟
lines.english: Do you want to learn counting?
lines.transliteration: hal turiidu an tata'allama al-'add?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الأَرشيف يَنتَظِرُكَ دائِماً
lines.english: The archives always await you.
lines.transliteration: al-arshiif yantaziruka daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ رَقم لَهُ قِصَّة
lines.english: Every number has a story.
lines.transliteration: kullu raqam lahu qissa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: واحِد — الرَّقم الأَوَّل
lines.english: Waahid — the first number (one).
lines.transliteration: waahid — ar-raqam al-awwal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِثنان — بَعدَ الواحِد
lines.english: Ithnaan — after one (two).
lines.transliteration: ithnaan — ba'da al-waahid

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَلاثَة — رَقمٌ مُبارَك
lines.english: Thalaatha — a blessed number (three).
lines.transliteration: thalaatha — raqmun mubaarak

name: Spice Seller Layla
role: Teaches spice and food vocabulary in her shop

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً في دُكّاني!
greeting.english: Welcome to my shop!
greeting.transliteration: ahlan wa sahlan fii dukkaanii!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يا هَلا! أَنا لَيلى، مَلِكَة البُهارات!
lines.english: Hello! I am Layla, queen of spices!
lines.transliteration: ya halaa! ana laylaa, malikat al-buhaaraat!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شُمّ هَذِهِ الرَّوائِح! كُلّ واحِدَة لَها اِسم
lines.english: Smell these aromas! Each one has a name.
lines.transliteration: shumm haadhihi ar-rawaa'ih! kullu waahida lahaa ism

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعالَ أُعَلِّمكَ أَسماءَ التَّوابِل والأَطعِمَة
lines.english: Come, I'll teach you the names of spices and foods.
lines.transliteration: ta'aala u'allimka asmaa' at-tawaabil wal-at'ima

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! هَل جُعتَ؟
lines.english: You're back! Are you hungry?
lines.transliteration: udta! hal ju'ta?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عِندي بُهارات جَديدَة اليَوم
lines.english: I have new spices today.
lines.transliteration: indii buhaaraat jadiida al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: فُلفُل — يُعطي الطَّعام حَرارَة
lines.english: Fulful — it gives food heat (pepper).
lines.transliteration: fulful — yu'tii at-ta'aam haraara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: زَعفَران — أَغلى بُهار في العالَم
lines.english: Za'faraan — the most expensive spice in the world (saffron).
lines.transliteration: za'faraan — aghlaa buhaar fil-'aalam

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: خُبز — نَأكُلُهُ كُلَّ يَوم
lines.english: Khubz — we eat it every day (bread).
lines.transliteration: khubz — na'kuluhu kulla yawm

name: Trader Hassan
role: Teaches clothing and textile vocabulary

greeting.arabic: تَفَضَّل! عِندي أَجمَل الأَقمِشَة
greeting.english: Come in! I have the finest textiles.
greeting.transliteration: tafaddal! indii ajmal al-aqmisha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً! أَنا حَسَّان، تاجِر الأَقمِشَة
lines.english: Hello! I am Hassan, the textile trader.
lines.transliteration: ahlan! ana hassaan, taajir al-aqmisha

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ قُماش لَهُ اِسم وَقِصَّة
lines.english: Every fabric has a name and a story.
lines.transliteration: kullu qumaash lahu ism wa qissa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن تَعرِفَ أَسماءَ المَلابِس؟
lines.english: Do you want to know the names of clothing?
lines.transliteration: hal turiidu an ta'rifa asmaa' al-malaabis?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً مَرَّة ثانِيَة يا صَديقي
lines.english: Welcome again, my friend.
lines.transliteration: ahlan marratan thaaniya ya sadiiqii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَصَلَت بَضائِع جَديدَة مِنَ الحَرير
lines.english: New silk goods have arrived.
lines.transliteration: wasalat badaa'i' jadiida mina al-hariir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ثَوب — المَلبَس التَّقليدي
lines.english: Thawb — the traditional garment.
lines.transliteration: thawb — al-malbas at-taqleedii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَباءَة — رِداء طَويل وَفَضفاض
lines.english: Abaaya — a long, loose cloak.
lines.transliteration: abaaya — ridaa' tawiil wa fadfaad

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حِذاء — ما نَلبَسُهُ في الأَرجُل
lines.english: Hidhaa — what we wear on our feet (shoes).
lines.transliteration: hidhaa' — maa nalbasuhu fil-arjul

name: Farmer Omar
role: Teaches nature and farming vocabulary

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ في بَيتي المُتَواضِع
greeting.english: Welcome to my humble home.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan bika fii baytii al-mutawaadi'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمْدُ لِلَّه! ضَيف في بَيتي
lines.english: Praise God! A guest in my home.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah! dayf fii baytii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا عُمَر، أَزرَع هَذِهِ الأَرض مُنذُ سِنين
lines.english: I am Omar, I have farmed this land for years.
lines.transliteration: ana 'umar, azra'u haadhihi al-ard mundhu siniin

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَتَحَدَّث عَن الطَّبيعَة!
lines.english: Let's talk about nature!
lines.transliteration: linatahaddath 'an at-tabii'a!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ! الأَرض خَضراء اليَوم
lines.english: You're back! The land is green today.
lines.transliteration: udta! al-ard khadraa' al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس وَاِشرَب شاياً
lines.english: Sit down and drink some tea.
lines.transliteration: ijlis wa ishrab shaayan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَجَرَة — هِيَ أُمّ الظِّل
lines.english: Shajara — she is the mother of shade (tree).
lines.transliteration: shajara — hiya umm az-zill

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: ماء — الحَياة نَفسُها
lines.english: Maa' — life itself (water).
lines.transliteration: maa' — al-hayaat nafsuhaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شَمس — تُنيرُ كُلَّ شَيء
lines.english: Shams — it lights everything (sun).
lines.transliteration: shams — tuniiru kulla shay'

name: Elder Tariq
role: Teaches time-related vocabulary and Bedouin wisdom

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً بِالضَّيف في خَيمَتي
greeting.english: Welcome, guest, to my tent.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan bid-dayf fii khaymatii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيكُم! اِجلِس عَلى هَذِهِ السَّجّادَة
lines.english: Peace be upon you! Sit on this carpet.
lines.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum! ijlis alaa haadhihi as-sajjaada

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الوَقت هُوَ أَثمَن شَيء عِندَ البَدو
lines.english: Time is the most precious thing to the Bedouin.
lines.transliteration: al-waqt huwa athman shay' inda al-badw

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَأُعَلِّمُكَ كَلِمات الوَقت
lines.english: I will teach you the words of time.
lines.transliteration: sa'u'allimuka kalimaat al-waqt

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الوَقت يَمُرّ كَالرِّياح في الصَّحراء
lines.english: Time passes like the winds in the desert.
lines.transliteration: al-waqt yamurr kar-riyaah fis-sahraa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَكِن دائِماً هُناكَ وَقت لِلتَّعَلُّم
lines.english: But there is always time for learning.
lines.transliteration: laakin daa'iman hunaaka waqt lit-ta'allum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَباح — أَوَّل الضَّوء
lines.english: Sabaah — the first light (morning).
lines.transliteration: sabaah — awwal ad-daw'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لَيل — عِندَما تَظهَر النُّجوم
lines.english: Layl — when the stars appear (night).
lines.transliteration: layl — indamaa tazhar an-nujuum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: يَوم — مِنَ الشُّروق إلى الغُروب
lines.english: Yawm — from sunrise to sunset (day).
lines.transliteration: yawm — mina ash-shuruuq ilaa al-ghuruub

name: Guide Salim
role: Teaches adjectives and descriptive vocabulary

greeting.arabic: أَهْلاً! اِستَرِح مِنَ الطَّريق
greeting.english: Hello! Rest from the journey.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan! istarih mina at-tariiq

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مَرْحَباً في بَيتي عَلى الجَبَل
lines.english: Welcome to my home on the mountain.
lines.transliteration: marhaban fii baytii alaa al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِنْ هُنا نَرى كُلّ شَيء — كَبير وَصَغير
lines.english: From here we see everything — big and small.
lines.transliteration: min hunaa naraa kulla shay' — kabiir wa saghiir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: لِنَتَعَلَّم كَيفَ نَصِف الأَشياء
lines.english: Let's learn how to describe things.
lines.transliteration: linata'allam kayfa nasif al-ashyaa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَبَل جَميل اليَوم
lines.english: The mountain is beautiful today.
lines.transliteration: al-jabal jamiil al-yawm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن نَتَعَلَّم صِفات جَديدَة؟
lines.english: Do you want to learn new adjectives?
lines.transliteration: hal turiidu an nata'allam sifaat jadiida?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كَبير — مِثل الجَبَل
lines.english: Kabiir — like the mountain (big).
lines.transliteration: kabiir — mithl al-jabal

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: صَغير — مِثل الحَصى
lines.english: Saghiir — like the pebbles (small).
lines.transliteration: saghiir — mithl al-hasaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: جَميل — مِثل هَذا المَنظَر
lines.english: Jamiil — like this view (beautiful).
lines.transliteration: jamiil — mithl haadha al-manzar

name: Imam Muhammad
role: Teaches spiritual greetings and respectful phrases

greeting.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَيكُم وَرَحمَة الله
greeting.english: Peace and God's mercy be upon you.
greeting.transliteration: as-salaamu alaykum wa rahmatu allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً بِكَ في بَيتِ الله
lines.english: Welcome to the house of God.
lines.transliteration: ahlan bika fii bayti allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هُنا نَتَعَلَّم الكَلِمات الَّتي تُقَرِّبُنا مِنَ الله
lines.english: Here we learn words that bring us closer to God.
lines.transliteration: hunaa nata'allam al-kalimaat allatii tuqarribunaa mina allaah

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَأُعَلِّمُكَ عِبارات الاِحتِرام والدُّعاء
lines.english: I will teach you phrases of respect and prayer.
lines.transliteration: sa'u'allimuka ibaaraat al-ihtiraam wad-du'aa'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بابُ المَسجِد مَفتوح دائِماً
lines.english: The mosque door is always open.
lines.transliteration: baabu al-masjid maftuuh daa'iman

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: تَعالَ مَتى شِئتَ لِلتَّعَلُّم
lines.english: Come whenever you wish to learn.
lines.transliteration: ta'aala mataa shi'ta lit-ta'allum

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: بِسمِ الله — نَقولُها قَبلَ كُلّ شَيء
lines.english: Bismillaah — we say it before everything (in God's name).
lines.transliteration: bismillaah — naquuluhaa qabla kulli shay'

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحَمْدُ لِلَّه — شُكر لِلَّه عَلى نِعَمِه
lines.english: Al-hamdu lillaah — thanks to God for His blessings.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah — shukr lillaah alaa ni'amihi

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: إِن شاءَ الله — عِندَما نَتَحَدَّث عَنِ المُستَقبَل
lines.english: In shaa' allaah — when we speak about the future (God willing).
lines.transliteration: in shaa' allaah — indamaa natahaddath anil-mustaqbal

name: Captain Rashid
role: Teaches food and drink vocabulary in the tavern

greeting.arabic: يا هَلا بِالبَحّار الجَديد!
greeting.english: Welcome, new sailor!
greeting.transliteration: ya halaa bil-bahhaar al-jadiid!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهْلاً! اِجلِس وَكُل! البَحر يَفتَح الشَّهِيَّة
lines.english: Welcome! Sit and eat! The sea opens the appetite.
lines.transliteration: ahlan! ijlis wa kul! al-bahr yaftah ash-shahiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا رَشيد، كُنتُ قُبطاناً والآن أُطعِم البَحّارَة
lines.english: I am Rashid, I was a captain and now I feed the sailors.
lines.transliteration: ana rashiid, kuntu qubtaanan wal-aan ut'im al-bahhaara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَعرِف أَسماء الأَطعِمَة؟
lines.english: Do you know the names of foods?
lines.transliteration: hal ta'rif asmaa' al-at'ima?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ لِلحانَة! هَل البَطن فارِغ؟
lines.english: Back at the tavern! Is the belly empty?
lines.transliteration: udta lil-haana! hal al-batn faarigh?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: اِجلِس، الطَّعام جاهِز
lines.english: Sit down, the food is ready.
lines.transliteration: ijlis, at-ta'aam jaahiz

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَمَك — مِنَ البَحر مُباشَرَة
lines.english: Samak — straight from the sea (fish).
lines.transliteration: samak — mina al-bahr mubaashara

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَرُزّ — أَساس كُلّ وَجبَة
lines.english: Aruzz — the base of every meal (rice).
lines.transliteration: aruzz — asaas kulli wajba

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: شاي — نَشرَبُهُ بَعدَ الأَكل
lines.english: Shaay — we drink it after eating (tea).
lines.transliteration: shaay — nashrabuhu ba'da al-akl

name: Vizier Abbas
role: Teaches formal Arabic and courtly expressions

greeting.arabic: مَن أَذِنَ لَكَ بِالدُّخول؟
greeting.english: Who permitted you to enter?
greeting.transliteration: man adhina laka bid-dukhuul?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِف! أَنتَ في قاعَة العَرش المَلَكِيَّة
lines.english: Halt! You are in the Royal Throne Room.
lines.transliteration: qif! anta fii qaa'at al-arsh al-malakiyya

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الوَزير عَبّاس. هُنا نَتَكَلَّم بِالفُصحى فَقَط
lines.english: I am Vizier Abbas. Here we speak only in formal Arabic.
lines.transliteration: ana al-waziir abbaas. hunaa natakallam bil-fushaa faqat

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: إِذا كُنتَ تُريدُ البَقاء، تَعَلَّم كَيفَ تَتَكَلَّم أَمامَ المَلِك
lines.english: If you wish to stay, learn how to speak before the king.
lines.transliteration: idhaa kunta turiidu al-baqaa', ta'allam kayfa tatakallam amaama al-malik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عُدتَ مَرَّة أُخرى. أَرجو أَن تَكونَ قَد تَعَلَّمت
lines.english: You return again. I hope you have learned.
lines.transliteration: udta marratan ukhraa. arjuu an takuuna qad ta'allamta

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَلِك لا يُحِبّ الجَهل
lines.english: The king does not tolerate ignorance.
lines.transliteration: al-malik laa yuhibb al-jahl

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَضرَة — لَقَب اِحتِرام لِلمَلِك
lines.english: Hadra — a title of respect for the king (Your Majesty).
lines.transliteration: hadra — laqab ihtiraam lil-malik

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَمَرَ — فِعل المَلِك: أَمَرَ وَأَطَعنا
lines.english: Amara — the king's verb: he commanded and we obeyed.
lines.transliteration: amara — fi'l al-malik: amara wa ata'naa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَدل — أَهَمّ صِفَة لِلحاكِم
lines.english: Adl — the most important quality for a ruler (justice).
lines.transliteration: 'adl — ahamm sifa lil-haakim

name: Mysterious Traveler
role: A traveler who only appears after you have met the scholar

greeting.arabic: أَهلاً يا طالِب العِلم... سَمِعتُ أَنَّكَ تَلتَقي بِيوسُف
greeting.english: Hello, seeker of knowledge... I heard you met Yusuf.
greeting.transliteration: ahlan ya taalib al-ilm... sami'tu annaka talqa bi-yuusuf

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الرِّحلَة إلى المَعرِفَة تَبدَأ بِخُطوَة
lines.english: The journey to knowledge begins with a step.
lines.transliteration: ar-rihla ilaa al-ma'rifa tabda' bi-khutwa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا مُسافِر. رَأَيتُ بِلاداً كَثيرَة وَتَعَلَّمتُ لُغاتٍ كَثيرَة
lines.english: I am a traveler. I have seen many lands and learned many languages.
lines.transliteration: ana musaafir. ra'aytu bilaadan kathiira wa ta'allamtu lughaat kathiira

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: العَرَبِيَّة — لُغَة الشِّعر وَالحِكمَة وَالعِلم
lines.english: Arabic — the language of poetry, wisdom, and science.
lines.transliteration: al-arabiyya — lughat ash-shi'r wal-hikma wal-'ilm

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: رَحَلتُ مِن الأَندَلُس إلى بَغداد — شَهرَيْن عَلى الجَمَل
lines.english: I traveled from Andalusia to Baghdad — two months on camel.
lines.transliteration: rahaltu min al-andalus ilaa baghdaad — shahrayn 'alaa al-jamal
lines.culturalNote: The medieval Islamic world was connected by vast trade and pilgrimage routes. Traveling from Cordoba in Andalusia (Spain) to Baghdad took months by camel caravan.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في كُلّ مَدينَة تَعَلَّمتُ كَلِمات جَديدَة — التُّجّار يَتَحَدَّثون العَرَبِيَّة في كُلّ مَكان
lines.english: In every city I learned new words — traders speak Arabic everywhere.
lines.transliteration: fii kull madiina ta'allamtu kalimaat jadiida — at-tujjaar yatahadathoon al-arabiyya fii kull makaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: سَفَر — هَذِهِ كَلِمَة مُهِمَّة لِلمُسافِر
lines.english: Safar — this is an important word for a traveler.
lines.transliteration: safar — haadhihi kalima muhimma lil-musaafir

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "safari" الإنجليزِيَّة جاءَت مِن العَرَبِيَّة — سَفَري
lines.english: And the English word "safari" came from Arabic — safarii (my journey).
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "safari" al-injliiziyya jaa'at min al-arabiyya — safarii
lines.culturalNote: "Safari" comes from Arabic safar (سَفَر, journey). Arab merchants and explorers established the trade routes across East Africa that later European explorers would follow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: كُلّ يَوم جَديد فُرصَة لِلتَّعَلُّم
lines.english: Every new day is an opportunity to learn.
lines.transliteration: kull yawm jadiid fursa lit-ta'allum

name: Night Guard
role: A guard who only patrols after dark

greeting.arabic: قِف! مَن أَنتَ في هذا الوَقت المُتَأَخِّر؟
greeting.english: Halt! Who goes there at this late hour?
greeting.transliteration: qif! man anta fii haadhaa al-waqt al-muta'akhkhir?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المَنطِقَة آمِنَة. تَوَقَّف عِندَ الحاجَة
lines.english: The area is safe. Stop if you need anything.
lines.transliteration: al-mantiqа aamina. tawqqaf 'inda al-haaja

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَنا الحارِس اللَّيلي. أَحمي المَدينَة مِن الغُروب إلى الفَجر
lines.english: I am the night guard. I protect the city from sunset to dawn.
lines.transliteration: ana al-haaris al-laylii. ahmi al-madiina min al-ghuroob ilaa al-fajr

choices.arabic: هَل تَعلَم شَيئاً عَن هَذِهِ المَدينَة؟
choices.english: Do you know something about this city?
How do you say "safety" in Arabic?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَذِهِ المَدينَة قَديمَة جِدَّاً. بُنِيَت قَبلَ مِئَة وَخَمسين سَنَة
lines.english: This city is very old. It was built 150 years ago.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi al-madiina qadiima jiddan. buniyat qabla mi'a wa khamsiin sana

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الحُراسُ الأَوائِل كانوا يَحفَظون القُرآن — كانَت تِلاوَتُهُم تُبعِد الشَّرّ
lines.english: The first guards memorized the Quran — their recitation was said to ward off evil.
lines.transliteration: al-hurrasu al-awaa'il kaanuu yahfazoon al-qur'an — kaanat tilaawatuhum tub'id ash-sharr

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَمَان — هَذِهِ الكَلِمَة الجَميلَة
lines.english: Amaan — this beautiful word.
lines.transliteration: amaan — haadhihi al-kalima al-jamiila

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: وَكَلِمَة "آمِن" تَعني safe — نَفس الجَذر: أ-م-ن
lines.english: And "aamin" means safe — same root: A-M-N.
lines.transliteration: wa kalima "aamin" ta'nii safe — nafs al-jadhr: a-m-n

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الجَذر العَرَبي يُعطيك عَشَرات الكَلِمات مِن ثَلاثَة حُروف
lines.english: The Arabic root gives you dozens of words from three letters.
lines.transliteration: al-jadhr al-arabii yu'tiika 'asharaat al-kalimaat min thalaatha huroof
lines.culturalNote: The Arabic root system (trilateral roots) is one of the most systematic in the world. The root A-M-N (أ-م-ن) generates: amaan (safety), aamin (safe), mu'min (believer), iimaan (faith), amiin (trustworthy).

name: Amira
role: The Chronicler — grammar specialist, Ancient Library companion

greeting.arabic: يا سلام، وَجَدتُكَ أَخيراً! أَنا أَميرَة المُؤَرِّخَة
greeting.english: How wonderful, I've found you at last! I am Amira the Chronicler.
greeting.transliteration: ya salaam, wajadtuka akhiiran! ana amira al-mu'arriikha

lines.arabic: يا سلام! أَنتَ إذاً العالِمُ الذي أَتقَنَ المَكتَبَة؟
lines.english: How wonderful! So you are the scholar who mastered the library?
lines.transliteration: ya salaam! anta idhan al-'aalim alladhi atqana al-maktaba?

lines.arabic: أَنا أَميرَة — أُرَكِّزُ عَلى النَّحوِ وَالجُمَل. سِجِلِّي يَحتاجُ إلى مُساعَدَتِك
lines.english: I am Amira — I focus on grammar and sentences. My chronicle needs your help.
lines.transliteration: ana amira — urakkiz 'ala an-nahw wal-jumal. sijilli yahtaaj ila musa'adatik

lines.arabic: هَل تَقبَلُ أَن تُساعِدَني في إِتمام سِجِلِّي التّاريخي؟
lines.english: Will you accept to help me complete my historical chronicle?
lines.transliteration: hal taqbalu an tusa'idani fi itmam sijilli at-tariikhi?

lines.arabic: سِجِلّي يَعتَمِدُ عَلى تَحليلِ النُّصوص — كُلُّ جُملَة تَحتاجُ قارِئاً يَفهَمُ النَّحو
lines.english: My chronicle relies on textual analysis — every sentence needs a reader who understands grammar.
lines.transliteration: sijilli ya'tamid 'ala tahlil an-nusuus — kullu jumla tahtaaj qaari'an yafham an-nahw

lines.arabic: سِجِلّي يَتَتَبَّعُ رِحَل العُلَماء — كُلُّ مَكانٍ مَشَوا فيهِ تَرَكَ أَثَراً في اللُّغَة
lines.english: My chronicle traces scholars' journeys — every place they walked left a mark on language.
lines.transliteration: sijilli yatatabba' rihal al-'ulamaa' — kullu makaanin mashaw fiihi taraka atharan fil-lugha

lines.arabic: سِجِلّي يَحفَظُ التّاريخَ اللُّغَوي — كُلُّ حَقبَة أَضافَت إلى العَرَبيَّة كَلِمات جَديدَة
lines.english: My chronicle preserves linguistic history — every era added new words to Arabic.
lines.transliteration: sijilli yahfaz at-taariikh al-lughawi — kullu haqba adaafat ilaa al-arabiyya kalimaat jadiida

lines.arabic: يا سلام! أَتمَمنا السِّجِلَّ مَعاً. النَّحوُ وَالجُمَلُ الآن مَحفوظَةٌ لِلأَبَد
lines.english: How wonderful! We completed the chronicle together. Grammar and sentences are now preserved forever.
lines.transliteration: ya salaam! atmamna as-sijill ma'an. an-nahw wal-jumal al-aan mahfuuza lil-abad

name: Khalid
role: The Desert Wanderer — vocabulary specialist, Oasis Village companion

greeting.arabic: الحمد لله! وَجَدتُ رَفيقَ طَريقٍ جَديد
greeting.english: Praise be to God! I found a new travelling companion.
greeting.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah! wajadtu rafiiq taariq jadiid

lines.arabic: الحمد لله! أَنتَ تَعرِفُ كَلِمات الواحَة. أَنا خالِد — رَحّالَة الصَّحراء
lines.english: Praise be to God! You know the oasis words. I am Khalid — the desert wanderer.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah! anta ta'rif kalimaat al-waaha. ana khaalid — rahhaala as-sahraa'

lines.arabic: أُريدُ إِنشاءَ أَطلَسِ مُفرَدات — خَريطَةَ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ في كُلِّ طَريق
lines.english: I want to create a vocabulary atlas — a map of every word on every route.
lines.transliteration: uriidu inshaa' atlas mufradaat — khariitat kull kalima fi kull tariq

lines.arabic: هَل تُساعِدُني في تَسجيل كَلِمات الطَّريق؟
lines.english: Will you help me record the route vocabulary?
lines.transliteration: hal tusa'iduni fi tasjil kalimaat at-tariq?

lines.arabic: الأَطلَسُ يَحتاجُ تَصنيفاً دَقيقاً — الجُذور أَوَّلاً، ثُمَّ المُشتَقّات، ثُمَّ الاستِخدام
lines.english: The atlas needs precise classification — roots first, then derivatives, then usage.
lines.transliteration: al-atlas yahtaaj tasniifan daqiiqan — al-judhuur awwalan, thumma al-mushtaqqaat, thumma al-istikhdaam

lines.arabic: كُلُّ طَريقٍ لَه لُغَتُه — الأَطلَسُ سَيُريكَ أَينَ يَلتَقي المُسافِرون بِالكَلِمات
lines.english: Every route has its language — the atlas will show you where travelers meet words.
lines.transliteration: kullu tariiqin lahu lughatu — al-atlas sa-yuriika ayna yaltaqii al-musaafiriin bil-kalimaat

lines.arabic: الكَلِمات تَنتَقِلُ مَعَ التُّجّار وَالجُيوش — الأَطلَسُ سَيَكشِفُ كَيفَ اِنتَشَرَت العَرَبيَّة عَبرَ التّاريخ
lines.english: Words travel with merchants and armies — the atlas will reveal how Arabic spread through history.
lines.transliteration: al-kalimaat tantaqil ma'a at-tujjaar wal-juyuush — al-atlas sa-yakshif kayfa intasharat al-arabiyya 'abra at-taariikh

lines.arabic: الحمد لله! الأَطلَسُ مُكتَمِل. كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ في مَكانِها
lines.english: Praise be to God! The atlas is complete. Every word in its place.
lines.transliteration: al-hamdu lillaah! al-atlas muktamil. kull kalima fi makaaniha

name: Zahra
role: The Flower Speaker — pronunciation specialist, Coastal Port companion

greeting.arabic: ما شاء الله! صَوتُكَ يَحمِلُ لَحنَ اللُّغَة
greeting.english: God has willed it! Your voice carries the melody of language.
greeting.transliteration: maa shaa' allaah! sawtuka yahmil lahn al-lugha

lines.arabic: ما شاء الله! أَنتَ تُتقِنُ المِيناء. أَنا زَهرَة — أُعَلِّمُ النُّطقَ بِالشِّعر
lines.english: God has willed it! You've mastered the port. I am Zahra — I teach pronunciation through poetry.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa' allaah! anta tutqin al-miinaa'. ana zahra — u'allim an-nutq bish-shi'r

lines.arabic: كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَتَفَتَّحُ كَزَهرَةٍ حين تَنطِقُها بِصِحَّة
lines.english: Every word blooms like a flower when you pronounce it correctly.
lines.transliteration: kull kalima tatafatahu kazahra hiin tantiquha bissiha

lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن تَنظِمَ مَعي بَيتاً يَتَفَتَّحُ بِالنُّطق الصَّحيح؟
lines.english: Would you like to compose with me a verse that blooms with correct pronunciation?
lines.transliteration: hal turiidu an tanzim ma'i baytan yatafatahu bin-nutq as-sahiih?

lines.arabic: النُّطقُ الصَّحيح يَكشِفُ المَعنى الخَفيَّ — العالِمُ يَسمَعُ فَرقاً بَينَ ضاد وَظاء
lines.english: Correct pronunciation reveals hidden meaning — the scholar hears the difference between Daad and Dhaa.
lines.transliteration: an-nutq as-sahiih yakshif al-ma'na al-khafiyy — al-'aalim yasma' farqan bayna dhaad wa dhaa

lines.arabic: في كُلِّ مِيناء لَهجَةٌ مُختَلِفَة — الشِّعرُ يُعَلِّمُكَ كَيفَ تُكَلِّمُ كُلَّ النّاس
lines.english: Every port has a different dialect — poetry teaches you how to speak to all people.
lines.transliteration: fii kulli miinaa' lahja mukhtalifa — ash-shi'r yu'allimuka kayfa tukallim kull an-naas

lines.arabic: الشِّعرُ العَرَبيُّ حَفِظَ اللُّغَة خِلالَ قُرونِ التَّحَوُّلات — كُلُّ بَيتٍ نافِذَةٌ إلى الماضي
lines.english: Arabic poetry preserved the language through centuries of change — every verse is a window to the past.
lines.transliteration: ash-shi'r al-arabiyy hafiz al-lugha khilaal quruun at-tahawwulaat — kullu bayt naafidha ilaa al-maadi

lines.arabic: ما شاء الله! البَيتُ مُكتَمِل. نُطقُكَ أَصبَحَ كَنَسيم الأَزهار
lines.english: God has willed it! The verse is complete. Your pronunciation has become like a flower breeze.
lines.transliteration: maa shaa' allaah! al-bayt muktamil. nutquka asbaha ka-nasim al-azhaar

name: Omar
role: The Market Keeper — vocabulary specialist, Desert Marketplace companion

greeting.arabic: طبعاً! أَنا عُمَر — كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ عِندي لَها سِعر
greeting.english: Of course! I am Omar — every word with me has a price.
greeting.transliteration: tab'an! ana 'umar — kull kalima 'indi laha si'r

lines.arabic: طبعاً! أَنتَ تُتقِنُ السُّوق. لَكِن دَفتَري المَفقود — مُشكِلَتي الكُبرى
lines.english: Of course! You've mastered the market. But my lost ledger — my biggest problem.
lines.transliteration: tab'an! anta tutqin as-suuq. laakin daftari al-mafquud — mushkilati al-kubraa

lines.arabic: كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ في الدَّفتَر تُساوي سُمعَتي التِّجارِيَّة
lines.english: Every word in the ledger is worth my trade reputation.
lines.transliteration: kull kalima fid-daftar tusaawi sum'ati at-tijariyya

lines.arabic: هَل تُساعِدُني في اِسترِداد كَلِمات دَفتَري؟
lines.english: Will you help me recover the words from my ledger?
lines.transliteration: hal tusa'iduni fi istirdaad kalimaat daftari?

lines.arabic: الدَّفتَرُ يَستَخدِمُ مُصطَلَحاتٍ تِجارِيَّةً دَقيقَة — فَقَط عالِمٌ بِالعَرَبيَّة يَفهَمُها
lines.english: The ledger uses precise trade terminology — only a scholar of Arabic can understand it.
lines.transliteration: ad-daftar yastakhdam mustalahaatan tijaariyya daqiiqa — faqat 'aalim bil-arabiyya yafhamuhaa

lines.arabic: الدَّفتَرُ ضائِعٌ في طَريقِ السُّوق — مَن يَعرِفُ طُرُقَ التُّجّار سَيَجِدُه
lines.english: The ledger is lost on the market route — one who knows the traders' paths will find it.
lines.transliteration: ad-daftar dhaa'i' fi tariiq as-suuq — man ya'rif turuq at-tujjaar sa-yajiduhu

lines.arabic: هَذا الدَّفتَرُ كُتِبَ عَلى طَريقَة تُجّار الحَرير — مَن يَعرِفُ التّاريخَ التِّجاري سَيَفهَمُ لُغَتَه
lines.english: This ledger was written in the style of Silk Road merchants — one who knows trade history will understand its language.
lines.transliteration: haadhaa ad-daftar kutib 'ala tariiqa tujjaar al-hariir — man ya'rif at-taariikh at-tijaariyy sa-yafham lughataه

lines.arabic: طبعاً! سُمعَتي عادَت. كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ في مَكانِها الصَّحيح
lines.english: Of course! My reputation is restored. Every word in its rightful place.
lines.transliteration: tab'an! sum'ati 'aadat. kull kalima fi makaaniha as-saahih

name: Layla
role: The Night Scholar — grammar specialist, Ancient Library companion

greeting.arabic: صحيح. أَنا لَيلى — أَعمَلُ في اللَّيل حينَ يَنامُ الآخَرون
greeting.english: Correct. I am Layla — I work at night while the others sleep.
greeting.transliteration: saahih. ana layla — a'mal fil-layl hiina yanaam al-aakhiruun

lines.arabic: صحيح! أَنتَ تُتقِنُ المَكتَبَة. أَنا أُصَحِّحُ مَخطوطَةً في سِرٍّ
lines.english: Correct! You've mastered the library. I am secretly correcting a manuscript.
lines.transliteration: saahih! anta tutqin al-maktaba. ana usahhih makhtuuta fi sirr

lines.arabic: الأَخطاءُ النَّحوِيَّةُ كَالجُروح — يَجِبُ تَضميدُها قَبلَ الفَجر
lines.english: Grammar errors are like wounds — they must be bandaged before dawn.
lines.transliteration: al-akhta' an-nahwiyya kaljuruuh — yajibu tadmiiduhaa qabl al-fajr

lines.arabic: أَحتاجُ إلى عالِمٍ واحِدٍ لِلتَّحَقُّق مِن عَمَلي. هَل أَنتَ ذَلِكَ العالِم؟
lines.english: I need one scholar to verify my work. Are you that scholar?
lines.transliteration: ahtaaju ila 'aalim waahid lit-tahaqquq min 'amali. hal anta dhaalika al-'aalim?

lines.arabic: النَّحوُ لَيسَ قُيوداً — هُوَ مَنطِقُ اللُّغَة الَّذي يَجعَلُ كُلَّ جُملَةٍ قَصيدَة
lines.english: Grammar is not chains — it is the logic of language that makes every sentence a poem.
lines.transliteration: an-nahw laysa quyuudan — huwa mantiq al-lugha alladhi yaj'al kull jumla qasiida

lines.arabic: اللَّيلُ وَقتُ التَّفكير — المُسافِرُ يَتَعَلَّمُ اللُّغَة حينَ يَسكُنُ المَكان لَيلاً
lines.english: Night is the time for reflection — the traveler learns language when they rest in a place at night.
lines.transliteration: al-layl waqt at-tafkiir — al-musaafir yata'allam al-lugha hiina yaskun al-makaan laylan

lines.arabic: المَخطوطاتُ كُتِبَت لَيلاً في أَغلَبِ الأَحيان — النُّسّاخُ عَمِلوا عَلى ضَوءِ الشَّمعَةِ لِيَحفَظوا المَعرِفَة لِلأَجيال
lines.english: Most manuscripts were written at night — scribes worked by candlelight to preserve knowledge for generations.
lines.transliteration: al-makhtuutaat kutibbat laylan fii aghalab al-ahyaan — an-nussaakh 'amiluu 'ala daw' ash-sham'a li-yahfazuu al-ma'rifa lil-ajyaal

lines.arabic: صحيح! التَّصحيحاتُ مُكتَمِلَة. النَّحوُ مَحفوظٌ لِلأَجيال
lines.english: Correct! The corrections are complete. Grammar is preserved for generations.
lines.transliteration: saahih! at-tashiihaat muktamila. an-nahw mahfuuz lil-ajyaal

name: Hassan
role: The Mountain Guide — culture specialist, Mountain Village companion

greeting.arabic: بسم الله. أَنا حَسَن — دَليلُ الجِبال وَحارِسُ التُّراث
greeting.english: In the name of God. I am Hassan — the mountain guide and guardian of heritage.
greeting.transliteration: bismillaah. ana hassan — daliil al-jibal wa haaris at-turaath

lines.arabic: بسم الله. أَنتَ اجتَزتَ حِكمَةَ الجَبَل. جَديرٌ بِالاطِّلاع عَلى المِيثاق
lines.english: In the name of God. You have passed the mountain wisdom. Worthy to see the code.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah. anta ijtazta hikmat al-jabal. jadiir bil-ittilaa' 'alal-miithaaq

lines.arabic: مِيثاقُ المُحارِب القَديم — كُلُّ فَضيلَةٍ بِاسمِها العَرَبيِّ الكِلاسيكي
lines.english: The ancient warrior code — every virtue named in classical Arabic.
lines.transliteration: miithaaq al-muharib al-qadiim — kull fadiila bi-ismiha al-'arabi al-kilaasiiki

lines.arabic: هَل تَستَطيعُ حِفظَهُ وَتِلاوَتَهُ وَفقَ تَقليد الهِضاب؟
lines.english: Can you memorise it and recite it according to the highland tradition?
lines.transliteration: hal tastati'u hifzahu wa tilaawatahu wafq taqliid al-hidaab?

lines.arabic: المِيثاقُ مَكتوبٌ بِالعَرَبِيَّة الفُصحى القَديمَة — يَحتاجُ عالِماً يَفهَمُ تَصريفَ الأَفعال
lines.english: The code is written in ancient Classical Arabic — it needs a scholar who understands verb conjugation.
lines.transliteration: al-miithaaq maktuum bil-arabiyya al-fushaa al-qadiima — yahtaaj 'aaliman yafham tasriif al-af'aal

lines.arabic: المِيثاقُ يُصاحِبُ المُحارِبَ في كُلِّ رِحلَة — المُسافِرُ الشُّجاعُ يَحفَظُهُ عَن ظَهرِ قَلب
lines.english: The code accompanies the warrior on every journey — the brave traveler memorises it by heart.
lines.transliteration: al-miithaaq yusaahib al-muharib fii kulli rihlla — al-musaafir ash-shujaa' yahfazuhu 'an zhahr qalb

lines.arabic: المِيثاقُ أَقدَمُ مِنَ الإسلام — جُذورُهُ في قَوانينِ القَبائِل العَرَبيَّة قَبلَ الكِتابَة
lines.english: The code is older than Islam — its roots lie in Arab tribal laws from before writing existed.
lines.transliteration: al-miithaaq aqdamu min al-islaam — judhuuruhu fii qawaniin al-qabaa'il al-arabiyya qabl al-kitaaba

lines.arabic: بسم الله. حَفِظتَ المِيثاق. أَنتَ الآنَ جُزءٌ مِن تُراثِ الجَبَل
lines.english: In the name of God. You memorised the code. You are now part of the mountain's heritage.
lines.transliteration: bismillaah. hafizta al-miithaaq. anta al-aan juz' min turaath al-jabal

name: Fatima
role: The Ruin Keeper — culture specialist, Royal Palace companion

greeting.arabic: سُبحان الله! هَذا المَكانُ يَروي قِصَصَ الأُمَم
greeting.english: Glory be to God! This place tells the stories of nations.
greeting.transliteration: subhaana allaah! haadha al-makaan yarwii qisas al-umam

lines.arabic: سُبحان الله! أَنتَ أَتقَنتَ العَرَبِيَّة. اِكتَشَفتُ أَرشيفاً مَخفِيَّاً
lines.english: Glory be to God! You've mastered Arabic. I've discovered a hidden archive.
lines.transliteration: subhaana allaah! anta atqanta al-arabiyya. iktashaftu arshifan makhfiyyan

lines.arabic: النُّقوشُ الثَّقافِيَّةُ تَحتاجُ إلى صَوتٍ يُحييها — صَوتِكَ
lines.english: The cultural inscriptions need a voice to bring them to life — your voice.
lines.transliteration: an-nuquush ath-thaqaafiyya tahtaaju ila sawt yuhyiiha — sawtik

lines.arabic: هَل تَقرَأُ النُّقوشَ مَعي حَتَّى نُؤَرِّخَها؟
lines.english: Will you read the inscriptions with me so we can archive them?
lines.transliteration: hal taqra' an-nuquush ma'ii hatta nu'arrikha?

lines.arabic: النُّقوشُ بِالعَرَبيَّة المُبكِّرَة — تَحليلُها يَكشِفُ كَيفَ تَطَوَّرَت الكِتابَة مِن الرَّسمِ إلى الحُرف
lines.english: The inscriptions are in early Arabic — analysing them reveals how writing evolved from images to letters.
lines.transliteration: an-nuquush bil-arabiyya al-mubakkira — tahliluhaa yakshif kayfa tatawwarat al-kitaaba min ar-rasm ilaa al-harf

lines.arabic: النُّقوشُ وَجَدتُها في طُرُق القَوافِل — كُلُّ نَقشٍ عَلامَةٌ تَرَكَها مُسافِرٌ لِمَن بَعدَه
lines.english: I found the inscriptions on caravan routes — every inscription is a sign left by a traveler for those who follow.
lines.transliteration: an-nuquush wajadtuhaa fii turuq al-qawaafil — kullu naqshin 'alaama tarakahaa musaafir liman ba'dahu

lines.arabic: هَذِهِ النُّقوشُ تَعودُ إلى ما قَبلَ الإسلام — إنَّها تَرابُطُ الحَضارات العَرَبيَّة عَبرَ الأَجيال
lines.english: These inscriptions date to pre-Islamic times — they are the continuity of Arab civilisations across the ages.
lines.transliteration: haadhihi an-nuquush ta'uud ilaa maa qabl al-islaam — innahaa taraabutu al-hadaaraat al-arabiyya 'abra al-ajyaal

lines.arabic: سُبحان الله! الأَرشيفُ مُكتَمِل. الكَلِماتُ حَيَّةٌ مِن جَديد
lines.english: Glory be to God! The archive is complete. The words are alive again.
lines.transliteration: subhaana allaah! al-arshiif muktamil. al-kalimaat hayya min jadiid

name: Ali
role: The Oasis Healer — pronunciation specialist, Oasis Village companion

greeting.arabic: إن شاء الله، صِحَّتُكَ طَيِّبَة. أَنا عَليّ — طَبيبُ الواحَة
greeting.english: God willing, your health is good. I am Ali — the oasis healer.
greeting.transliteration: in shaa' allaah, sihhutuka tayyiba. ana 'ali — tabiib al-waaha

lines.arabic: إن شاء الله، أَنتَ تَعرِفُ الواحَة. أَحتاجُ مَن يَتَعَلَّمُ دُعاءَ الشِّفاء
lines.english: God willing, you know the oasis. I need someone to learn the healing prayer.
lines.transliteration: in shaa' allaah, anta ta'rif al-waaha. ahtaaju man yata'allamu du'aa' ash-shifaa'

lines.arabic: الدُّعاءُ بِالعَرَبِيَّة الكِلاسيكِيَّة — نُطقُهُ يَجِبُ أَن يَكونَ سَليماً
lines.english: The prayer in classical Arabic — its pronunciation must be correct.
lines.transliteration: ad-du'aa' bil-arabiyya al-kilaasiikiyya — nutquhu yajibu an yakuuna saliiman

lines.arabic: هَل تَتَعَلَّمُ الدُّعاءَ مَعي وَتَتلوهُ بِصِحَّة؟
lines.english: Will you learn the prayer with me and recite it correctly?
lines.transliteration: hal tata'allamu ad-du'aa' ma'ii wa tatluuhu bissiha?

lines.arabic: الدُّعاءُ الطِّبيُّ يَستَلزِمُ تَحليلَ كُلِّ لَفظَة — كَلِمَة شِفاء لَيسَت مُرادِفَةً لِكَلِمَة صِحَّة
lines.english: The healing prayer requires analysing every word — shifa (cure) is not synonymous with sihha (health).
lines.transliteration: ad-du'aa' at-tibbiyy yastalzimu tahlil kulli lafza — kalima shifaa' laysat muraadifan li-kalima sihha

lines.arabic: الشِّفاءُ في كُلِّ أَرض — المُسافِرُ يَتَعَلَّمُ الدُّعاء لِيَحمِيَ نَفسَه في أَيِّ طَريق
lines.english: Healing exists in every land — the traveler learns the prayer to protect themselves on any road.
lines.transliteration: ash-shifaa' fii kulli ard — al-musaafir yata'allamu ad-du'aa' li-yahmiya nafsahu fii ayy tariiq

lines.arabic: الطِّبُّ العَرَبيُّ كانَ طِبَّ الجِسمِ وَالرُّوح — الدُّعاءُ كانَ جُزءاً مِن وِصفَةِ كُلِّ طَبيب
lines.english: Arab medicine healed both body and soul — the prayer was part of every physician's prescription.
lines.transliteration: at-tibb al-arabiyy kaana tibb al-jism war-ruuh — ad-du'aa' kaana juz'an min wasfa kulli tabiib

lines.arabic: إن شاء الله! الدُّعاءُ الآنَ مَحفوظ. نُطقُكَ سَليمٌ تَماماً
lines.english: God willing! The prayer is now preserved. Your pronunciation is completely correct.
lines.transliteration: in shaa' allaah! ad-du'aa' al-aan mahfuuz. nutquka saliim tamaaman

name: Maryam
role: The Coastal Warrior — grammar specialist, Coastal Port companion

greeting.arabic: يَلَّا! أَنا مَريَم — حارِسَةُ الساحِل. لا وَقتَ لِلتَّرَدُّد
greeting.english: Let's go! I am Maryam — guardian of the coast. No time for hesitation.
greeting.transliteration: yalla! ana maryam — haarisa as-saahil. laa waqt lit-taraddud

lines.arabic: يَلَّا! أَنتَ أَتقَنتَ المِيناء. أَحتاجُ مِنكَ إِتقانَ نَحوِ الأَوامِر
lines.english: Let's go! You've mastered the port. I need you to master command grammar.
lines.transliteration: yalla! anta atqanta al-miinaa'. ahtaaju minka itqaan nahw al-awamir

lines.arabic: الجُملَةُ القِتالِيَّة: فِعلٌ ثُمَّ فاعِلٌ ثُمَّ مَفعول — هَكَذا نَأمُر
lines.english: The battle sentence: verb then subject then object — that's how we command.
lines.transliteration: al-jumla al-qitaaliyya: fi'l thumma faa'il thumma maf'uul — hakadha na'mur

lines.arabic: هَل تُتقِنُ البِنيَةَ وَتُثبِتُ جَدارَتَكَ أَمامي؟
lines.english: Will you master the structure and prove your worth before me?
lines.transliteration: hal tutqin al-binyata wa tuthbit jadaraataka amamii?

lines.arabic: النَّحوُ القِتاليُّ مَبنيٌّ عَلى قَواعِدَ صارِمَة — العالِمُ يَستَخدِمُ الأَوزانَ الصَّرفيَّةَ كَسُيوف
lines.english: Battle grammar is built on strict rules — the scholar wields morphological patterns like swords.
lines.transliteration: an-nahw al-qitaaliyy mabniyy 'ala qawaa'id saarimа — al-'aalim yastakhdam al-awzaan as-sarfiyya ka-suyuuf

lines.arabic: المُسافِرُ الشُّجاعُ لا يَتَرَدَّد — البِنيَةُ تَحمي لِسانَكَ في كُلِّ بَلَد
lines.english: The brave traveler does not hesitate — structure protects your tongue in every land.
lines.transliteration: al-musaafir ash-shujaa' laa yataraddad — al-binyatu tahmi lisaanik fii kulli balad

lines.arabic: العَرَبُ الفُرسانُ كانوا شُعَراء أَيضاً — السَّيفُ وَالبَيانُ وَجهانِ لِقُوَّةٍ واحِدَة
lines.english: Arab knights were also poets — the sword and eloquence are two faces of one power.
lines.transliteration: al-'arab al-fursaan kaanuu shu'araa' aydan — as-sayf wal-bayaan wajhaan li-quwwa waahida

lines.arabic: يَلَّا! أَحسَنتَ. نَحوُكَ القِتالي أَصبَحَ سِلاحاً حَقيقِيَّاً
lines.english: Let's go! Well done. Your battle grammar has become a real weapon.
lines.transliteration: yalla! ahsanta. nahwuka al-qitaali asbaha silahan haqiiqiyyan

name: Samir
role: The Market Brawler — pronunciation specialist, Desert Marketplace companion

greeting.arabic: وَالله! أَنتَ جَريءٌ أَن تَقتَرِبَ. أَنا سَمير — أُعَلِّمُ بِسُرعَة
greeting.english: By God! You're bold to approach. I am Samir — I teach fast.
greeting.transliteration: wallaah! anta jarii' an taqtarib. ana samir — u'allim bisur'a

lines.arabic: وَالله! أَنتَ أَتقَنتَ السُّوق. لَكِن نُطقُكَ بَطيء جِدَّاً
lines.english: By God! You've mastered the market. But your pronunciation is too slow.
lines.transliteration: wallaah! anta atqanta as-suuq. laakin nutquka batiiy' jiddan

lines.arabic: في السُّوق الكَلِماتُ تَتَطايَرُ — مَن لا يَنطِقُها سَريعاً يَخسَر
lines.english: In the market words fly — whoever doesn't pronounce them fast loses.
lines.transliteration: fis-suuq al-kalimaat tatataayr — man laa yantiquha sarii'an yakhsar

lines.arabic: هَل تَجرُؤُ عَلى تَحَدِّيَ النُّطقي؟
lines.english: Do you dare to face my pronunciation challenge?
lines.transliteration: hal tajra'u 'ala tahaddiyi an-nutqii?

lines.arabic: النُّطقُ السَّريعُ لا يَعني النُّطقَ الأَدقَّ — العالِمُ يُوازِنُ بَينَ السُّرعَةِ وَالضَّبط
lines.english: Fast pronunciation does not mean more precise pronunciation — the scholar balances speed with accuracy.
lines.transliteration: an-nutq as-sarii' laa ya'nii an-nutq al-adaqq — al-'aalim yuwaazin bayna as-sur'a wad-dabt

lines.arabic: في كُلِّ مَدينَة لَهجَةٌ مُختَلِفَة — المُسافِرُ يَتَكَيَّفُ مَعَ إيقاعِ كُلِّ مَكان
lines.english: Every city has a different dialect — the traveler adapts to the rhythm of every place.
lines.transliteration: fii kulli madiina lahja mukhtalifa — al-musaafir yatakayaf ma'a iiqa' kulli makaan

lines.arabic: أَسواقُ بَغداد وَالقاهِرَة وَالأَندَلُس كُلٌّ لَها إيقاعُها — التّاريخُ يُسمَعُ في سُرعَةِ الكَلام
lines.english: The markets of Baghdad, Cairo, and Andalusia each had their own rhythm — history is heard in the speed of speech.
lines.transliteration: aswaaq baghdaad wal-qaahira wal-andalus kullun lahaa iiqa'uhaa — at-taariikh yusma' fii sur'at al-kalaam

lines.arabic: وَالله! فُزتَ. نُطقُكَ أَصبَحَ بِسُرعَة البَرق
lines.english: By God! You won. Your pronunciation has become as fast as lightning.
lines.transliteration: wallaah! fuzta. nutquka asbaha bisur'at al-barq

name: Nadia
role: The Mountain Herbalist — culture specialist, Mountain Village companion

greeting.arabic: الله أكبر! هَذا الجَبَلُ يَحمِلُ أَسرارَ الأَعشاب
greeting.english: God is greatest! This mountain holds the secrets of herbs.
greeting.transliteration: allaahu akbar! haadha al-jabal yahmil asraar al-a'shaab

lines.arabic: الله أكبر! أَنتَ تُتقِنُ الجَبَل. أَنا نادِيَة — أَحفَظُ تَقاليدَ الأَعشاب
lines.english: God is greatest! You've mastered the mountain. I am Nadia — I preserve herb traditions.
lines.transliteration: allaahu akbar! anta tutqin al-jabal. ana naadiya — ahfazu taqaaliid al-a'shaab

lines.arabic: كُلُّ عُشبَةٍ لَها اِسمٌ عَرَبيٌّ قَديمٌ يَجِبُ أَن يُعَلَّمَ لِلأَجيال
lines.english: Every herb has an ancient Arabic name that must be taught to the generations.
lines.transliteration: kull 'ushba laha ism 'arabi qadiim yajibu an yu'allama lil-ajyaal

lines.arabic: هَل تُساعِدُني في تَعليم أَسماء الأَعشاب لِلجيل القادِم؟
lines.english: Will you help me teach the herb names to the next generation?
lines.transliteration: hal tusa'iduni fi ta'liim asmaa' al-a'shaab lil-jiil al-qaadim?

lines.arabic: التَّصنيفُ العِلمي لِلأَعشاب كَتَبَهُ العُلَماءُ العَرَب — كُلُّ اِسمٍ يَحمِلُ خُصائِصَ النَّبات
lines.english: The scientific classification of herbs was written by Arab scholars — every name carries the plant's properties.
lines.transliteration: at-tasniif al-'ilmiyy lil-a'shaab katabahu al-'ulamaa' al-'arab — kullu ism yahmil khasaa'is an-nabaat

lines.arabic: الأَعشابُ الطِّبيَّة تَنمو في كُلِّ جَبَل — المُسافِرُ يَتَعَلَّمُ أَسماءَها لِيَنجوَ في البَريَّة
lines.english: Medicinal herbs grow on every mountain — the traveler learns their names to survive in the wilderness.
lines.transliteration: al-a'shaab at-tibbiyya tanmu fii kulli jabal — al-musaafir yata'allam asmaa'ahaa li-yanjuwa fil-barriyya

lines.arabic: الطِّبُّ النَّباتيُّ الإسلامي وَثَّقَ أَلفَ نَباتٍ قَبلَ عُلَماء أُوروبّا — هَذِهِ الأَسماءُ هِيَ التُّراث
lines.english: Islamic botanical medicine documented a thousand plants before European scholars — these names are the heritage.
lines.transliteration: at-tibb an-nabaatiyy al-islaamiyy waththaqa alf nabaat qabl 'ulamaa' uurubbaa — haadhihi al-asmaa' hiya at-turaath

lines.arabic: الله أكبر! التَّقليدُ مَحفوظ. أَسماءُ الأَعشاب سَتَعيشُ لِلأَبَد
lines.english: God is greatest! The tradition is preserved. The herb names will live forever.
lines.transliteration: allaahu akbar! at-taqliid mahfuuz. asmaa' al-a'shaab sata'iishu lil-abad

name: Tariq
role: The Ruin Defender — vocabulary specialist, Royal Palace companion

greeting.arabic: بالتأكيد. أَنا طارِق — صَامِدٌ هُنا حَتَّى تَكونَ النُّقوشُ في أَمان
greeting.english: Certainly. I am Tariq — standing here until the inscriptions are safe.
greeting.transliteration: bittakiid. ana tariq — saamid huna hatta takuuna an-nuquush fi amaan

lines.arabic: بالتأكيد. أَنتَ أَتقَنتَ العَرَبِيَّة. النُّقوشُ بِحاجَةٍ إلى عالِمٍ مِثلِك
lines.english: Certainly. You've mastered Arabic. The inscriptions need a scholar like you.
lines.transliteration: bittakiid. anta atqanta al-arabiyya. an-nuquush bihaajatin ila 'aalim mithlak

lines.arabic: كُلُّ نَقشٍ يُعَلِّمُ مُفرَداتٍ نادِرَة — لَكِنَّ النَّهَّابينَ يَقتَرِبون
lines.english: Every inscription teaches rare vocabulary — but looters are approaching.
lines.transliteration: kull naqsh yu'allim mufradaat naadira — laakin an-nahhaabiin yaqtaribuun

lines.arabic: هَل تُساعِدُني في فَكِّ رُموزِ النُّقوش وَتَسجيلِها قَبلَ فَوات الأَوان؟
lines.english: Will you help me decode and record the inscriptions before it's too late?
lines.transliteration: hal tusa'iduni fi fakk rumuuz an-nuquush wa tasjiiluha qabl fawaat al-awan?

lines.arabic: فَكُّ الرُّموز عِلمٌ دَقيق — العالِمُ يَربِطُ كُلَّ رَمزٍ بِجَذرِهِ اللُّغَوي
lines.english: Decoding symbols is a precise science — the scholar links every symbol to its linguistic root.
lines.transliteration: fakk ar-rumuuz 'ilmun daqiiq — al-'aalim yarbit kull ramzin bi-jadhrihi al-lughawiyy

lines.arabic: النُّقوشُ مَنتَشِرَةٌ عَلى طُرُق القَوافِل — المُسافِرُ يَتَعَلَّمُ مِنها الاتِّجاهات وَالتّاريخ مَعاً
lines.english: Inscriptions are scattered along caravan routes — the traveler learns both directions and history from them.
lines.transliteration: an-nuquush muntashira 'ala turuq al-qawaafil — al-musaafir yata'allam minhaa al-ittijaahaat wat-taariikh ma'an

lines.arabic: النُّقوشُ شُهودٌ صامِتَة عَلى الحَضارات — كُلُّ حَرفٍ هُوَ بَقيَّةٌ مِن عالَمٍ بَنى وَاندَثَر
lines.english: Inscriptions are silent witnesses of civilisations — every letter is a remnant of a world that built and then faded.
lines.transliteration: an-nuquush shuhuudun saamita 'ala al-hadaaraat — kullu harfin huwa baqiyya min 'aalam banaa wantathara

lines.arabic: بالتأكيد. النُّقوشُ مُسَجَّلَة. المُفرَداتُ في أَمانٍ لِلأَبَد
lines.english: Certainly. The inscriptions are recorded. The vocabulary is safe forever.
lines.transliteration: bittakiid. an-nuquush musajjala. al-mufradaat fi amaan lil-abad

greeting.arabic: أَهلاً بِكَ يا مُسافِر — الشِّعرُ طَريقُ القَلب
greeting.english: Welcome, traveller — poetry is the path of the heart
greeting.transliteration: ahlan bika ya musafir — ash-shi'ru tariiqu al-qalb

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَهلاً بِكَ يا مُسافِر — الشِّعرُ طَريقُ القَلب
lines.english: Welcome, traveller — poetry is the path of the heart

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تُريدُ أَن تَخوضَ مُسابَقَةَ الشِّعر مَعي؟
lines.english: Would you like to enter a poetry contest with me?

greeting.arabic: قَرَأتُ كُلَّ الدَّواوين — هَل تَجرُؤُ عَلى مُنافَستي؟
greeting.english: I have read every divan — do you dare to compete with me?
greeting.transliteration: qara'tu kulla al-dawaaween — hal tajru' ala munafasatii?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قَرَأتُ كُلَّ الدَّواوين — هَل تَجرُؤُ عَلى مُنافَستي؟
lines.english: I have read every divan — do you dare to compete with me?

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: المُتَنَبّي قالَ: عَلى قَدرِ أَهلِ العَزم تَأتي العَزائِم
lines.english: Al-Mutanabbi said: According to the people of resolve, so come the great deeds

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل أَنتَ مِن أَهلِ العَزم؟ أَثبِت ذَلِك!
lines.english: Are you among the people of resolve? Prove it!

greeting.arabic: أُلقي الشِّعرَ في كُلِّ زاوِيَة مِن هَذا السّوق!
greeting.english: I recite poetry in every corner of this market!
greeting.transliteration: ulqii ash-shi'ra fii kulli zaawiya min haadha as-suuq!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أُلقي الشِّعرَ في كُلِّ زاوِيَة مِن هَذا السّوق!
lines.english: I recite poetry in every corner of this market!

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: هَل تَسمَعُ؟ ابنُ زَيدون كانَ يَعِيشُ هُنا في قَلبِه — تَعال نَتَنافَس
lines.english: Do you hear? Ibn Zaydun lived here in his heart — come, let us compete

greeting.arabic: الصَّحراءُ تُعَلِّمُني الشِّعر — الرِّمالُ والنُّجوم ملهَمتي
greeting.english: The desert teaches me poetry — sand and stars are my inspiration
greeting.transliteration: as-sahraa tu'allimunii ash-shi'r — ar-rimaal wan-nujuum mulhimatii

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: الصَّحراءُ تُعَلِّمُني الشِّعر — الرِّمالُ والنُّجوم ملهَمتي
lines.english: The desert teaches me poetry — sand and stars are my inspiration

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: أَبو نُواس كانَ يَسير في هَذِه الصِّحراء — هَل تَعرِفُ شِعرَه؟
lines.english: Abu Nuwas walked this desert — do you know his poetry?

greeting.arabic: مِن هَذِه الأَطلال يُنادينا امرُؤُ القَيس عَبرَ الزَّمان
greeting.english: From these ruins, Imru al-Qais calls to us across time
greeting.transliteration: min hadhihi al-atlal yunaadinaa imru ul-qays abra az-zamaan

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن هَذِه الأَطلال يُنادينا امرُؤُ القَيس عَبرَ الزَّمان
lines.english: From these ruins, Imru al-Qais calls to us across time

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: قِفا نَبكِ — هَل تَعرِفُ مَعنى هَذِه الكَلِمات العَتيقَة؟
lines.english: Halt, let us weep — do you know the meaning of these ancient words?

greeting.arabic: في عُزلَتي هَذِه أَحفَظُ أَشعارَ العَرَب وأَتَأَمَّلُها
greeting.english: In my solitude I memorise and contemplate the poetry of the Arabs
greeting.transliteration: fii uzlatii hadhihi ahfadhu ash'aar al-arab wa ata'ammaluhaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: في عُزلَتي هَذِه أَحفَظُ أَشعارَ العَرَب وأَتَأَمَّلُها
lines.english: In my solitude I memorise and contemplate the poetry of the Arabs

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: السَّيفُ أَصدَقُ إِنباءً مِن الكُتُب — هَل تُحِبُّ أبا تَمّام؟
lines.english: The sword is more truthful than books — do you appreciate Abu Tammam?

greeting.arabic: البَحرُ يُلهِمُني مِثلَما أَلهَمَ الشُّعَراءَ القُدامى
greeting.english: The sea inspires me as it inspired the poets of old
greeting.transliteration: al-bahru yulhimunii mithlamaa alhama ash-shu'araa al-qudaamaa

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: البَحرُ يُلهِمُني مِثلَما أَلهَمَ الشُّعَراءَ القُدامى
lines.english: The sea inspires me as it inspired the poets of old

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: حَسّانُ بنُ ثابِت مَدَحَ بِأَجمَلِ القَصائِد — هَل تَحفَظُ شَيئاً؟
lines.english: Hassan ibn Thabit praised with the most beautiful odes — do you know any?

greeting.arabic: مِن أَعلى الجَبَل أَرى الدُّنيا كَما رَآها لَبيد بنُ رَبيعَة
greeting.english: From the mountain top I see the world as Labid ibn Rabi'ah saw it
greeting.transliteration: min a'laa al-jabal araa ad-dunyaa kamaa ra'aahaa labiid ibn rabii'a

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: مِن أَعلى الجَبَل أَرى الدُّنيا كَما رَآها لَبيد بنُ رَبيعَة
lines.english: From the mountain top I see the world as Labid ibn Rabi'ah saw it

lines.speaker: npc
lines.arabic: عَفَتِ الدِّيارُ — هَل تَعرِفُ مُعَلَّقَة لَبيد؟ سَنَختَبِرُ ذَلِك الآن
lines.english: The abodes have faded — do you know Labid's Ode? We shall test that now
